en: INTRODUCTION
zh: 引言

en: On October 7, 1930, Japanese patrolman Yoshimura Katsumi passed through the hamlet of Mehebu (near Wushe) during a wedding celebration. There, a Sediq man, one Tadao Mona, beckoned him for a drink. Yoshimura brusquely refused, thereby slighting Tadao publicly. Tadao’s hands were bloody from butchering meat for the festival repast. Nonetheless, he touched Yoshimura’s freshly laundered uniform and left a red stain. Yoshimura angrily struck Tadao twice on the hand with a cane. Along with his younger brother Bassao Mona, Tadao wrestled Yoshimura to the ground and returned the blows. The next day, their father, headman Mona Ludao, went to the nearby Japanese police box with bottles of millet wine in hand to formally apologize. Much to Mona’s chagrin, the branch chief, Sugiura Kōichi, refused the gift and apologies. Instead, Mona and his sons were reported to Sugiura’s superiors. Mona was told to expect severe punishment; the possibilities ranged from detention to a punitive expedition against his entire village. Yoshimura’s report and Sugiura’s handling of the matter drove Mona into the arms of other rebellious Sediq men. Mona Ludao himself led the bloody Wushe Rebellion three weeks later. In the October 27, 1930, assaults, Tadao Mona’s squad killed Yoshimura Katsumi in the first wave.
zh: 1930 年 10 月 7 日，日本巡查吉村克己（Yoshimura Katsumi）在一场婚礼庆典期间经过马赫坡（Mehebu，近雾社）这个小村。在那里，一名赛德克男子达道·莫那（Tadao Mona）招呼他喝酒。吉村粗率地拒绝，从而当众轻慢了达道。达道双手因给婚宴切肉而沾了血。尽管如此，他还是碰了吉村刚洗净的制服，留下一块红渍。吉村恼怒地用手杖打了达道的手两下。达道与弟弟巴沙奥·莫那（Bassao Mona）把吉村摔倒在地，回敬了拳脚。第二天，他们的父亲、头人莫那·鲁道（Mona Ludao）手提几瓶小米酒，到附近的日本警察派出所正式道歉。令莫那极为懊恼的是，分所长杉浦孝一（Sugiura Kōichi）拒绝了礼物与道歉。相反，杉浦把涉及莫那和他儿子的这件事报告给了上级。莫那被告知等着受严惩；可能的处置从拘留到针对他整个村落的惩罚性远征不等。吉村的报告与杉浦对此事的处理，把莫那促使莫那同其他准备反抗的赛德克男子联手。三周后，莫那·鲁道亲自领导了血腥的雾社起义。在 1930 年 10 月 27 日的袭击中，达道·莫那的小队在第一波就杀死了吉村克己。

en: These events of early October, known as the “
beating incident” (Yoshimura ōda jiken) have been recounted (and sometimes embellished) in numerous government inquests, Japanese memoirs, document collections, and overviews of the Wushe uprising.
A popular 2001 comic book reconstructed the dispute for a general audience of post–martial law Taiwanese, while the blockbuster 2011 movie
dramatized it in a multilingual feature film.

There are conflicting facts in these accounts. We are left to wonder: What type of meat bloodied Tadao’s hands? How many Japanese patrolmen visited the wedding? How many bottles of wine did Mona offer to Sugiura? Did Mona jump in and help assault Yoshimura, or did he break up the fight? But regarding the main sequence of events, all accounts agree: a wedding took place on October 7; a fight between Yoshimura and Tadao erupted; and Mona Ludao’s attempt at informal mediation was rejected in favor of an administratively determined punishment.
zh: 这些十月初的事件，被称为“吉村殴打事件”（Yoshimura ōda jiken），在无数政府调查、日本人回忆录、文件汇编与雾社起义概述中被反复讲述（有时还被添油加醋）。
2001 年一本流行漫画为解严后台湾的一般读者重构了这场纠纷，而 2011 年的大片《赛德克·巴莱》（Seediq Bale）则在一部多语言故事片中把它戏剧化。
这些记述中存在相互冲突的事实。我们不禁要问：是什么肉的血沾满了达道的双手？有几名日本巡查到过婚礼现场？莫那向杉浦奉上了几瓶酒？莫那是跳进去帮忙殴打吉村，还是劝开了打斗？但关于事件的主序列，所有记述都一致：10 月 7 日举行了一场婚礼；吉村与达道之间爆发了打斗；莫那·鲁道非正式调解的尝试遭到拒绝，取而代之的是由行政决定的惩罚。

en: From Mona’s perspective, Sugiura’s recourse to superiors constituted a rejection of Mona’s chiefly authority to resolve disputes on the basis of his status as a revered Sediq headman. At the same time, the administrative hand-off subordinated Sugiura; it was an admission that he was not Mona’s equivalent, a “local Japanese chief” with wide discretionary powers. This indeed was a momentous change, and it signaled the termination of rule by the outcasts of empire on both sides of the “savage border.” The Yoshimura beating incident exemplified the regime’s efforts to dispense with an intermediary layer of quasi officials at its geographic extremities.
zh: 从莫那的视角看，杉浦诉诸上司，构成了对莫那酋长权威的拒绝——那种基于他作为受人尊崇的赛德克头人身份、来解决纠纷的权威。与此同时，这一行政上的移交也使杉浦处于从属地位；它等于承认他并非莫那的对等者，不是一个拥有广泛裁量权的“地方日本头人”。这的确是一个重大变化，它标志着“生番界”两侧由帝国弃民进行统治的终结。吉村殴打事件例示了该政权在其地理末端撤去这层充当中介的准官员的努力。

en: In the new order, the authority of Japanese officials and indigenous leaders would be derived solely through competition and recruitment through the public-school system and the police bureaucracy. At least theoretically, this new hierarchy, on both sides of the ethnic divide, reached all the way up to the emperor in Tokyo, thereby unifying the island administratively—almost.
zh: 在新秩序中，日本官员与原住民领袖的权威，将仅仅通过公立学校体系和警察官僚机构的竞争选拔而来。至少在理论上，这一新等级制在族群分界的两侧都一直上达东京的天皇，从而在行政上统一了全岛——几乎如此。

en: WET DIPLOMACY AND EARLY JAPANESE COLONIAL RULE
zh: 湿外交与日本早期殖民统治

en: Six decades prior to Yoshimura’s pointed refusal to drink with Tadao Mona, outsiders with business on the edges of Qing territory in Taiwan accepted alcoholic beverages from indigenes and stuck around to imbibe them at close quarters. We can think of such transactions as instances of “wet diplomacy.” Throughout the island, alcohol was consumed as a liquid, but in northern Taiwan, the preferred method was called “conjoined drinking” (gōin), which entailed contact with an interlocutor’s saliva (see

). The term “wet diplomacy” is therefore descriptive of a particular type of activity, but it also denotes an ideal-typical form of human interaction. The phrase is not used in this study to distill a particularly “Japanese” form of sociability but rather is adopted to account for the frequent and repetitive descriptions of diplomatic drinking in the source material, and for the insistence of historical actors themselves that the relationships thus consecrated were personal and not abstract or contractual. This ideal type contrasts with

(dry) interaction, which is fungible. Wet bonds must be renewed with periodic expressions of fealty, while dry relationships are rule governed and attach to social roles or official ranks rather than individuals.
zh: 在吉村断然拒绝与达道·莫那共饮的六十年前，那些在台湾清朝领土边缘有事的外来者，会接受原住民递来的酒，也会留下来与他们近距离共饮。我们可以把这类交易视为“湿外交”的实例。在全岛，各地都以饮用的方式摄取酒液，但在台湾北部，偏好的方式称为“共饮”（gōin，合口饮酒），它涉及与对话者唾液的接触（见

）。因此，“湿外交”一词既描述一种特定类型的活动，也指称一种理想典型式的人际互动形式。本研究使用这个短语，不是为了提炼一种特别“日本式”的社交形式，而是为了说明史料中对外交饮酒频繁而重复的描述，以及历史行动者本人坚持认为由此确认的关系是具体个人之间的、而非抽象或契约性的。这一理想类型与“干”（durai）的互动相对照，后者不因换人而改变。湿的纽带必须以定期的效忠表达来更新，而干的关系受规则支配，附着于社会角色或官阶，而非个体。

en: In the late 1890s and early 1900s, the early years of formal Japanese rule in Taiwan, wet diplomacy was the coin of the realm along Taiwan’s savage border. It evinced continuity with the precedent-setting practices of the Taiwan Expedition in the 1870s. In both instances, Japanese officials, merchants, and scholars entered into personal relations with indigenes to secure forbearance, goods, labor, or guidance. In the course of these transactions, indigenous merchants, chiefs, and interpreters established bonds of trust with particular outsiders. These relationships frequently involved intermarriage (see chapter 2). In the wet diplomatic context, favoritism and loyalty were expected—in fact, they were the whole point.
zh: 在 1890 年代晚期与 1900 年代早期，即日本正式统治台湾的最初几年，湿外交是台湾生番界沿线的通行手段。它显示出与 1870 年代台湾远征那些开创先例的做法的连续性。在这两种情形中，日本官员、商人与学者都同原住民建立个人关系，换取对方克制、提供货物或劳力，或为他们引路。在这些交易过程中，原住民商人、酋长与通事同特定外来者建立了信任纽带。这些关系常常涉及通婚（见第 2 章）。在湿外交语境中，偏袒与忠诚是被期待的——事实上，这正是全部意义所在。

en: Indigenous leaders sought access to Japanese goods and political patronage to gain advantage over local rivals or to shore up authority within their segmented polities. Therefore, from their perspective, the notion that all Taiwanese would be treated equally as children of the emperor was anathema. This Japanese policy was formally known as “nondiscrimination” (isshi dōjin). Under it, all loyalty and obligation were directed toward a single apex, the emperor—thus making isshi dōjin structurally analogous to modern nationalism, which also channels loyalty upward as it postulates horizontal fraternities of juridically equal and interchangeable subject-citizens. Indigenous Taiwan’s small-scale, nonstate polities were inimical to the instantiation of isshi dōjin, however, because they were held together by the politics of redistribution. Here, chiefly authority was augmented by public displays of favoritism vis-à-vis other indigenes and successful warfare against neighboring enemies.
zh: 原住民领袖寻求获取日本货物与政治庇护，以压倒地方对手、或在其分节政体内巩固权威。因此，从他们的视角看，所有台湾人都将作为天皇之子被平等对待的观念，是可憎的。这项日本政策正式称为“一视同仁”（isshi dōjin，不歧视）。在其之下，一切忠诚与义务都指向一个单一顶点——天皇——从而使一视同仁在结构上类似于现代民族主义：后者也把忠诚向上引导，同时设定法律上平等、可互换的臣民—公民之间的横向兄弟关系。然而，原住民台湾那些小型、非国家的政体不利于一视同仁的确立，因为它们是靠再分配政治凝聚起来的。在这里，酋长权威通过当众对其他原住民显示偏袒、以及对邻近敌人成功的战争而得到增强。

en: Japanese isshi dōjin proclamations promised impartiality for all Taiwanese but were nonetheless premised on Japanese preeminence. That is to say, even the most fair-minded Japanese officials believed that indigenes were savages squatting on the emperor’s land. However, as long as chiefs were receiving gifts, publicly engaging in joined-mouth drinking with Japanese colonists, or themselves apportioning banquet victuals, the vagaries of language allowed indigenous leaders to convert wet-diplomatic encounters into political capital vis-à-vis followers and rivals. But in the long run, the logics of centralized administration and bureaucratic rationality were incompatible with the protocols of wet diplomacy.
zh: 日本的一视同仁宣言承诺对所有台湾人一视同仁，却仍以日本的优越为前提。也就是说，即便最公正的日本官员也相信，原住民是擅自占据天皇土地的野蛮人。然而，只要酋长们还在接受礼物、当众与日本殖民者合口饮酒、或亲自分配宴席食物，语言的种种微妙便允许原住民领袖把湿外交接触转化为相对于追随者与对手的政治资本。但从长远看，中央行政与官僚理性的逻辑，同湿外交的规程不相容。

en: To overcome the paradoxes of wet diplomacy and establish a less particularistic and labor-intensive form of rule, the TGG stationed guard posts along a scorched-earth trail known as the aiyūsen (see

) to enclose the Atayal, Sediq, and Truku settlements of northern Taiwan. This denuded landscape provided clear lines of fire, while it physically divided northern Taiwan into two distinct zones: one for imperial subjects and another for outcast rebels. From 1903 through 1915, government forces extended the scorched-earth barrier and then marched it inward.

The Indigenous Peoples of Taiwan, as a modern political-cultural formation, emerged from the ruins of these scorched-earth campaigns. The surrender ceremonies themselves, and the nakedly asymmetrical power relations they enforced, epitomized “dry” interpersonal relations—the lists of demands Japanese policemen read from their elevated platforms were couched not in the language of reciprocity and benevolence but as orders for compliance upon pain of punishment (see

). The trade-starved, bombed-out, and battered indigenous delegations were summoned to these spaces as supplicants. To resume trading relations and stop the shelling, they were forced to surrender their weapons and listen to lists of conditions enforced by carrot-and-stick methods, rather than renewed displays of friendship, as called for in wet diplomacy (see
zh: 为克服湿外交的悖论、建立一套较少依赖私人关系、更节省人力的统治方式，总督府沿着一条称为隘勇线（aiyūsen）的焦土小径设置哨所（见
），以圈围台湾北部的泰雅、赛德克与德路固聚落。地表植被被清除后，射界开阔，同时在物理上把台湾北部划分为两个截然不同的区域：一个给帝国臣民，另一个给被弃的反叛者。从 1903 到 1915 年，政府军延伸这道焦土屏障，然后把它向内推进。
台湾原住民作为一个现代政治—文化形态，从这些焦土战役的废墟中浮现。投降仪式本身、以及仪式强制确立的明显不对等权力关系，集中体现了“干”的人际关系——日本警察从其高台上宣读的要求清单，不是用互惠与仁惠的语言措辞，而是作为以惩罚为威胁、要求服从的命令（见
）。那些贸易断绝、遭轰炸、被打垮的原住民代表团，作为恳求者被召到这些空间。为恢复贸易关系、停止炮击，他们被迫缴械，并聆听以软硬兼施手段强制执行的条件清单，而非湿外交所要求的那种重新展示友好（见

en: Yet after the highlands were largely disarmed, wet diplomacy did not dry up. The guardline campaigns had, in fact, exhausted the Taiwan Government-General. In the late 1910s through early 1930s, state-society relations were left in the hands of rural district police officers, their indigenous wives, and local chiefs such as Mona Ludao. These districts remained outside the tax base and were labeled “special,” “savage,” or “aborigine.” I will refer to this phase of Japanese rule as the era of “native authority,” following Mahmood Mamdani.
zh: 然而，在高山地区基本被解除武装之后，湿外交并未干涸。隘勇线战役事实上已使台湾总督府筋疲力尽。从 1910 年代晚期到 1930 年代早期，国家—社会关系被留在乡村地区警察官员、他们的原住民妻子、以及莫那·鲁道这类地方酋长手中。这些地区仍在税基之外，被标记为“特别”“生番”或“蕃人”。沿用马哈茂德·马姆达尼（Mahmood Mamdani），我将把日本统治的这一阶段称为“土著权威”时代。

en: Wet diplomacy solved several problems for the Japanese, as it did for the Qing in earlier times: with a meager budget, the government-general established itself in the highlands despite linguistic and cartographic ignorance. From the strategic choke points thus established, information could be collected and relationships forged. However, wet diplomacy hindered the efficient and reliable extraction of resources from the upland forests, and it blurred the boundaries of state sovereignty along the so-called “savage border.” This chapter plots the history of indigenous-Japanese relations around the forced march from wet diplomacy to scorched earth, and then from scorched earth to native authority. It further posits an isomorphism between wet diplomacy and the low-velocity milieu of tributary interstate relations. By the same token, it will argue for a congruence between dry human relations and the horizontal integration of space that is presupposed by the regime of rule from a distance. This latter mode of governance, in turn, sought to facilitate the generation, accumulation, and funneling of surplus wealth to state coffers.
zh: 湿外交为日本人解决了若干问题，正如它早先为清朝所解决的：凭借微薄的预算，总督府尽管缺乏当地语言和地理知识，仍在高山地区立足。从由此控制的战略要冲，可以收集信息、锻造关系。然而，湿外交妨碍了从山地森林高效而可靠地抽取资源，并模糊了所谓“生番界”沿线国家主权的边界。本章围绕从湿外交到焦土、再从焦土到土著权威的强行军，勾勒原住民—日本关系的历史。它进一步设定湿外交与朝贡式国家间关系的低速环境之间的同构性。同理，它将论证干的人际关系与远程统治体制所预设的空间横向整合之间的契合。后一种治理模式反过来力图使剩余财富更容易产生、积累，再汇入国库。

en: TREATY-PORT TAIWAN AND THE MUDAN VILLAGE INCIDENT
zh: 条约口岸台湾与牡丹社事件

en: As with the 1930 Yoshimura beating incident, the 1871 shipwreck of the Ryūkyūans in Taiwan could have been resolved locally, on the spot. In each case, recourse to central authorities occurred in the context of increased volumes and velocities of resource extraction in these imperial peripheries. Such pressures catapulted otherwise unexceptional events to historical turning points. The 1930 Wushe uprising was set off by the Japanese government’s heightened demand for timber in central Taiwan. Yoshimura himself was brought to Wushe to supervise a Sediq labor force in felling and hauling gigantic cedars, at fixed wages, to complete a series of public works projects. Yoshimura was not locally embedded, as some of his superiors were, but was a specialist hired to accelerate the process of forest exploitation. When his tone-deaf rejection of Tadao’s entreaty caused a ruckus, his supervisor Sugiura construed the wedding brawl as an assault on imperial authority and sent his report up the chain of command, escalating matters beyond the point of no return. Six decades earlier, a longer chain of events, with a larger cast of characters and an even higher body count, presaged a similar set of problems at the outer margins of state-administered territory in Taiwan.
zh: 与 1930 年吉村殴打事件一样，1871 年琉球人在台湾的沉船事件本可以在当地、当场解决。在两个案例中，诉诸中央当局都发生在这些帝国边缘资源抽取的体量与速度增加的语境中。此类压力把原本平平无奇的事件弹射为历史转折点。1930 年雾社起义由日本政府对台湾中部木材需求的激增所引发。吉村本人被带到雾社，督率按固定工资雇用的赛德克工人砍伐、拖运巨杉，以完成一系列公共工程。吉村不像他的有些上司那样在当地有深厚的人际联系，而是被雇来加速森林开发进程的专家。他不顾场合地拒绝了达道的邀约，引发冲突，他的上司杉浦把这场婚礼斗殴解读为对帝国权威的袭击，并把报告沿指挥链上报，使事态升级到无可挽回的地步。六十年前，一连串拖得更久的事件、更多的人物、更高的死亡人数，预示了台湾国家直接管理领土外缘一套类似的问题。

en: The increase in Asia-bound commerce that followed the Opium Wars (1839–42) turned the Taiwan Strait into a major thoroughfare in the China trade. After two treaty ports were opened there in 1860, Taiwan’s “poorly charted and still-unlighted coasts” and rocky shallow waters became a graveyard for boats and their crews. One tally estimates that about “150 foreign vessels... foundered in the vicinity of the Taiwan coast between 1850 and 1869 of which over thirty were plundered or burned.”
Another calculates that at “least forty-six Western merchant ships” disappeared or were destroyed from 1861 through 1874.

Most infamously, in December 1871 near Bayao Bay, Taiwanese murdered 54 shipwrecked sailors from Miyakojima (Ryūkyū Islands / Okinawa), an act that occasioned the invasion of over 3,000 Japanese troops beginning in May 1874 (see
zh: 鸦片战争（1839–42）之后驶往亚洲的商船越来越多，使台湾海峡成为中国贸易的一条主要通道。1860 年那里开放两个条约口岸后，台湾“测绘粗劣、仍未设灯标的海岸”与多礁浅水，成了船只及其船员的坟墓。一项统计估计，约“150 艘外国船只……在 1850 至 1869 年间于台湾海岸附近沉没，其中三十多艘遭劫掠或焚毁”。
另一项统计推算，从 1861 到 1874 年，“至少四十六艘西方商船”失踪或被毁。
最臭名昭著的是，1871 年 12 月在八瑶湾附近，台湾人杀害了来自宫古岛（琉球群岛/冲绳）的五十四名沉船船员，这一行为引发了从 1874 年 5 月开始、三千多名日军的入侵（见

en: MAP 3. Taiwan, the Ryūkyū Islands, the Langqiao Peninsula, Mudan, and Satsuma, in East Asia.
zh: 地图 3. 东亚的台湾、琉球群岛、琅峤半岛、牡丹社与萨摩。
parallelFigureCaption: MAP 3. Taiwan, the Ryūkyū Islands, the Langqiao Peninsula, Mudan, and Satsuma, in East Asia.
地图 3. 东亚的台湾、琉球群岛、琅峤半岛、牡丹社与萨摩。

en: Most historical accounts of the 1871 shipwreck are based on the recollections of a Japanese official and two Miyakojima survivors. Oral testimonies of the protagonists, their rescuers, and local officials were jotted down in 1872 and subsequently combed over by generations of scholars in Taiwan, Japan, the Ryūkyū Islands, and beyond. Chou Wan-yao summarized this scholarship in a recent review article,
while Miyaguni Fumio has republished the primary-source materials.
Ōhama Ikuko has mined archives in Taiwan and Japan (including Okinawa) and reconstructed the events with great care.
In addition, local historian and native of Kuskus village Valjeluk Mavaliu has collated written evidence with his geographical and genealogical knowledge,
while Mudan resident and oral historian Gao Jiaxin (Lianes Punanang) has interviewed a dozen or so Paiwan elders (including Valjeluk Mavaliu),
to provide a local perspective.
zh: 关于 1871 年沉船事件的大多数历史记述，都基于一名日本官员与两名宫古岛幸存者的回忆。当事人、搭救者与地方官员的口头证词在 1872 年被匆匆记下，随后被台湾、日本、琉球群岛及其他地方一代代学者反复梳理。周婉窈（Chou Wan-yao）在一篇近期综述文章中综述了这些研究，
宫里文雄（Miyaguni Fumio）则重新刊布了原始史料。
大滨郁子（Ōhama Ikuko）挖掘了台湾与日本（含冲绳）的档案，极为细致地重构了事件。
此外，地方史家、高士佛（Kuskus）村人瓦耶鲁克·马瓦利乌（Valjeluk Mavaliu）把书面证据与其地理及谱系知识相互校勘，
而牡丹社居民、口述史家高加馨（Gao Jiaxin，Lianes Punanang）访谈了十来位排湾长老（含瓦耶鲁克·马瓦利乌），
以提供一个地方视角。

en: The drama was set in motion by the November 30, 1871, departure of four tribute ships from the castle complex of Shuri (near Naha), on the island of Okinawa. The ships were returning to Miyakojima and the Yaeyama Islands in the Ryūkyū Kingdom. Within sight of Miyakojima, the ships were blown off course and succumbed to a typhoon on December 12, 1871. One of the ships from the Yaeyama Islands was lost forever, but another landed on Taiwan’s western coast. The survivors of the latter wreck made it back to Naha through the good offices of Qing officials. Of the two Miyakojima ships, one made it safely back to its port of origin, but the other—the famous one—capsized off the east coast of southern Taiwan, near Bayao Bay.
zh: 这场戏剧由 1871 年 11 月 30 日四艘朝贡船从冲绳岛首里（近那霸）城堡建筑群启程而启动。这些船正返回琉球王国的宫古岛与八重山群岛。在望见宫古岛之处，船只被吹离航线，于 1871 年 12 月 12 日屈服于台风。来自八重山群岛的船之一永远失踪，但另一艘在台湾西海岸靠岸。后一艘沉船的幸存者经清朝官员的斡旋回到那霸。两艘宫古岛船中，一艘安全返回其始发港，但另一艘——那艘著名的——在台湾南部东海岸、八瑶湾附近倾覆。

en: There were sixty-nine passengers on the ill-fated Miyakojima ship. Three of them perished trying to get ashore. The other sixty-six made landfall five days after the horrible storm. Soon after, they encountered two Chinese men who reportedly warned them away from traveling inland among dangerous Paiwan peoples. It is difficult to know what transpired at this juncture. The survivors’ deposition indicates that the sixty-six Ryūkyūans were robbed by the Chinese and decided to part ways with their hosts. They spent the night in makeshift outdoor lodgings and set out the morning of December 18. As they wandered westward, they encountered men with large earrings and distended earlobes, presumably Paiwanese.
zh: 那艘命途多舛的宫古岛船上有六十九名乘客。其中三人在试图上岸时丧生。其余六十六人在可怕风暴五天之后登陆。不久，他们遇到两名华人男子，据称警告他们别深入排湾人聚居的内陆，说那里危险。很难知道这一刻究竟发生了什么。幸存者的证词表明，六十六名琉球人被华人抢劫，遂决定与主人分道扬镳。他们在临时搭建的户外住所过夜，于 12 月 18 日早晨出发。当他们向西流浪时，遇到戴着大耳环、耳垂拉长的人，想必是排湾人。

en: The Ryūkyūans followed the Paiwanese to a settlement of fifteen or sixteen thatched homes, Kuskus, where the lost mariners were given water and food and were put up for the evening. The provision of water by Kuskus residents, for them at least, symbolized an offer of protection and friendship, according to Valjeluk Mavaliu.

The deposition claims that during the night, they were robbed again by their Kuskus hosts. In the morning, a departing group of hunters ordered the Ryūkyūans to stay put and offered to return with enough game to provide a feast. However, the presence of so many armed men, coupled with the rumors of head hunting that had greeted them on shore two days earlier, impelled them to make a break for it while the hunting party was absent.
zh: 琉球人跟随排湾人来到一个有十五六间茅屋的聚落高士佛，迷路的水手在那里得到水和食物，并被留宿一晚。据瓦耶鲁克·马瓦利乌所言，高士佛居民提供水，至少对他们而言，象征着提供保护与友谊。
证词声称，夜间他们再次被高士佛主人抢劫。早晨，一队即将出发的猎人命令琉球人留在原地，并提议带回足够的猎物以设宴。然而，如此多武装男子的在场，加上两天前他们上岸时便听到的猎首传闻，促使他们趁狩猎队不在时夺路而逃。

en: Dozens of the fleeing Ryūkyūans found shelter in the home of seventy-three-year-old Hakka trading-post operator Deng Tianbao (named “Old Weng” in the deposition
) and his thirty-year-old son in a nearby settlement of five or six houses. Most Taiwanese Hakka (

) people immigrated from Guangdong Province. Throughout Taiwan, the Hakka established settlements in foothills and acted as commercial conduits between Austronesians in the mountains and Han people of Fujianese extraction (Hok-los) in the plains.
Valjeluk Mavaliu writes that Deng was married to a Paiwanese woman named Utjau,
a common practice for cross-border merchants in this area.
zh: 数十名逃跑的琉球人在附近一个五六户人家的聚落里，到七十三岁的客家贸易站经营者邓天保（证词称“老翁”
）和他三十岁儿子的家中避难。台湾大多数客家（Kejia）人从广东省移民而来。在整个台湾，客家人在山麓建立聚落，充当山地南岛语族与平原福建裔汉人（福佬，Hok-los）之间牵线经商。
瓦耶鲁克·马瓦利乌写道，邓娶了一位名叫乌兆（Utjau）的排湾女子，
这是该地区跨界商人的常见做法。

en: That same day, Paiwan men caught up with the Ryūkyūans. They forcibly entered Deng’s compound. Dozens of Ryūkyūans were dragged out and slaughtered in a courtyard; others were caught in flight. Nine Ryūkyūans avoided detection in Deng’s home, and another three escaped (and were captured by other Paiwanese subsequently). The other fifty-four were killed in the melee. The next day, the nine survivors were removed to the much larger Hakka settlement of Poliac (Baoli) and put under the care of the village head, Yang Youwang—Deng’s son-in-law. Poliac was an ammunition depot, trade junction, and place of arms manufacture. Hakka merchants transshipped powder, shot, and guns to Paiwan buyers inland from this location (see
zh: 同一天，排湾男子追上了琉球人。他们强行进入邓的院落。数十名琉球人被拖出、在一个院子里屠杀；其他人在逃跑中被抓。九名琉球人在邓家中躲过搜查，另有三人逃脱（随后被其他排湾人捕获）。其余五十四人在混战中被杀。第二天，九名幸存者被转移到大得多的客家聚落保力（Poliac/Baoli），交由村长杨友旺——邓的女婿——照料。保力是储存弹药、贸易转运和制造武器的据点。客家商人从这里把火药、弹丸与枪支转运给内陆的排湾买家（见

en: MAP 4. The Langqiao Peninsula, ca. 1874.
zh: 地图 4. 琅峤半岛，约 1874 年。
parallelFigureCaption: MAP 4. The Langqiao Peninsula, ca. 1874.
地图 4. 琅峤半岛，约 1874 年。

en: In addition to securing the safety of these nine, Yang also arranged for the ransom of the three separated men. Yang Youwang then sheltered these twelve survivors for about forty days, before sending them to the administrative seat of Taiwan Prefecture (Taiwan-fu, today’s Tainan). The Ryūkyūans were returned to Naha in July 1872, over seven months after the four ships were hit by the typhoon.
zh: 除了确保这九人的安全，杨还安排赎回了那三名失散者。杨友旺随后庇护这十二名幸存者约四十天，然后把他们送往台湾府的府治（Taiwan-fu，今台南）。琉球人于 1872 年 7 月回到那霸，距四艘船遭台风袭击已七个多月。

en: Although it became a truism among Japanese officials and subsequent chroniclers that Paiwanese Mudan villagers murdered the seafarers, residents of Kuskus, today known as Gaoshifo, were the assailants.

It has been proposed that the violence resulted from the Ryūkyūan visitors’ ignorance of guest etiquette (they ate and ran), or that the captors could not find buyers to pay ransom and thus killed them.

Gao Jiaxin’s oral histories provide another plausible explanation. Sixty-six adults, unable to communicate in the local languages, walked into Kuskus farmland and began taking food and trampling over hotly contested village boundaries. On top of these nuisances, efforts to feed and shelter dozens of strangers, who brought no provisions and could not make themselves understood, strained Kuskus resources and hospitality. Finally, the intruders were killed as punishment for their multiple misdeeds.
The best estimates put the population of Gaoshifo at 250 at the time.
Therefore, one can imagine that caring for sixty-six guests would have been a major, to say nothing of disruptive, undertaking in this sparsely populated area of rural Taiwan.
zh: 尽管排湾族牡丹社村民杀害航海者成了日本官员与后来编年史家中间的老生常谈，真正的行凶者却是高士佛社（Kuskus，今高士佛）的居民。
有人提出，暴力源于琉球访客不懂待客礼仪（他们吃了就跑），或绑架者找不到买主付赎金、因而杀了他们。
高加馨的口述史提供了另一种可信的解释。六十六名成人无法用当地语言沟通，走进高士佛农田，开始拿取食物、践踏激烈争夺的村界。除了这些扰害，要喂养并庇护数十名既未带口粮、又无法让人听懂自己的陌生人，使高士佛的资源与好客之道不堪重负。最终，入侵者因其多重劣行而被杀以示惩罚。
最佳估计认为当时高士佛人口为 250。
因此可以想见，在台湾这个人口稀疏的乡村地区，照料六十六名客人会是一项重大的、更不用说扰乱性的事业。

en: Whatever the motivations of the people who killed the Ryūkyūans, the slaughter did not immediately raise eyebrows in Japan. While a few officials who happened to be in Beijing or Naha in mid-1872 got wind of the massacre, it did not become a full-blown international incident until April 1874. The 1872 repatriation of the twelve survivors from Poliac to Fenggang to Taiwan-fu to Fuzhou appears to have been by the book. In fact, the Qing system for repatriating Ryūkyūan shipwreck victims on the shores of China (including Taiwan) settled 401 incidents over the course of the seventeenth to the nineteenth centuries. Qing policy throughout its realm was to provide food, clothing, and ship repairs for stranded mariners. Reciprocal agreements with neighboring powers returned Chinese shipwreck survivors to the Qing realm from Japan, Korea, Vietnam, and the Ryūkyūs in over 700 incidents during the same period.
zh: 无论杀害琉球者动机为何，这场屠杀并未立即在日本引起侧目。虽然 1872 年年中恰好在北京或那霸的少数官员风闻了屠杀，但它直到 1874 年 4 月才成为一场全面的国际事件。1872 年把十二名幸存者从保力经枫港、台湾府到福州的遣返，似乎完全照章办事。事实上，清朝遣返中国海岸（含台湾）琉球沉船受害者的制度，在十七至十九世纪间处理了 401 起事件。清朝在其全境的政策是为搁浅水手提供食物、衣物与修船。与邻国的互惠协议在同一时期从日本、朝鲜、越南与琉球把中国沉船幸存者送回清境，超过 700 起。

en: Edwin Pak-wah Leung has argued that this regional repatriation system worked without visible complaint until the arrival of the Western-centered treaty-port regime in the late nineteenth century. He notes that the Ryūkyūan court itself did not request Japanese officials to intercede on its behalf regarding the fifty-four victims of the 1871 shipwreck. It was Japanese officials visiting Okinawa who lobbied for the invasion. The Ryūkyū monarch Shō Tai (Shang-tai), instead of requesting Japanese aid, sent a reward to Chinese officials in Fuzhou after the return of the twelve survivors from Taiwan. In fact, Ryūkyūans had been stranded on Taiwanese shores on fifty-three recorded occasions between 1701 and 1876 and were repatriated by the Qing in each instance.

Because such incidents were unexceptional and because Japan’s expedition to avenge the deaths of the fifty-four Ryūkyūans occurred over two years after the event, the question of the timing of the 1874 invasion has been of great interest to historians. Quite rightly, scholars have looked to Japan’s national politics and diplomatic history for answers, decoupling the May 1874 invasion from the December 1871 shipwreck.
zh: 梁伯华（Edwin Pak-wah Leung）论证，这一区域遣返体系一直运转而无明显怨言，直到十九世纪晚期以西方为中心的条约口岸体制到来。他指出，琉球朝廷本身并未请求日本官员就 1871 年沉船的五十四名受害者出面交涉。是访问冲绳的日本官员游说发动入侵。琉球君主尚泰（Shō Tai）非但没有请求日本援助，反而在十二名幸存者从台湾返回后，向福州的中国官员送去赏赐。事实上，1701 至 1876 年间有记载的琉球人搁浅台湾海岸共五十三次，每次都由清朝遣返。
由于此类事件平平无奇，也由于日本为五十四名琉球人之死复仇的远征发生在事件两年多之后，1874 年入侵的时机问题一直令史家极感兴趣。学者们相当正确地把目光投向日本国内政治与外交史寻求答案，把 1874 年 5 月的入侵与 1871 年 12 月的沉船脱钩。

en: At the time of the Meiji Restoration (1868), state-to-state relations within East Asia had yet to become international and are more properly termed interdynastic, or the “tributary system.” To assure that diplomacy demonstrated the sovereign’s centrality and paramountcy, tributary courts received official delegations from other states at specified times and for periods of limited duration. The missions followed carefully prescribed routes, performed minutely orchestrated guest rituals, and returned home. Much has been made of the cultural chauvinism and hierarchical ordering that informed diplomatic practice under this system. In this analysis, however, the important hallmarks of tributary forms are not their validation of a generalized, transhistorical sense of Chinese superiority but rather more portable features that can be extended to other premodern regimes. Namely, tributary relations were tailored to the specificity of each diplomatic transaction. Guest rituals in this system were adjusted for differences between supplicant states or even for the size of missions. Tributary relations also eschewed the notion that interstate relations be put on a permanent, contractual, and routinized basis. In their emphases on the necessity for periodic renewal and forthrightly particularistic forms,
Qing, Tokugawa, and Joseon guest rituals bore a family resemblance to the “wet diplomacy” described above.
zh: 明治维新（1868）之时，东亚内部的国与国关系尚未成为国际性的，更恰当地应称为王朝间的，即“朝贡体系”。为确保外交展示主权者的中心性与至高性，接受朝贡的朝廷在特定时间、以有限时长接待他国的官方使团。使团遵循精心规定的路线，表演细致编排的宾客礼仪，然后回国。人们大谈这一体系下外交实践所体现的文化沙文主义与等级排序。然而在本分析中，朝贡形式的重要标志，不是它对一种普遍化、跨历史的中国优越感的确认，而是那些可移植到其他前现代政权的、更便于迁移的特征。即，朝贡关系针对每次外交往来的具体情况而量身定制。这一体系中的宾客礼仪，会因朝贡国之间的差异、甚至使团规模而调整。朝贡关系也摒弃那种把国家间关系置于永久、契约、常规化基础上的观念。在其对定期更新之必要性、以及公开按交往对象采取有别的礼仪的强调上，
清、德川与朝鲜的宾客礼仪与上文描述的“湿外交”有相通之处。

en: According to Takeshi Hamashita, “modernity” did not overpower encrusted East Asian “tradition” with the coming of the Western treaty ports at the conclusion of the Opium Wars. Rather, the Atlantic powers overlaid a new set of institutions, practices, and personnel onto existing Chinese, Japanese, and Korean maritime trade circuits. Independent of the new trade, intra-Asian commerce experienced its own growth spurt in the nineteenth century. East Asian politicians and merchants themselves could be eager proponents of trade-volume expansion, tariff standardization, harbor improvements, and efficient customs agencies. In a word, Hamashita demonstrated that the routinization of cross-border commercial practices within Asia, rather than threatening dynasties, could, in fact, strengthen central authority.

The ideological divide in dynastic circles was not so much between moderns and traditionalists but about means to increase, regulate, or reject higher volumes of foreign trade in order to protect sovereignty.
zh: 据滨下武志（Takeshi Hamashita）所言，“现代性”并未随鸦片战争结束时西方条约口岸的到来而压倒积淀深厚的东亚“传统”。毋宁说，大西洋列强把一套新的制度、实践与人员叠加到既有的中国、日本、朝鲜海上贸易回路之上。独立于新贸易，亚洲内部商业在十九世纪经历了自身的增长突进。东亚政客与商人本身可能积极主张扩大贸易、统一关税标准、改善港口并建立高效海关。一言以蔽之，滨下展示，亚洲内部跨界商业实践的常规化非但不威胁王朝，事实上反而能强化中央权威。
王朝圈子里的意识形态分歧，与其说在现代派与传统派之间，不如说在于以何种手段增加、管制或拒绝更高体量的对外贸易，以保护主权。

en: These debates about how to meet the challenges and opportunities presented by the arrival of industrial capitalism in East Asia raged in Japan during the interval between the December 1871 killing of the Ryūkyūans in Deng Tianbao’s courtyard and the May 1874 Japanese invasion of Taiwan. Simultaneously, the Japanese government struggled to assert authority throughout its three major islands of Honshū, Kyūshū, and Shikoku. Rural rebellions against increased taxes, compulsory education, and military conscription, as well as the “chastise Korea debate” (

) at the higher levels of government, formed the backdrop for the 1874 invasion. Saigō Tsugumichi’s occupation of southern Taiwan, therefore, not only aimed to clear the Langqiao Peninsula of parasites who leeched wealth from the global system but also advanced the Meiji project to stamp out regionalism and resistance to central authority within Japan.

As Norihito Mizuno put it, the varied projects subsumed under the Taiwan Expedition—to colonize the Langqiao Peninsula, to siphon off samurai discontent with a foreign adventure, and to assert exclusive sovereignty over the Ryūkyūs—all conformed to a single logic: the young Meiji state’s heightened threat perception vis-à-vis its industrialized competitors in the arena of nation-state imperialism.
zh: 这些关于如何应对工业资本主义到来东亚所提出挑战与机遇的辩论，在 1871 年 12 月琉球人在邓天保院中被杀、与 1874 年 5 月日本侵台之间的间隔里，于日本激烈进行。与此同时，日本政府奋力在其三大岛本州、九州、四国全境确立权威。反对增税、义务教育与征兵的乡村叛乱，以及政府高层的“征韩论争”（seikanron），构成了 1874 年入侵的背景。因此，西乡从道对台湾南部的占领，不仅旨在清除琅峤半岛上那些被当作从全球体系吸取财富的“寄生虫”的人，还推进了明治在日本国内铲除地方主义与对中央权威抵抗的工程。
正如水野直人（Norihito Mizuno）所言，统摄于台湾远征之下的种种工程——殖民琅峤半岛、以一场对外冒险分流武士的不满、以及对琉球宣示排他主权——全都符合一个单一逻辑：年轻的明治国家在民族国家帝国主义角力场中，对其工业化竞争对手加剧的威胁感知。

en: It will be recalled that the lack of succor for shipwrecked American whalers at the hands of Japanese local officials energized the U.S. government to pursue a “water and wood” treaty with the Tokugawa Shogunate (1603–1867) in 1853. The 1854 Treaty of Peace and Amity, signed between the United States and Japan on the heels of two U.S. naval missions led by Commodore Matthew Perry, was aimed at a Japanese government actively hostile to shipwreck victims, and by extension, to untrammeled access to the ocean’s natural resources.

America’s whalers were extending their range deeper into the Pacific, making the problem of shipwrecks on Japan’s shores a persistent one if Americans were to keep increasing oil consumption. Under threat of naval bombardment, the Tokugawa Shogunate signed the 1854 treaty with the United States and a subsequent 1858 treaty to open trade and treaty ports.
zh: 应当记得，日本地方官员对沉船美国捕鲸者缺乏救助，促使美国政府在 1853 年向德川幕府（1603–1867）追求一项“供水供柴”条约。1854 年《和平友好条约》在美国海军准将马修·佩里（Matthew Perry）率领的两支美国海军使团之后由美日签署，针对的是一个对沉船受害者积极敌视、并也因此阻碍外国人自由取得海洋资源的日本政府。
美国捕鲸者把活动范围推向太平洋更深处，使日本海岸的沉船问题成为一个持续存在的问题——如果美国人要继续增加鲸油消费的话。在海军炮击的威胁下，德川幕府签署了 1854 年对美条约，以及随后 1858 年开放贸易与条约口岸的条约。

en: The government in Edo managed to dodge the bullet of foreign invasion, but its actions met with dire consequences. After the shogunate signed these unpopular instruments, civil wars erupted throughout the realm, in addition to a wave of political assassinations. When rebellious Satsuma (a southwestern domain in Kyūshū) shore batteries fired on British ships in 1863, also to protest Japan’s new policies of openness, British naval bombardment nearly decimated the castle town of Kagoshima.
Outgrowths of this civil strife, brought on by a central government’s overreach to satisfy the demands of mercantile powers, fomented the collapse of the Tokugawa Shogunate in 1868.
zh: 江户政府设法避开了外国入侵，但其行动招致可怕后果。幕府签署这些不得人心的文书后，全境爆发内战，外加一波政治暗杀。当反叛的萨摩（九州西南部的一个藩）的岸炮在 1863 年向英国船只开火——同样为抗议日本新的开放政策——英国海军炮击几乎摧毁了鹿儿岛城下町。
这场由中央政府为满足商业列强要求而过度伸展所引发的内乱的种种衍生后果，促成了 1868 年德川幕府的崩溃。

en: As the Tokugawa regime was teetering on its last legs, U.S. consul to Amoy (Xiamen) Charles LeGendre reprised, on a smaller scale, the 1853–54 U.S. missions to Tokyo in Langqiao, Taiwan. In the fall of 1867, LeGendre concluded a verbal agreement with the Langqiao headman Toketok to protect shipwrecked sailors from assault, robbery, and ransoming on Taiwan’s south coast.

The agreement, like the 1854 Japan-U.S. treaty, reflected the efforts of maritime powers to make the seas safer for greater volumes and velocities of commerce. The LeGendre-Toketok negotiations, like the U.S.-Japan talks of the late 1850s, averted armed confrontation in the short run, while they placed unbearable strains upon Toketok’s ability to hold together a loose confederation of subordinate polities. Toketok’s problems, in fact, mirrored those of the Tokugawa government vis-à-vis Western gunboats.
zh: 正当德川政权摇摇欲坠、苟延残喘之际，美国驻厦门（Amoy）领事查尔斯·李仙得（Charles LeGendre）在台湾琅峤以更小的规模重演了 1853–54 年美国赴东京的使团。1867 年秋，李仙得与琅峤头人卓杞笃（Toketok）达成一项口头协议，保护沉船船员在台湾南海岸免受袭击、抢劫与勒索赎金。
该协议与 1854 年日美条约一样，反映了海洋列强为保障海上贸易在更大规模、更快速度下安全进行所做的努力。李仙得—卓杞笃谈判与 1850 年代晚期美日会谈一样，短期内避免了武装对抗，却给卓杞笃维系一个松散从属政体联盟的能力施加了难以承受的压力。事实上，卓杞笃面对的处境与德川幕府面对西方炮舰时相似。

en: LEGENDRE EXTENDS THE TREATY-PORT SYSTEM TO LANGQIAO
zh: 李仙得把条约口岸体系扩展到琅峤

en: In April 1867, LeGendre made his first journey to Taiwan to investigate an American shipwreck that became known as the
incident. The consul’s visit ignited a seven-year fuse that exploded with the landing of four Japanese warships in Langqiao in May 1874. The barque
bottomed out on Taiwan’s south cape in March 1867. After it capsized, the

’ s captain, his wife, and his crew were murdered on shore by Koaluts (a Paiwan tribe) while trying to secure help. The one survivor of the attack, a Chinese man, reported the incident to authorities in Gaoxiong after making his escape. Thereafter, a British steamer left the same port to investigate but was turned back by the eruption of musket fire from the camouflaged and elevated positions of the Koaluts. LeGendre headed to the south cape for a ten-day tour.
He failed to find survivors or remains since he could not secure local guides.
zh: 1867 年 4 月，李仙得首次赴台，调查一起后来称为罗妹号（Rover）事件的美国沉船事件。这位领事的访问点燃了一根七年引信，最终在 1874 年 5 月日军乘四艘军舰在琅峤登陆时爆炸。三桅帆船“罗妹号”于 1867 年 3 月在台湾南端搁浅。倾覆后，罗妹号船长、其妻及船员在岸上试图求援时，被龟好儿（Koalut，一个排湾部落）杀害。袭击中唯一的幸存者是一名华人男子，逃脱后向高雄当局报告了事件。此后，一艘英国汽船离开同一港口前往调查，却被龟好儿人从伪装的高处阵地爆发的火枪射击逼退。李仙得前往南端进行了十天巡视。
由于无法找到当地向导，他未能找到幸存者或遗骸。

en: While LeGendre plotted his next move in Xiamen, U.S. vice admiral H. H. Bell launched a frontal attack from the location of the

’ s wreck. Ignoring the advice of LeGendre, Bell skipped a stop at the port town of Siaoliao. LeGendre had suggested that Bell activate the “mediating networks” of Hakka, Hok-lo, bicultural, and Paiwan villagers that connected the port of Siaoliao to the protected and isolationist Koalut polity.

Going it alone instead, Bell successfully landed, but soon after, one Lieutenant Captain Mackenzie was shot through the heart by a Koalut marksman during an uphill infantry charge against unseen defenders. The American warship pulled anchor and shelled the Koaluts from a safe distance, apparently inflicting great damage. But without access to kin, trade, and alliance networks, Bell could not locate survivors or discover who specifically had killed the crew of the
zh: 当李仙得在厦门谋划下一步时，美国海军中将 H. H. 贝尔（H. H. Bell）从罗妹号沉船地点发动正面进攻。贝尔无视李仙得的建议，没有在射寮（Siaoliao）港停靠。李仙得曾建议贝尔激活把射寮港同受保护、闭关自守的龟好儿政体连接起来的由客家、福佬、跨文化群体及排湾村民组成的“中介网络”。
贝尔反而独自行事，成功登陆，但不久后，一名麦肯齐上尉（Mackenzie）在率步兵向坡上的隐蔽守军冲锋时，被一名龟好儿射手射穿心脏。美国军舰起锚，从安全距离炮击龟好儿人，显然造成重大破坏。但由于无法接入亲属、贸易与联盟网络，贝尔找不到幸存者，也查不出究竟是谁杀了罗妹号船员。

en: As a treaty-port consul in Xiamen, which subsumed Taiwan on the American diplomatic organizational chart, LeGendre took the Langqiao Peninsula’s opacity as a professional and personal affront. A letter to LeGendre from the Taiwan circuit attendant regarding the

referred to Articles 11 and 13 of the 1858 Treaty of Tianjin to state “that whenever within the jurisdiction of the Emperor of China, anyone shall molest Americans, the military and civil authorities must, on hearing of the same, try to punish the authors.” However, the note added—and this became the sticking point for years to come—“the Savage country does not come within the limits of our jurisdiction, and our military force is not able to operate in it.”

Finding this response unsatisfactory, LeGendre took the matter all the way to the top (short of an imperial audience). In person, he proposed to the governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang, Wu Tang, that the Langqiao Peninsula be occupied by Chinese inhabitants and garrisoned permanently by Qing forces.
zh: 作为厦门的条约口岸领事——在美国外交组织图表上厦门统辖台湾——李仙得把琅峤半岛的不透明视为一种对其领事职责与个人尊严的冒犯。台湾道就罗妹号致李仙得的一封信，援引 1858 年《天津条约》第 11、13 条，声称“凡在中国皇帝管辖之内，任何人骚扰美国人，军政当局一经闻知，必须设法惩办肇事者。”然而，照会又补充道——这成了此后多年的症结——“生番地界不在我管辖范围之内，我军兵力亦无法在其中行动。”
李仙得觉得这一答复不能令人满意，便把此事一直报到最高层（仅次于觐见皇帝）。他当面向闽浙总督吴棠提议，琅峤半岛应由华人居民占据、并由清军永久驻防。

en: Langqiao’s meager population—about fifteen thousand people, of whom three thousand were indigenous, seven thousand or so bicultural, and another four or five thousand Hakka and Hok-lo
—and its variety of unknown (to Chinese officials) languages and inaccessible terrain

did not commend the extension of civil and military administration to this remote corner of empire. Understandably, Wu did not formally consent to LeGendre’s proposals, but neither could he ignore them. It is testament to the force of British and French arms and the demonstration effects of the 1860 sacking of Beijing
that LeGendre could obtain a meeting with Wu, who sat at the apex of an administrative unit that governed perhaps thirty million Qing subjects.
It was surely in this larger context that the American’s numerous requests, if not honored, were generally entertained.
zh: 琅峤稀少的人口——约一万五千人，其中三千原住民、七千左右双文化人、另有四五千客家与福佬
——及其种种（对中国官员而言）未知的语言与难以进入的地形，
并不使人想把民政与军政扩展到这个帝国偏远角落。可以理解，吴棠没有正式同意李仙得的提议，但也无法置之不理。英法的武力以及1860年洗劫北京所产生的威慑
，使李仙得得以会见吴棠。吴棠所辖区域约有三千万清朝臣民。
正是在这一更大语境中，这位美国人的众多请求即便未被应允，也大体得到了受理。

en: Wu Tang’s successor, Ying Gui, therefore allowed LeGendre to accompany a military tour of Langqiao led by General Liu Mingdeng in September 1867.

LeGendre recounted travel to Langqiao from the prefectural capital, Taiwan-fu, as an arduous affair. Although ranking Qing officials extended LeGendre diplomatic courtesies, transportation was halting. LeGendre rode on a sedan chair in proximity to General Liu, but his journey was delayed by bad weather and slow communications. As one moved south, the last Chinese city on the coast, Fangliao, was literally the end of the road. To go beyond, Liu’s troops (who numbered about five hundred), built a forty-mile path—supposedly at LeGendre’s urging—before the expedition could proceed (see
zh: 因此，吴棠的继任者英桂允许李仙得随同 1867 年 9 月由刘明灯将军率领的一次琅峤军事巡视。
李仙得把从府治台湾府前往琅峤的旅程描述为一桩苦差。尽管高级清朝官员给予李仙得外交礼遇，交通却时断时续。李仙得乘轿紧邻刘将军，但行程因恶劣天气与迟缓的通讯而延误。随着南行，海岸上最后一座华人城市枋寮，就是当时道路的实际尽头。要再往前，刘的部队（约五百人）修筑了一条四十英里的小径——据说是应李仙得的催促——远征才得以继续（见

en: MAP 5. Principal administrative centers, contact zones, and political boundaries mentioned in this book. The Taiwan Government-General’s 1909 –20 prefectures are in all capitals. The lighter area of the map is TGG-demarcated Aborigine Territory (ca. 1905–45).
zh: 地图 5. 本书提及的主要行政中心、接触地带与政治边界。台湾总督府 1909–20 年的各厅以全大写标示。地图较浅区域为总督府划定的蕃地（约 1905–45）。
parallelFigureCaption: MAP 5. Principal administrative centers, contact zones, and political boundaries mentioned in this book. The Taiwan Government-General’s 1909 –20 prefectures are in all capitals. The lighter area of the map is TGG-demarcated Aborigine Territory (ca. 1905–45).
地图 5. 本书提及的主要行政中心、接触地带与政治边界。台湾总督府 1909–20 年的各厅以全大写标示。地图较浅区域为总督府划定的蕃地（约 1905–45）。

en: LeGendre’s contemporary accounts of his progress through Taiwan, which he appears to have kept scrupulously accurate within the limits of his knowledge, do not suggest that Taiwan was divided into two separate zones, Chinese and indigenous (see

). He would adopt this divisive view later, after his trips to the island ceased and his knowledge was, in a sense, weaponized for use in the diplomatic arena. As Bruce Greenfield wrote of the Lewis and Clark journals, expedition accounts subsume numerous genres of writing, each with its own source of authority. For LeGendre the amateur scientist and aspiring author, recording surfeits of local detail established his credibility and retained reader interest.

At the same time, LeGendre wrote in a combative, legalistic style to prosecute his official duties. In this register, later complicated by his advocacy of a Japanese invasion, his descriptions of Taiwan lost much of their veracity and took on a hortatory aspect.
zh: 李仙得对其台湾行程的同时代记述——他似乎在其知识限度内一丝不苟地保持准确——并不表明台湾被划分为华人区与原住民区两个分离区域（见
）。他后来才采纳这种分裂观点，那是在他停止赴岛、其知识在某种意义上被武器化用于外交角力场之后。正如布鲁斯·格林菲尔德（Bruce Greenfield）论刘易斯与克拉克日记时所写，远征记述统摄多种写作体裁，每种各有其权威来源。对作为业余科学家与有志作家的李仙得而言，记录大量地方细节确立了他的可信度、并留住读者兴趣。
与此同时，李仙得以一种好斗、拘泥法律的文风写作，以履行其公务。在这一语域中——后来因他主张日本入侵而更复杂——他对台湾的描述丧失了许多真实性，带上了政策鼓动的色彩。

en: During this 1867 procession and follow-up tours in 1869 and 1872, LeGendre entered a region of marked ethnic diversity and hybridity; its indigenes—predominantly Paiwan—presented outsiders with a confusing array of settlements, confederations, and diplomatic forms.

The principle Paiwan people that LeGendre dealt with are known as the Eighteen-Tribe Confederation. The eighteen tribes were considered to have been under Toketok’s leadership in Western sources, though the bases of that leadership and what it entailed were murky to contemporaries and remain an object of research and speculation.
zh: 在 1867 年这次巡行及 1869、1872 年的后续巡视中，李仙得进入一个族群多样性与混合性显著的区域；其原住民——以排湾为主——向外来者呈现出一套令人困惑的聚落、联盟与外交形式。
李仙得打交道的主要排湾人称为十八社联盟。西方史料认为十八社处于卓杞笃领导之下，尽管那种领导的基础及其内涵对当时人而言晦暗不明，至今仍是研究与推测的对象。

en: These eighteen tribes (including the Kuskus who killed the Miyakojimans and the Koalut who killed Mackenzie) were of Paiwan ethnicity. The primary political and residential unit was a village, with populations ranging from seventy-five to four hundred people; these villages were mostly located in the mountains beyond the western coastal plain. Paiwan villages were militarily predominant in Langqiao before 1875. They collected taxes and tribute from Han settlers. Among the Paiwan lived a smaller population of Amis people, migrated from Taidong, and people of plains indigene descent known as Makatao. Four lineages—of Puyuma or Beinan ancestry—produced the locally paramount “big stride chiefs” (ōmata tōmoku) such as Toketok and Isa. The four noble clans of lower Hengchun viewed themselves, and were treated by Paiwans, as distinctly “foreign.” Later Japanese ethnologists referred to the lineages as Skaro peoples, or Paiwanized Puyuma. The four Skaro clans were revered as descendants of militarily powerful invaders; the southern clans that Toketok and Isa headed were also feared as efficacious and dangerous magicians.
zh: 这十八社（包括杀害宫古岛人的高士佛、与杀害麦肯齐的龟好儿）属排湾族群。基本的政治与居住单位是村，人口从七十五到四百不等；这些村大多位于西部海岸平原之外的山地。1875 年前，排湾村在琅峤军事上占优势。他们向汉人定居者征税与贡。排湾人之中还住着较少人口：从台东迁来的阿美人，以及称为马卡道（Makatao）的平原原住民后裔。四个宗族——具卑南（Puyuma/Beinan）血统——产生了地方上至高的“大股头目”（ōmata tōmoku），如卓杞笃与伊萨（Isa）。下恒春的四个贵族氏族自视、也被排湾人视为明显“外来”。后来日本民族学家把这些宗族称为斯卡罗（Skaro）人，即排湾化的卑南。四个斯卡罗氏族被尊为军事强大入侵者的后裔；卓杞笃与伊萨所领的南方氏族，还因被认为擅长法术而令人畏惧。

en: Villages, such as Kuskus, Sabaree, and Tuilasok, were located less than forty meters above sea level and sat astride well-traveled river corridors. Others, such as the feared Koaluts and Mudans, were more geographically isolated. Hakka peoples in Langqiao inhabited trade junctions between the plains and the mountains and frequently intermarried with Paiwan peoples. Today Hakka people are normally grouped with Han Chinese, but outsiders such as LeGendre and his interpreter, William Pickering, considered them a distinct people. Most remarked upon was the village of Baoli (Poliac), proximate to the two largest coastal Han settlements, Checheng and Siaoliao. This Hakka village also guarded the entrance to the valley that led to Kuskus (see
zh: 高士佛、射麻里（Sabaree）、猪朥束（Tuilasok）等村位于海拔不足四十米处，横跨往来频繁的河流走廊。另一些，如令人畏惧的龟好儿与牡丹社，则地理上更孤立。琅峤的客家人居住在平原与山地之间的贸易枢纽，常与排湾人通婚。今天客家人通常被归入汉族，但李仙得及其通事毕麒麟（William Pickering）等外来者视其为一个独特民族。最受瞩目的是保力（Baoli/Poliac）村，邻近两个最大的沿海汉人聚落车城与射寮。这个客家村还守卫着通往高士佛的山谷入口（见

en: Less well-defined groups, variously called “plains savages” or “half-castes,” are less easily described by ethnic labels. I will refer to them as bicultural, although many of them were tricultural. The man known to history as Miya belongs to this category. He was familiar with Paiwanic and southern Chinese languages and was related through kinship, commercial, and professional networks to a Paiwan confederation chief, a Qing general, and the headman of Siaoliao town. One of Langqiao’s few ports, Siaoliao was a Han-dominated coastal village that LeGendre referred to as “half-caste.” Miya would become LeGendre’s factotum in Langqiao and then go on to help the Japanese establish military operations there in May 1874.
zh: 界定较模糊的群体，被分别称为“平埔番”或“混血”，较难用族群标签描述。我将称他们为双文化人，尽管其中许多是三文化人。史上称为米亚（Miya）的那个人就属这一类。他熟悉排湾语与华南语言，并通过亲属、商业与职业网络，同一名排湾联盟酋长、一名清朝将军、以及射寮镇头人相连。射寮是琅峤少数港口之一，一个汉人主导的沿海村庄，李仙得称之为“混血”。米亚将成为李仙得在琅峤的总管，随后在1874年5月协助日军在那里展开行动。

en: Han peoples known as Hok-los, mainly from Fujian, were the majority population of nonindigenous people in Taiwan. They also resided in Langqiao, and they were known to be in competition with Hakka settlements, if not engaged in actual armed conflict. As LeGendre and Pickering, his interpreter, were quick to point out, however, common cause, such as the arrival of Qing soldiers or defense against Paiwans, could bring these two groups together as temporary allies.
zh: 称为福佬（Hok-los）的汉人主要来自福建，是台湾非原住民人口中的多数。他们也住在琅峤，素与客家聚落竞争，有时甚至发生武装冲突。然而，正如李仙得及其通事毕麒麟很快指出的，共同的利害关系，例如应对清军到来或防御排湾人——能使这两个群体成为临时盟友。

en: The Paiwan peoples of the extreme south, who most concerned General Liu Mingdeng’s Qing scouts in September 1867, maintained their military preponderance with supplies of shot, powder, and metal, purchased from Hakka traders in exchange for mountain products (furs, meat, medicinal ingredients, loot from shipwrecks). Further north near Fenggang, where Japanese troops would camp in mid-1874, Han settlements paid taxes or tribute to Paiwan villages.

So-called “aborigine rents” were relatively light; they did not fund infrastructure but were paid out as protection money. Villagers also paid taxes to Paiwans farther south, with the important exceptions of larger settlements such as Checheng and Siaoliao.
zh: 最南端的排湾人——1867 年 9 月刘明灯将军的清军侦察最关注者——以从客家商人购得的弹丸、火药与金属维持其军事优势，以山产（毛皮、肉、药材、沉船劫掠物）交换。再往北近枫港——1874 年年中日军将扎营之处——汉人聚落向排湾村纳税或贡。
所谓“番租”相对轻；它们不资助基础设施，而是作为保护费付出。村民也向更南的排湾人纳税，重要的例外是车城与射寮等较大聚落。

en: To summarize, for people who hoped to conduct business in Langqiao circa 1870, it was imperative to know how particular settlements were connected together and to secure the aid of people who could mediate the appropriate constellations of polities suited to a particular type of errand. Administrative ranks such as LeGendre’s were of little help unless they were attached to armies on the move, generous caches of gifts, or personal connections to embedded locals.
zh: 总而言之，对约 1870 年希望在琅峤做生意的人而言，至关重要的是知道特定聚落如何彼此相连，并取得那些能居间协调适合特定差事之政体组合的人的协助。像李仙得这样的行政官阶几乎无济于事，除非它们附着于行军中的军队、慷慨的礼物储备、或与嵌入地方者的私人关系。

en: Returning to LeGendre’s mission: A little over two weeks after the U.S. consul’s September 6, 1867, arrival, he and General Liu entered the town of Langqiao behind a color guard of fifty flag bearers. The townspeople prepared shrines and memorial tablets for the arriving mandarin and foreign dignitary. The locals prostrated themselves accordingly. Eight sedan bearers carried LeGendre. The consul was not bothered by the fact that he could neither read the ceremonial calligraphy produced for his benefit nor understand conversations between Liu and the reception committee. Separating himself from the seemingly unwholesome conditions of the Chinese town, LeGendre camped outside Langqiao with an interpreter and a few attendants. From there, he ran a shadow operation in parallel to the more expansive Qing effort, sending emissaries to find Toketok, the man whom General Liu had planned to negotiate with, as well.
zh: 回到李仙得的使命：在这位美国领事 1867 年 9 月 6 日抵达两周多后，他与刘将军在一支五十名旗手的仪仗队之后进入琅峤镇。镇民为到来的清朝官员与外国显贵准备了神龛与牌位。当地人依礼跪拜。八名轿夫抬着李仙得。这位领事并不介意自己既读不懂为迎接他而写的礼仪文字、也听不懂刘与接待委员会之间的谈话。为使自己脱离华人城镇看似不洁的环境，李仙得与一名通事及几名随从在琅峤城外扎营。从那里，他开展了一项与清军大规模行动同时进行的私下交涉，派遣使者去找卓杞笃——刘将军也计划与之谈判的那个人。

en: LeGendre believed that Liu’s large armed retinue would impede negotiations, so he ended up meeting Toketok on neutral ground with five interpreters and a guide. The October 10, 1867, tête-à-tête lasted about forty-five minutes and ended abruptly. Toketok brought about two hundred men under arms; he had mustered some six hundred for a previous meeting in Poliac, even though his home village of Tuilasok had a population of less than one hundred.
zh: 李仙得相信刘的大批武装随从会妨碍谈判，于是他最终在中立地带与卓杞笃会面，带了五名通事与一名向导。1867 年 10 月 10 日的私下会谈持续约四十五分钟，突然结束。卓杞笃带来约两百名武装男子；他此前在保力的一次会面曾集结约六百人，尽管其家乡猪朥束村人口不足一百。

en: From LeGendre’s perspective, Toketok was willing to negotiate because LeGendre himself and the war hero Lieutenant Captain Mackenzie (shot by a Koalut man) were brave men whom Toketok could respect. Time and again, LeGendre emphasized the personal nature of his relationship with Toketok and praised the frankness and simplicity of the Paiwan leader. He also claimed that Toketok would not deal with Han people or Qing emissaries because of their lack of courage.
During the 1874 expedition itself, Toketok’s successor as paramount chief of the eighteen tribes reportedly expressed a reluctance to deal with anyone but LeGendre,
so important was the personal connection forged during the 1867, 1869, and 1872 visits to Langqiao.
zh: 从李仙得的视角看，卓杞笃愿意谈判，是因为李仙得本人、以及战争英雄麦肯齐上尉（被一名龟好儿人射杀）都是卓杞笃能够尊重的勇敢之人。李仙得一再强调他与卓杞笃关系的人格性质，赞美这位排湾领袖的坦率与质朴。他还声称，卓杞笃因汉人与清朝使者缺乏勇气而不愿与之打交道。
在 1874 年远征期间，卓杞笃作为十八社最高酋长的继任者据称表示不愿与除李仙得以外的任何人打交道，
可见 1867、1869、1872 年访问琅峤期间锻造的私人关系何等重要。

en: It is impossible to weigh the extent to which personal ties such as the ones articulated by LeGendre mattered to the Langqiaoans. LeGendre’s linguistic transactions occurred through interpreters, usually more than one. Moreover, he could not read or understand Chinese dialects. Thus the speech he imputed to Toketok, or that which LeGendre’s successor, Commander Douglas Cassel, heard from Toketok’s successor, Isa (see below), must be taken as approximations. While Toketok may have resented Qing officials and found common cause with the frustrated treaty-port official LeGendre, and while it was undoubtedly a bold stroke to meet Toketok with such a small escort, LeGendre’s diplomatic offensive had at its back a massive Qing army and at its front a seasoned commercial interpreter who laid much of the groundwork for the meeting. Moreover, as shall be explored later in this book, Toketok was able to ritually incorporate LeGendre into a sphere of exchange and tribute by orchestrating the receptions of gifts and dispositions of banquets in accord with local forms (see chapter 3).
zh: 无法衡量李仙得所表述的那种私人纽带对琅峤人究竟有多重要。李仙得与人交谈通过通事进行，通常不止一名。此外，他读不懂也听不懂汉语方言。因此，他归于卓杞笃的言辞、或李仙得的继任者道格拉斯·卡塞尔海军中校（Commander Douglas Cassel）从卓杞笃继任者伊萨那里听到的言辞（见下文），都必须视为近似。虽然卓杞笃可能怨恨清朝官员、并与受挫的条约口岸官员李仙得有共同事业，虽然以如此小的护卫队去见卓杞笃无疑是一记大胆之举，但李仙得的外交攻势背后有一支庞大的清军，前面有一位为会面奠定大量基础的老练商业通事。此外，正如本书后面将探讨的，卓杞笃能够依照地方形式编排礼物的接受与宴席的布置，从而在仪式上把李仙得纳入一个交换与朝贡的领域（见第 3 章）。

en: William Pickering recalled several visits to Toketok as an emissary from Langqiao residents and asserted that LeGendre’s meeting was but an afterthought and a ceremonial ratification of negotiations largely completed by Pickering himself. More importantly, while LeGendre was discussing the finer points of shore safety with Toketok on October 10, over five hundred Qing troops, spies, and interpreters were fanning out across the peninsula threatening to exterminate the Paiwan and advertising the fact that many more Qing soldiers lay in reserve on the mainland.
LeGendre’s introduction to the region, it should be recalled, was his grand entrance to Langqiao with General Liu at the back of a color guard and in the front of an army.
zh: 毕麒麟回忆作为琅峤居民使者几次拜访卓杞笃，并断言李仙得的会面只是后来添上的一环，以仪式确认由毕麒麟本人基本谈妥的事项。更重要的是，当李仙得 10 月 10 日与卓杞笃讨论海岸安全的细节时，五百多名清军、间谍与通事正散布整个半岛，威胁要灭绝排湾人，并宣扬大陆还有更多清军后备的事实。
应当记得，李仙得对这个地区的引入，是他与刘将军在仪仗队之后、军队之前盛大进入琅峤。

en: Despite this general atmosphere of intimidation, the actual terms of the “treaty” (which was never acknowledged by LeGendre’s superiors in Beijing, despite his repeated efforts) suggest that Toketok was not overawed by the Qing troops. Some of the stipulations resemble the 1854 U.S. treaty with Japan: shipwrecked mariners were to be provided with basic provisions and shelter and would be brought ashore at only specified locations. However, there were major differences. For example, the 1854 treaty with Japan stipulates that U.S. sailors could not be confined at close quarters like the Dutch in their compound in Nagasaki but must be allowed to move about freely. It also leaves open the possibility of putting U.S. consuls at one or both “wood and water” stations (Shimoda and Hakodate). In contrast, Toketok’s agreement restricted foreigners to coming ashore in a very specific location and did not allow them to “visit the hills and villages” of Paiwans. When Toketok revisited the 1867 discussions, he also asked for the right to kill visitors without red flags (unless they were victims of nautical accidents).
zh: 尽管有这种普遍的恐吓气氛，“条约”的实际条款（尽管李仙得反复努力，其北京上司从未承认）表明卓杞笃并未被清军震慑。某些条款类似 1854 年美日条约：沉船水手应获基本口粮与庇护，并只在指定地点被送上岸。然而有重大差异。例如，1854 年对日条约规定美国水手不能像长崎商馆里的荷兰人那样被禁闭于狭小空间，而必须允许自由走动。它还保留了在一个或两个“供水供柴”站（下田与函馆）设置美国领事的可能。相比之下，卓杞笃的协议限制外国人只能在一个非常具体的地点上岸，不允许他们“访问排湾人的山地与村落”。当卓杞笃重提 1867 年讨论时，他还要求有权杀死没有红旗的访客（除非他们是海难受害者）。

en: It appears that some sailors were actually saved thanks to the agreement with Toketok. However, LeGendre’s personalized brand of treaty making was insufficient to effect his stated aims. Upon returning to Langqiao in 1869 and 1872, LeGendre had to reactivate local networks anchored by Miya—who was not a salaried Qing official—just to locate Toketok. Then he was informed that the treaty would have more force if it could be renewed annually with personal meetings between the U.S. consul and the Paiwan headman. In addition, as the celebrated massacre of the Ryūkyūans revealed, Langqiaoans understood the agreement as valid only for sailors who could be linked to LeGendre himself (non-Asian mariners). And just as problematic, from a treaty-power viewpoint, was the fact that Toketok’s promises did not carry much weight beyond Tuilasok, one of the smallest settlements of the eighteen tribes.
zh: 似乎确有一些水手因与卓杞笃的协议而获救。然而，李仙得这种依赖个人关系的缔约方式不足以实现他宣称的目标。1869 与 1872 年重返琅峤时，李仙得不得不重新激活以米亚为锚的地方网络——米亚并非领薪的清朝官员——只为找到卓杞笃。然后他被告知，如果条约能每年以美国领事与排湾头人之间的私人会面来更新，就会更有约束力。此外，正如那场著名的琉球人屠杀所揭示的，琅峤人把协议理解为仅对能与李仙得本人挂钩的水手（非亚洲航海者）有效。而从条约列强的视角看同样成问题的是，卓杞笃的承诺在猪朥束之外没有多少分量——那是十八社中最小的聚落之一。

en: After LeGendre left Taiwan in late 1867, Governor-General Ying Gui wrote a memorandum to the Qing central administration in Beijing with recommendations to keep foreigners out of Langqiao completely. Instead of backing LeGendre’s proposal to integrate Langqiao more tightly into the treaty-port economy, he tried to prevent the area from becoming a flash point for diplomatic disputes with Westerners. Ying Gui also proposed stationing troops and officers and appointing a few local headmen (Hok-lo, Hakka, and bicultural) to rescue shipwreck victims after the fact. These representatives and troops would be stationed in coastal Fenggang and Fangliao, not in Paiwan territory as LeGendre had envisioned. The Qing plan was premised on an indirect form of supervision.
In short, these proposed Qing measures were consonant with the older, low-velocity tributary mechanisms described above for ameliorating, rather than preventing, incidents like the
zh: 李仙得 1867 年底离开台湾后，总督英桂向北京的清廷递交了一份奏报，建议把外国人完全挡在琅峤之外。他没有支持李仙得把琅峤更紧密纳入条约口岸经济的提议，反而试图防止该地区成为与西方人外交争端的爆发点。英桂还提议驻扎军队与军官、任命少数地方头人（福佬、客家、双文化），在事后搭救沉船受害者。这些代表与军队将驻扎在沿海的枫港与枋寮，而非李仙得设想的排湾领土。清朝计划以一种间接监督形式为前提。
简言之，这些拟议的清朝措施与上文描述的较古老、低速的朝贡机制相合——旨在缓解而非防止罗妹号之类事件。

en: The indefatigable LeGendre countered again. In an official letter to his Qing counterpart, he urged that better roads, a large garrison, and monthly displays of Qing naval force off the south coast—leavened with threats of trade embargoes on powder, shot, and other necessities—would bring the Paiwan to heel and reduce the menace they posed to commerce once and for all. Writing in 1869, LeGendre showed awareness that his propositions would dramatically increase Qing budget outlays. And indigenous villages would be forced to deal routinely with soldiers and settlers under his plan—a sure recipe for bloodshed.
zh: 不知疲倦的李仙得再次反驳。在致清朝同僚的公函中，他力陈：更好的道路、一支大驻军、以及每月在南海岸展示清朝海军力量——辅以对火药、弹丸及其他必需品贸易禁运的威胁——将使排湾人驯服，并一劳永逸地减少他们对商业构成的威胁。写于 1869 年的这封信表明，李仙得意识到他的主张会急剧增加清朝预算开支。而在他的计划下，原住民村将被迫经常与士兵和定居者打交道——这必定酿成流血。

en: According to the Qing records of the October 1867 proceedings, Taiwan officials agreed with General Liu that fort construction on the south cape would provoke the Paiwanese (whom they termed “savages”).

Based on the events of 1875, we know that the Qing ministers had cause for concern. In the years immediately following the Taiwan expedition of 1874, Koalut, Saparek, and Mudan raids into lowland territory killed many, and one follow-up Qing expedition was massacred.

Even in 1867, without hindsight, it seemed to Qing officials that anything less than extermination or permanent occupation would add to the disorder that LeGendre sought to alleviate. As LeGendre himself pointed out, nonindigenous Langqiaoans who paid taxes to Paiwanese were getting off lightly. Were the Qing to extend its administration south of Fangliao, the financial burden would fall on them. Like his American counterparts who negotiated treaties with the Tokugawa Shogunate, then, LeGendre was urging the Qing to become more activist in ways that would surely create chaos, violence, and tax increases. The goal, in each case, was to expand the arena of global commerce in the name of a “general good” that, at least for the foreseeable future, did not include very many East Asians.
zh: 据清朝 1867 年 10 月交涉记录，台湾官员与刘将军一致认为，在南端筑堡会激怒排湾人（他们称之为“番”）。
基于 1875 年的事件，我们知道清朝大臣确有理由担忧。1874 年台湾远征之后紧接着的几年里，龟好儿、射麻里（Saparek）与牡丹社对低地领土的袭击杀死许多人，一支随后派出的清军队伍遭到屠杀。

即便在 1867 年、没有后见之明，清朝官员也觉得，除灭绝或永久占领外的任何做法，都会加剧李仙得试图缓解的混乱。正如李仙得本人指出的，向排湾人纳税的琅峤外来居民，所负担的税其实较轻。倘若清朝把行政扩展到枋寮以南，财政负担将落在他们身上。因此，像那些与德川幕府缔约的美国同僚一样，李仙得在敦促清朝以更积极干预的方式行事，而那必定制造混乱、暴力与增税。每个案例的目标，都是以一种“普遍善”的名义扩大全球商业的角力场——而这种善至少在可预见的未来并不包括太多东亚人。

en: It was not the case that all residents of Taiwan suffered at the hands of the activist American consul. For example, the residents of LeGendre’s base of operations in Siaoliao, where Japanese troops would also set up shop in 1874, eagerly joined efforts to extend the treaty-port economy’s reach. Wages for guide service, in addition to transshipment opportunities for the spoils of wreckage and profits from more legitimate forms of coastal trade, enriched Siaoliao residents in the 1860s and 1870s. Even before the arrival of LeGendre in 1867, the post–Opium War increase in intra-Asian junk traffic redounded to Siaoliao’s economic benefit.
zh: 并非所有台湾居民都在这位积极干预的美国领事手下受苦。例如，李仙得在射寮的行动基地的居民——1874 年日军也将在此驻扎——热切地加入了扩展条约口岸经济触角的努力。向导服务的工资，加上转运沉船劫掠物的机会、以及更正当形式的沿海贸易利润，使射寮居民在 1860 与 1870 年代致富。甚至在李仙得 1867 年到来之前，鸦片战争后亚洲内部帆船（junk）运输的增长就已给射寮带来经济利益。

en: When LeGendre received word in early 1872 that Toketok wished to see him again, it was through Miya (the son of a Siaoliao headman mentioned above) and his network that arrangements were made. Again the occasion was shipwreck trouble, this time the

. To assist in this case, LeGendre took the initiative without an official invitation and started for Taiwan in his capacity as a “piracy-suppressing consular official.” LeGendre briefly docked at the walled city of Taiwan-fu to apprise “civil and military authorities of the island” of his mission. Without personally visiting local officials in the prefectural capital, LeGendre steamed south and docked at Fangliao on March 1, 1872, with his picked men.
zh: 1872 年初，当李仙得收到卓杞笃希望再次见他的消息时，正是通过米亚（上文提到的一位射寮头人之子）及其网络才作了安排。这次的起因又是沉船麻烦，这回是伦敦城堡号（London Castle）。为协助处理此案，李仙得在没有官方邀请的情况下主动出击，以“镇压海盗的领事官员”身份启程赴台。李仙得在有城墙的台湾府城短暂停靠，向“岛上的文武官员”通报他的使命。他没有亲自拜访府城的地方官员，便乘船南下，于 1872 年 3 月 1 日带着他挑选的人手在枋寮靠岸。

en: LeGendre expected to find a garrison at Fangliao, in addition to personnel entrusted with securing castaways from Paiwanese hosts or captors, per his negotiations with Qing officials in 1867 through 1870. LeGendre found instead that the Qing had attached a single “military messenger” to the local headman. LeGendre turned to unnamed civilians for aid, but they proposed a service fee that LeGendre declined to pay, perhaps on principle. The next morning, LeGendre’s team disembarked farther south, near Siaoliao. When the party arrived on March 2, a U.S. consulate interpreter named James Johnson—himself a native of Xiamen, a veteran of the American Civil War, and a resident of New Jersey—sought out a Siaoliao man named Miya.

Miya had been LeGendre’s guide to the area in 1867 and 1869, and for his efforts as a member of Liu Mingdeng’s militia in 1867, he “was awarded the fifth military rank by the Taiwan” circuit intendant.
zh: 按照他 1867 至 1870 年间与清朝官员的谈判，李仙得本以为会在枋寮发现一支驻军，外加受托从收留或扣押他们的排湾人手中接回遇险船员的人员。结果李仙得发现，清朝只给地方头人配了一名“军中信差”。李仙得转而向一些未具名的平民求助，但他们提出一笔服务费，李仙得拒绝支付——或许是出于原则。次日早晨，李仙得的队伍在更南边、靠近射寮处登陆。当一行人于 3 月 2 日抵达时，一位名叫詹姆斯·约翰逊（James Johnson）的美国领事馆通事——他本人是厦门人、美国内战老兵、新泽西居民——去找一位名叫米亚的射寮人。
米亚曾在 1867 与 1869 年担任李仙得在该地区的向导，而因他 1867 年作为刘明灯团练一员的功劳，他被台湾道台“授予五品武职”。

en: Johnson finally located Miya. He and LeGendre then hatched a plan to visit Sabaree, a Paiwan settlement about an “hour’s walk from” the coast. LeGendre and Miya hired another guide and “twenty seven Chinese coolies” to haul the required gifts for diplomacy with the Paiwans. LeGendre described Miya and his other Siaoliao guide as “half-castes,” by which he meant people conversant in spoken Chinese (probably the Minnan variant) and a Paiwan dialect.
zh: 约翰逊终于找到了米亚。他与李仙得随即谋划拜访射麻里（Sabaree）——一个距海岸约“一小时步行路程”的排湾聚落。李仙得与米亚另雇了一名向导和“二十七名中国苦力”，搬运与排湾人外交所需的礼物。李仙得把米亚和他另一位射寮向导描述为“混血儿”（half-castes），他指的是能操汉语口语（大概是闽南语变体）和一种排湾方言的人。

en: A Paiwan man named Isa (also known as Esok or Yeesuk) presented himself to Miya and Johnson as the responsible leader in Sabaree, the via point for LeGendre’s meeting with Toketok. Like Miya and Johnson, Isa had met LeGendre on a previous occasion. After spending one evening in Sabaree, the U.S. consul, Miya, the Siaoliao guide, James Johnson, and twenty-seven porters walked another two hours inland to Tuilasok. Today, Highway 200 in Pingdong County runs through this same corridor; it is about two and a quarter miles from Sabaree to Tuilasok. In 1872, Tuilasok was the abode of Toketok. In Tuilasok, LeGendre and his large entourage were made to wait because Toketok had been detained on matters in a different village. Upon Toketok’s return, animals were slaughtered for a feast.
zh: 一位名叫伊萨（Isa，又名 Esok 或 Yeesuk）的排湾人向米亚与约翰逊自我介绍为射麻里的负责领袖——射麻里是李仙得与卓杞笃会面的途经点。与米亚和约翰逊一样，伊萨此前也见过李仙得。在射麻里度过一晚后，这位美国领事、米亚、射寮向导、詹姆斯·约翰逊与二十七名脚夫又向内陆步行两小时到猪朥束。如今，屏东县的 200 号公路正穿过这同一条走廊；从射麻里到猪朥束约两又四分之一英里。1872 年，猪朥束是卓杞笃的居所。在猪朥束，李仙得及其大批随从被迫等候，因为卓杞笃被另一个村的事务耽搁了。卓杞笃回来后，宰杀牲畜设宴。

en: LeGendre inquired about the disposition of shipwrecked sailors in the area since the 1867 agreement. It turned out that Toketok had aided a few groups but had never heard from Qing authorities about their ultimate safety. LeGendre took this lack of communication or recompense as a sign of Qing bad faith. LeGendre’s other reports emphasized that Paiwan settlements were jealous about the entry of outsiders and that Toketok was contemptuous of Qing officials. James Horn’s reports, quoted approvingly by William Pickering, painted Toketok as a shrewd manipulator and ransom taker. It is not clear why LeGendre expected the relationship between Qing officials and a toll-state broker such as Toketok to have been more cordial, routinized, and intimate. In fact, despite having a Siaoliao network in place and having met Toketok on two previous occasions, it was no small matter for the U.S. consul himself to locate Toketok and conduct business.
zh: 李仙得询问自 1867 年协议以来该地区沉船水手的处置情况。结果发现，卓杞笃曾援助过几批人，却从未从清朝当局那里得知他们最终是否安全。李仙得把这种缺乏沟通或酬报视为清朝背信的信号。李仙得的其他报告强调，排湾村社警惕外人进入，而卓杞笃蔑视清朝官员。詹姆斯·霍恩（James Horn）的报告——被毕麒麟赞许地引用——把卓杞笃描绘成一个精明的操纵者与赎金收取者。不清楚李仙得为何指望清朝官员与卓杞笃这样一个关卡型政体（toll-state）的居间人之间会有更融洽、更常规化、更亲密的关系。事实上，尽管已有一个射寮网络就位、且此前两次见过卓杞笃，对这位美国领事本人而言，找到卓杞笃并办事仍非易事。

en: It was during this visit to Siaoliao that LeGendre first heard about the plight of the fifty-four Ryūkyūans. Based on his interview with Toketok, LeGendre darkly hinted that the Chinese themselves were responsible for their deaths because the Qing government had refused to staff frontier outposts with agents who could expedite the ransom payments that would have saved the Ryūkyūans.
zh: 正是在这次射寮之行中，李仙得首次听说了五十四名琉球人的遭遇。基于他与卓杞笃的访谈，李仙得意有所指地暗示，中国人自己应对他们的死负责，因为清朝政府拒绝在边境哨所派驻能加快赎金支付的人员——而那些赎金本可救下琉球人。

en: The various eighteen tribes, as they were called, had populations of a couple hundred people—some more, some less. Their economies were of modest scale, compared to the nations that sent ships halfway around the world. Housing large groups of strangers who required shelter, food, water, and “supervision” strained local resources—to judge from the constant refrain that payment to the hosts was a sticking point for release. Sensibly, LeGendre urged that regular gift distribution and timely payments were key to securing the victims of shipwrecks. Oddly, LeGendre appears not to have considered the probability that large and routine payments to confederation leaders such as Toketok would have only increased their independence from the Qing, as well as the Hakka and bicultural settlements who provided LeGendre himself access to Paiwan representatives.
zh: 所谓的十八社，各社人口约两百人——有的多些，有的少些。与那些把船派到半个地球之外的国家相比，它们的经济规模不大。要为需要庇护、食物、水和“看管”的大批陌生人提供住宿，使地方资源吃紧——从一再出现的“向主人付酬是放人的症结”这一说法即可判断。李仙得明智地力陈，定期分发礼物与及时付酬是保全沉船受害者的关键。奇怪的是，李仙得似乎没有考虑到这种可能性：向卓杞笃这类联盟领袖大额而常规地付酬，只会让他们更不依赖清廷，也更不依赖那些为李仙得本人牵线、使他接触排湾代表的客家与跨文化村社。

en: But if strong and independent chiefs posed threats to the smooth functioning of a treaty-port maritime economy, so did weak ones. As Toketok explained it himself at the 1872 meeting, his authority among the confederated eighteen tribes was contested and not wholly dependable. At the banquet, LeGendre maneuvered Isa of Sabaree and Toketok of Tuilasok into explaining their exact political relationship, which turned out to be one of rivalry. As the public face of diplomacy with outsiders, Toketok made plenty of local enemies by collaborating with outsiders. Accordingly, Qing officials did reward Toketok with gifts and payments to help him maintain that authority, noted LeGendre. (We will find Mona Ludao facing the same dilemma in 1930, when Taiwan was under Japanese rule.)
zh: 但如果说强大而独立的酋长对条约口岸海洋经济的顺畅运转构成威胁，弱小的酋长亦然。正如卓杞笃本人在 1872 年会上所解释的，他在十八社联盟中的权威受到挑战，并不完全可靠。宴席上，李仙得设法让射麻里的伊萨与猪朥束的卓杞笃说明他们确切的政治关系，结果那是一种竞争关系。作为与外人外交的公开门面，卓杞笃因与外人合作而树敌众多。李仙得指出，因此清朝官员确曾以礼物和酬金回报卓杞笃，帮他维持那种权威。（我们会看到莫那·鲁道在 1930 年日本统治下的台湾面临同样的两难。）

en: Having said his farewells to Isa and the assembled Sabaree men at his second feast of the day, LeGendre headed back to Siaoliao on the coast, never to engage in palavers, gift exchanges, and toasts with Paiwan political leaders again. The date was March 5, 1872.
zh: 在当天第二场宴席上向伊萨与聚集的射麻里男子道别后，李仙得返回海岸边的射寮，此后再未与排湾政治领袖进行交涉、交换礼物与敬酒。日期是 1872 年 3 月 5 日。

en: THE MEIJI RESTORATION AND THE 1874 INVASION OF TAIWAN
zh: 明治维新与 1874 年侵台

en: Between 1867 and 1872, Charles LeGendre made a total of eight trips to Taiwan.

As LeGendre was shuttling back and forth from Xiamen to Taiwan-fu and making circuits of the island, the Tokugawa Shogunate in Japan was overthrown. The successor state was promulgated in 1868 with a sixteen-year-old emperor named Mutsuhito as the figurehead and symbolic apex/center. Mutsuhito is known to history as the emperor Meiji. A group of samurai, mostly from the old feudal domains of Satsuma and Chōshū, strove to build a state that could resist the impositions of industrialized Euro-American powers. Thus, the so-called Meiji oligarchs set out to collapse the status-group distinctions and regional inequalities sanctioned by the Tokugawa dynastic state. At the same time, they positioned the nascent national geobody within a complex regional system at the intersection of Western international society and the East Asian tributary system.
zh: 1867 至 1872 年间，李仙得共八次赴台。

当李仙得在厦门与台湾府之间往返穿梭、环岛巡行时，日本的德川幕府被推翻。继任国家于 1868 年宣告成立，以一位名叫睦仁（Mutsuhito）的十六岁天皇为名义上的领袖和国家统一的最高象征。睦仁在历史上以明治天皇之名闻名。一群武士——主要来自萨摩与长州（Chōshū）旧封建藩——努力建设一个能抵抗工业化欧美列强强加要求的国家。于是，所谓的明治寡头着手消除德川王朝政权所维系的身份等级和地区不平等。与此同时，他们把这个新生的国家地理体安置在一个复杂区域体系之中——该体系处于西方国际社会与东亚朝贡体系的交汇处。

en: Almost from the start, Meiji diplomats tried to do away with tributary protocol because it diminished the dignity of the Japanese emperor by referring to him as a mere “king,” a subordinate to the Middle Kingdom (Qing) emperor. Facing their neighbors, the Meiji oligarchs promoted the new form of state-to-state relations (see introduction). Japan’s central authority, the Council of State, launched a number of ill-fated diplomatic initiatives to the Korean court in the 1870s to abolish older practices, finally imposing a trade treaty in 1876 through the use of force.
zh: 几乎从一开始，明治外交官就试图废除朝贡礼仪，因为它把日本天皇仅称为“国王”——中国（清朝）皇帝的臣属——从而贬损了日本天皇的尊严。面对邻国，明治寡头推行新型的国家间关系（见导论）。日本的中央权威太政官（Council of State）在 1870 年代向朝鲜朝廷发起了一系列命运多舛的外交倡议，以废除旧有做法，最终于 1876 年通过武力强加了一项通商条约。

en: Regarding Japan’s more powerful neighbor, the Qing dynasty, negotiation was the only way forward. An early treaty was signed with the Qing in 1871. Many in Japan, however, found it objectionable for retaining the irksome extraterritoriality clauses of Western treaties with Japan and China. To revise the 1871 Qing treaty, diplomat Yanaihara Sakimitsu went to Beijing in 1872. There, he read about the murder of the fifty-four Ryūkyūans in Langqiao from the official gazette,

. Yanaihara sent the clipping to Minister of Foreign Affairs Soejima Taneomi in Tokyo in May 1872. This letter put the incident on the central government’s radar even before the survivors returned to Naha. After the shipwreck victims were repatriated on July 12, a visiting Kagoshima man, Ichiji Sadaka, caught wind of their plights while in Naha and relayed the news to Kagoshima Prefecture governor Ōyama Tsunayoshi.
zh: 至于日本更强大的邻国清朝，谈判是唯一出路。1871 年与清朝签订了一项早期条约。然而日本国内许多人觉得它令人反感，因为它保留了西方与日本、中国所订条约中那些恼人的治外法权条款。为修订 1871 年清约，外交官柳原前光（Yanaihara Sakimitsu）于 1872 年赴北京。在那里，他从官方邸报《京报》（Jingbao）上读到五十四名琉球人在琅峤被杀的消息。柳原于 1872 年 5 月把这份剪报寄给东京的外务卿副岛种臣（Soejima Taneomi）。这封信使该事件在幸存者返回那霸之前就进入了中央政府的视野。7 月 12 日沉船受害者被遣返后，一位来访的鹿儿岛人伊地知贞馨（Ichiji Sadaka）在那霸期间风闻他们的遭遇，并把消息转达给鹿儿岛县令大山纲良（Ōyama Tsunayoshi）。

en: Since 1609, the Ryūkyūs had been tributary to both Satsuma domain (which subsumed Kagoshima castle town) in Japan and the Qing empire. On August 29, 1871, the domains in Japan were abolished, and the Ryūkyūs were, on paper at least, folded into the new entity of Kagoshima Prefecture.

However, there was still a court in Shuri castle of Naha, and the Ryūkyūans considered themselves tributary to the Qing. It was precisely during the Miyakojima sailors’ ordeal in Taiwan (November 30, 1871, through July 12, 1872) that central administrators in Tokyo were devising institutional and pragmatic stratagems for integrating Ryūkyū into the Japanese state, destroying the legitimacy of the Shō dynasty, and separating Ryūkyū from China. Because of its timing, then, the shipwreck was a godsend for Japanese who sought a firmer international claim to exclusive sovereignty over the Ryūkyūs.
zh: 自 1609 年以来，琉球一直同时向日本的萨摩藩（辖鹿儿岛城下町）与清帝国朝贡。1871 年 8 月 29 日，日本废藩，琉球至少在纸面上被并入新设的鹿儿岛县。
然而，那霸首里城仍有一个朝廷，琉球人自认为向清朝朝贡。正是在宫古岛水手于台湾受难期间（1871 年 11 月 30 日至 1872 年 7 月 12 日），东京的中央行政官员正在谋划把琉球并入日本国家、摧毁尚氏王朝合法性、并使琉球脱离中国的制度性与务实性策略。因此，由于其时机，这场沉船事件对那些寻求对琉球排他性主权更坚实国际主张的日本人而言，是天赐良机。

en: Kagoshima governor Ōyama’s August 31, 1872, letter urged Meiji to punish the Taiwanese for harming his subjects (the ill-fated Miyakojima tribute mission) in order to “spread the imperial prestige abroad and succor the angry spirits of Your islanders below.”

In October 1872, these bottom-up rumblings from Kagoshima gained traction in Tokyo with the aid of Charles De Long, the American minister to Japan. Seeking to drive a wedge between the Qing and Japan, De Long stirred the pot by drawing Minister of Foreign Affairs Soejima Taneomi’s attention to the Taiwan shipwreck and suggesting that it be made the occasion of an armed expedition. To further his aims, De Long introduced Soejima to LeGendre, who was just six months past his last visit to the Langqiao headmen Isa and Toketok. The two statesmen discussed Taiwan with the aid of LeGendre’s extensive map collection. By December 1872, Soejima convinced the Council of State to hire LeGendre as a high-ranking advisor to the Japanese court.
zh: 鹿儿岛县令大山 1872 年 8 月 31 日的信敦促明治惩罚伤害其臣民（命运多舛的宫古岛朝贡使团）的台湾人，以“扬皇威于海外，慰尔岛民愤怒之灵于下”。

1872 年 10 月，这股来自鹿儿岛地方的施压，在美国驻日公使查尔斯·德朗（Charles De Long）的助力下，在东京得到响应。德朗企图在清朝与日本之间打入楔子，他煽风点火，把外务卿副岛种臣的注意力引向台湾沉船事件，并建议以此为由发动武装远征。为推进其目标，德朗把副岛引荐给李仙得——后者距上次拜访琅峤头人伊萨与卓杞笃仅六个月。两位政治家借助李仙得丰富的地图收藏讨论台湾。到 1872 年 12 月，副岛说服太政官聘请李仙得为日本朝廷的高级别顾问。

en: The Meiji emperor himself received Soejima and LeGendre on March 9, 1873, and issued a rescript granting Soejima full authority to avenge the deaths of the Ryūkyūans.
They both set off for Beijing in mid-March 1873 to ratify a revised version of the Sino-Japanese Friendship Treaty of 1871.

But there was also an unannounced goal for this mission: Soejima and Yanaihara Sakimitsu would put the Ryūkyū shipwreck case before Qing officials to notify them of an invasion of the areas of Taiwan “beyond Qing government.” LeGendre thought the Qing might actually cede a portion of the island and allow its permanent occupation by Japan without a fight. On June 21, back-channel negotiations conducted by Yanaihara, his interpreter, Zheng Yan’ning (Tei Entei), and three Qing officials named Mao Changxi, Dong Xun, and Sun Shida addressed the 1871 shipwreck.
zh: 明治天皇本人于 1873 年 3 月 9 日接见副岛与李仙得，并颁布敕语，授予副岛为琉球人之死复仇的全权。
两人于 1873 年 3 月中旬启程赴北京，以办理1871年《中日修好条规》修订本的批准换约。
但此行还有一个未公开的目标：副岛与柳原前光将把琉球沉船案提交清朝官员，以通知他们日本将入侵台湾“清朝政府之外”的地区。李仙得以为清朝或许真会割让该岛一部分，并允许日本不经战斗而永久占领。6 月 21 日，由柳原、其通事郑永宁（Tei Entei）与三位清朝官员毛昶熙、董恂、孙士达进行的秘密渠道谈判，处理了 1871 年沉船案。

en: The Japanese side, according to later testimony (the correspondence was not preserved), claimed to be the rightful defenders of the beheaded Ryūkyūans. They informed Qing negotiators that Japan would send a punitive expedition to Taiwan to find the murderers and punish them. The Japanese delegation argued that Taiwan was so starkly divided between its governed, Chinese territory and its ungoverned, indigenous territory that a foreign army could militarily occupy the latter without appreciably affecting the former.
zh: 据后来的证词（往来信件未保存），日方自称是被斩首琉球人的正当保护者。他们告知清朝谈判代表，日本将派一支惩罚性远征军赴台，找出凶手并予以惩罚。日本代表团辩称，台湾在其受治理的华人领土与不受治理的原住民领土之间划分得如此鲜明，以至于一支外国军队可以军事占领后者，而不会明显影响前者。

en: Qing statesmen, led by Li Hongzhang himself, did not acknowledge these side talks as part of the formal diplomatic mission. The Qing view that emerged from the discussions nonetheless defined the Ryūkyū Kingdom as tributary to the Qing; the 1871 shipwreck was an internal matter. According to Beijing, the Qing magistrate’s repatriation of twelve survivors to Naha demonstrated sovereignty. They considered the case closed. Qing officials stated that the savages (
) were but one of many border peoples whom the empire allowed to maintain separate customs and usages. Qing claims that the assailants were beyond the pale of civilization (
) and yet within the imperial realm were seized upon by Japanese negotiators, who made much of the term
in subsequent diplomatic squabbles regarding the righteousness of the 1874 invasion.
zh: 以李鸿章本人为首的清朝政治家，不承认这些私下会谈是正式外交使命的一部分。尽管如此，从讨论中浮现的清朝观点把琉球王国界定为向清朝朝贡；1871 年沉船案是内部事务。按北京的说法，清朝地方官把十二名幸存者遣返那霸，体现了主权。他们认为此案已了结。清朝官员声称，番人（banmin、seiban）不过是帝国允许保留各自风俗与习惯的众多边境民族之一。清朝关于袭击者在教化所不及的“化外”（kegai），却仍处于帝国疆域以内的说法，被日本谈判代表抓住不放，他们在随后关于 1874 年入侵正当性的外交争执中大做“化外”一词的文章。

en: By failing to restrain wreckers on the south coast, the Japanese side reasoned, the Qing had forfeited its claims to jurisdiction in Langqiao. The Japanese delegates argued that it was their right and duty to “chastise” the “barbarians,” either before a European power filled the vacuum by annexing Taiwan as a colony, or before enraged Japanese vigilantes stormed the island in defiance of all governments.
The diplomats returned to Japan with the Mudan village incident left unresolved.
zh: 日方推论，清朝因未能约束南海岸的劫掠者，已丧失其对琅峤的管辖权主张。日本代表辩称，“惩戒”“蛮夷”是他们的权利与义务——要么赶在某个欧洲列强通过把台湾吞并为殖民地来填补真空之前，要么赶在愤怒的擅自采取报复行动的日本人无视一切政府、攻上该岛之前。
外交官们返回日本，牡丹社事件悬而未决。

en: Foreign Minister Soejima resigned in the aftermath of the October 1873 debates among Council of State oligarchs over invading Korea (the

affair). Therefore, plans for the invasion of Taiwan remained dormant that winter. In the spring of 1874, however, they were revived to mollify Satsuma men such as Saigō Tsugumichi. In the wake of the

hollowing out of Japan’s central administration, the Taiwan invasion held together a fractured oligarchy by throwing a bone to expansionists who remained in Tokyo. On May 4,Ōkuma Shigenobu was put in charge of the “Taiwan Savage Territory Office” to occupy Langqiao. As the plans to invade Taiwan became public knowledge, Western diplomats declared their neutrality in deference to the Qing, though sub rosa support for Japan was also in evidence.

Recalibrating in light of foreign pressure,Ōkubo Toshimichi, a leading member of the council, cabled the expedition’s commander, Saigō Tsugumichi, to delay the mission.
