In contravention of Ōkubo’s order, on May 2, 1874, Saigō sent the first transport with 1,200 soldiers to Taiwan, with three more to follow.
zh: 外务卿副岛在 1873 年 10 月太政官寡头就是否入侵朝鲜展开辩论（征韩论事件）之后辞职。因此，入侵台湾的计划在那个冬天搁置。然而 1874 年春，这些计划被重新提起，以安抚西乡从道等萨摩人士。在征韩论掏空日本中央行政之后，侵台计划通过给留在东京的扩张派一点好处，把分裂的寡头集团维系在一起。5 月 4 日，大隈重信（Ōkuma Shigenobu）被任命主管“蕃地事务局”，以占领琅峤。随着侵台计划成为公开知识，西方外交官出于对清朝的尊重宣布中立，尽管暗中支持日本的迹象也存在。
在外国施压后调整对策，太政官核心成员大久保利通致电远征军司令西乡从道，要求推迟任务。与大久保的命令相违，1874 年 5 月 2 日，西乡派出第一艘运输船载 1200 名士兵赴台，随后还有三艘。

en: The Japanese expeditionary force deployed 3,658 men between May and December 1874. LeGendre himself did not participate, but his network was put to good use by General Akamatsu Noriyoshi and Douglas Cassel, a lieutenant commander in the U.S. Navy charged with operations planning. The first Japanese ship arrived in Langqiao Bay on May 7. It docked at Siaoliao, where LeGendre had disembarked for the 1872 mission recounted above.
zh: 1874 年 5 月至 12 月间，日本远征军部署了 3658 人。李仙得本人没有参与，但他的网络被赤松则良（Akamatsu Noriyoshi）将军与道格拉斯·卡塞尔充分利用——后者是美国海军少校，负责作战计划。第一艘日本船于 5 月 7 日抵达琅峤湾。它在射寮靠岸，即上文所述李仙得 1872 年任务登陆之处。

en: The lengthy correspondence between Ōkuma Shigenobu and Charles LeGendre reveals that cooperation with local agents in Siaoliao was anticipated, as well as some sort of alliance with Toketok and the Tuilasok Paiwans. LeGendre recommended that Siaoliao headman Miya be sought out before troops disembarked. According to LeGendre’s instructions, the Siaoliao and Tuilasok men were to be threatened with an invasion force of twenty-five thousand men and utter extermination. They had narrowly escaped suspicion for collusion in the deaths of the fifty-four Ryūkyūans, LeGendre warned through Cassel, because they had extended courtesies to LeGendre in 1872.
zh: 大隈重信与李仙得之间冗长的通信表明，日方预期与射寮的地方代理人合作，并与卓杞笃及猪朥束排湾人结成某种联盟。李仙得建议在部队登陆前先找到射寮头人米亚。按李仙得的指示，要以一支两万五千人的入侵部队和彻底灭绝来威胁射寮与猪朥束人。李仙得通过卡塞尔警告说，他们之所以才勉强没有被视为杀害五十四名琉球人的同谋，是因为他们 1872 年曾礼遇李仙得。

en: Commander Cassel arrived in Langqiao with Fukushima Kunari, the Japanese consul at Xiamen, on May 6, 1874, aboard the vessel Yūkōmaru. Cassel had also taken a commission from the Japanese government to execute the punitive expedition to Taiwan. The Chinese-American interpreter James Johnson was sent ashore to locate Miya and his relatives. A payment of cash was offered to retain the services of the leading family of Siaoliao, while LeGendre’s threats and promises were issued on shipboard. The following week, through Miya’s orchestration, the Japanese hired around five hundred Chinese laborers, organized by headmen, at wages of thirty cents per day. The local economy received another boon from the sale of provisions and land rentals. Journalist Edward House remarked sardonically about the entrepreneurial spirit of local Langqiaoans, who leveraged their bargaining power without hesitation.
zh: 1874 年 5 月 6 日，卡塞尔海军中校与日本驻厦门领事福岛九成（Fukushima Kunari）乘有功丸（Yūkōmaru）抵达琅峤。卡塞尔还接受了日本政府的委任，执行对台湾的惩罚性远征。华裔美国通事詹姆斯·约翰逊被派上岸去找米亚及其亲属。日方提出付现金以留用射寮望族的服务，而李仙得的威胁与许诺则在船上发出。接下来一周，经米亚居间安排，日本人雇了约五百名中国劳工，由头人组织，日薪三十美分。地方经济又从出售口粮与出租土地中获得一笔好处。记者爱德华·豪斯（Edward House）讥讽地谈到当地琅峤人的创业精神——他们毫不犹豫地利用自己的议价能力。

en: On May 10, Cassel sent Johnson, Miya, and attached Siaoliao interpreters to arrange a meeting with Tuilasok leaders. Miya had reported Toketok’s death earlier, so plans to work through his successor, Isa of Sabaree, were put into place. The first diplomatic encounter between Japanese officers and the Langqiao confederation was held on May 16. The encounter took place at the village of Wangsha, a small settlement called “semi-savage” in Japanese accounts and “half-caste” in English accounts—signifying its location in the foothills at the entrance to the areas of Paiwan domination.
zh: 5 月 10 日，卡塞尔派约翰逊、米亚及随行的射寮通事去安排与猪朥束领袖的会面。米亚此前已报告卓杞笃之死，于是通过其继任者、射麻里的伊萨来运作的计划被付诸实施。日本军官与琅峤联盟之间的首次外交接触于 5 月 16 日举行。接触发生在网纱（Wangsha）村——一个在日本记述中被称为“半番”、在英文记述中被称为“混血”的小聚落，意指它位于排湾人支配区域入口处的山麓丘陵。

en: Three Paiwan headmen agreed to meet with the Japanese on neutral ground. They refused to enter the Japanese camp near Siaoliao, and they resisted requests to enter their own villages beyond Wangsha in the mountains. The Sabaree chief Isa, who took charge of the Paiwan delegation, brought a large retinue of armed retainers. Cassel acted as General Akamatsu’s translator, it appears, while he also issued his own declarations as LeGendre’s surrogate. Johnson translated for Cassel (from English into southern Chinese), while Miya translated for Johnson (from southern Chinese into a Paiwan dialect). Journalist Edward House reported: “The interview was not very long, and although the colloquy was necessarily slow, requiring triple translation each way—from Japanese into English, thence into Chinese and again into the savage dialect, with the same process in reverse in replies—there was little occasion for extensive discussion.

children: The mere forms of meeting and recognition, and the interchange of a few reassuring words were about all that was really required

en: .” Three Snider rifles were given to Isa and the other Paiwan headmen, and the meeting was concluded with drinks and a feast.
zh: 三位排湾头人同意在中立地带与日本人会面。他们拒绝进入射寮附近的日军营地，也不肯让日方进入网纱以外、山中的本方村落。负责排湾代表团的射麻里酋长伊萨带来大批武装扈从。看来卡塞尔充当赤松将军的翻译，同时他又以李仙得代理人的身份发表自己的声明。约翰逊为卡塞尔翻译（从英语译成南方汉语），米亚则为约翰逊翻译（从南方汉语译成一种排湾方言）。记者爱德华·豪斯报道：“会谈不长，虽然对话必然缓慢——每一方向都需三重翻译：从日语到英语，再到汉语，再到番语方言，答复时则反向重复同一过程——但也很少有必要展开讨论。真正需要的，不过是会面与致意的形式，以及几句安抚话的交换。”三支斯奈德（Snider）步枪赠给伊萨与其他排湾头人，会面以饮酒和宴席结束。

en: Aspects of the scene described above were repeated late into the summer of 1874. In published writings, journalist Edward House and LeGendre emphasized the warm relations that permeated indigenous-outsider relations in Langqiao. Saigō Tsugumichi’s 1902 obituary claimed that he wore the silver bracelet received from Paiwan headmen at one of these feasts into old age. This bracelet was immortalized in a postcard set issued on the twentieth anniversary of his death and in a photo attached to a 1936 tribute to his Taiwan days, financed by Saigō’s family and admirers.
zh: 上述场景的某些方面一直重复到 1874 年夏末。在公开发表的文字中，记者爱德华·豪斯与李仙得强调弥漫于琅峤原住民与外人关系中的温情。西乡从道 1902 年的讣告声称，他一直把在一次这类宴席上从排湾头人那里收到的银手镯戴到老年。这只手镯在他逝世二十周年发行的一套明信片中、以及在 1936 年一份由其家人及仰慕者出资、纪念他台湾岁月的纪念出版物所附照片中留下记录。

en: But Gatling guns, military parades, and intimations of larger troop deployments were subsequently brandished to intimidate the Paiwan emissaries who received Japanese gifts. And as Japanese troops began to use this firepower to destroy Paiwan bodies, villages, and landscapes, it became easier to arrange meetings. Thereafter, the conferences lost the character of diplomatic encounters and became occasions for the Japanese to enumerate demands and specify the parameters of acceptable conduct.
zh: 但随后，加特林（Gatling）机枪、阅兵式、以及更大规模部队部署的暗示被炫耀出来，以恐吓接受日本礼物的排湾使者。而随着日军开始用这种火力摧毁排湾人的身体、村落与地景，安排会面变得更容易。此后，这些会议失去了外交接触的性质，变成日本人罗列要求、规定哪些行为可以接受的场合。

en: This paradigm shift is illustrated by the second major meeting between Japanese forces and Paiwan headmen, held on May 25, 1874. This meeting occurred three days after a battle that broadcast the Japanese Army’s capacity for carnage loudly and clearly. The May 22, 1874, Stone Gate Battle broke out during the search for perpetrators of an earlier Paiwan ambush. According to Cassel, the Japanese troops blundered into Stone Gate for lack of discipline—merely to avenge the death of a single soldier. The two or three hundred Paiwanese defenders at Stone Gate were led by Alok and his son. Both were killed in the melee, along with another thirty or so Mudan warriors. Many more were wounded. On the Japanese side, between four and seven were killed and over a dozen wounded (accounts vary). News of Alok’s death and the ferocity of Japanese troops—who severed a dozen Paiwan heads and brought them back to camp with other trophies of war—prompted Isa and other leaders to seek out Commander Saigō in order to avoid becoming the next victims.
zh: 这一范式转变，由 1874 年 5 月 25 日日军与排湾头人之间的第二次重要会面所体现。这次会面发生在一场战役三天之后，那场战役响亮而清楚地宣示了日本陆军制造杀戮的能力。1874 年 5 月 22 日的石门战役，是在搜捕此前一次排湾伏击的肇事者时爆发的。据卡塞尔说，日军因缺乏纪律而莽撞闯入石门——只为给一名士兵之死复仇。石门两三百名排湾守军由阿碌（Alok）及其子率领。两人都在混战中被杀，另有约三十名牡丹社战士丧生。更多人受伤。日方有四至七人被杀、十余人受伤（各记述不一）。阿碌之死的消息、以及日军的凶残——他们割下十二颗排湾人头，连同其他战利品带回营地——促使伊萨与其他领袖去找西乡司令，以免成为下一批受害者。

en: The May 25, 1874, conference was attended by Commander Saigō himself and was held at Miya’s personal residence. The main forces of Paiwanese guards and Japanese soldiers were kept away, since there was mutual suspicion. The five Paiwan delegates themselves arrived with a cow, ten chickens, hides, and millet wine. Saigō “ordered a very large package of very handsome presents to be brought,”
which “consisted of two superb Japanese swords, packages of silk, woolen and cotton cloths, and a variety of... ‘fancy goods.’”
zh: 1874 年 5 月 25 日的会议由西乡司令本人出席，在米亚的私宅举行。由于彼此猜疑，排湾护卫与日本士兵的主力都被隔开。五名排湾代表自己带着一头牛、十只鸡、兽皮与小米酒前来。西乡“命人取来一大包非常丰厚的礼物”，
其中“包括两把极好的日本刀、成包的丝绸、毛料与棉布，以及各式……‘精巧货品’”。

en: The Japanese side, through the same three layers of translation that obtained during the first meeting on May 16, admonished Isa and the others that
zh: 日方通过 5 月 16 日首次会面时所用的同样三层翻译，告诫伊萨等人：

en: …there were two tribes of people with whom we [the Japanese forces] have a deadly quarrel, and that not one single man of these should escape the death which they deserved at our hands. These were the [Mudan], and the [Kuskus] who had helped them, and that, as sure as the sun rose in the East and set in the West every man of these wicked people should surely die by our hands. But that we had heard that some of the people from [Sabaree] and [Tuilasok], and the other Southern tribes had availed themselves of the mountain roads to go round and join our enemies, these treacherous and murderous [Mudan], and I wished to solemnly warn him that if this were really done, the most dreadful punishment would fall upon him and all his people.
zh: ……有两个社的人，我们[日军]与之有不共戴天之仇，他们中没有一个能逃脱应死于我们之手的命运。这就是[牡丹社]，以及帮助过他们的[高士佛]；正如太阳东升西落一样确定，这些邪恶之人每一个都必死于我们之手。但我们听说，[射麻里]与[猪朥束]及其他南方各社的一些人，曾利用山路绕道去加入我们的敌人——这些奸诈而嗜杀的[牡丹社]人；我要郑重警告他：倘若真这样做，最可怕的惩罚将降临他和他全体族人身上。

en: Isa, who led this delegation, did not require Miya’s third layer of interpretation; like Toketok’s brother and his adopted son, Bunkiet, Isa could understand spoken Chinese. He assented to the demands that Japanese troops have free access to the peninsula and that Mudan and Kuskus men not be harbored. Cassel then promised to distribute flags to sixteen of the eighteen tribes of Langqiao—Isa asked to receive them personally. The absence of the flags would then identify the Mudan and Kuskus foes as fair game for Japanese soldiers to fire upon at will. Imperial Japanese presumption of indigenous collective guilt, and the delineation of free-fire zones marked out for generalized punishment, would reemerge in the early twentieth century in the camphor wars against the Atayal, Saisiyat, Truku, and Sediq peoples of northern Taiwan.
zh: 率领这个代表团的伊萨不需要米亚的第三层翻译；与卓杞笃的兄弟及其养子文杰（Bunkiet）一样，伊萨能听懂汉语口语。他应允了这些要求：日军可自由进入半岛，且不得窝藏牡丹社与高士佛人。卡塞尔随即承诺向琅峤十八社中的十六社分发旗帜——伊萨要求亲自接收。届时没有旗帜，就会把牡丹社与高士佛敌人标识为日本士兵可随意射击的目标。日本帝国对原住民集体罪责的推定，以及为普遍惩罚而划定的自由射击区，将在二十世纪初对台湾北部泰雅、赛夏、德路固与赛德克各民族的樟脑战争中重新出现。

en: Since the Japanese did not have actual flags on hand for villages to hoist for protection, numbered certificates with the names of the villages and headmen were issued and then distributed as promissory notes on the flags (see

). It is hard to imagine how such placards might have shielded civilians from collateral damage or cases of mistaken identity. In any event, Japanese official histories reproduced facsimiles of them in their accounts of the occupation, as if to document the army’s precision and discrimination, in the midst of a rough-and-ready display of brute force that sent a message not dissimilar to that of the French crown’s execution of the regicide Damian, as famously reconstructed by Michel Foucault.

Against this backdrop of imminent threat, Cassel wrangled an agreement out of Isa for permission to build another fort in Langqiao, this time on the east coast. The sufficiently rattled Isa accepted. After these terse communications were relayed back and forth, Saigō’s gifts were distributed while cups of “Chinese samshu” were passed around so the gathered parties could “drink Friendship” (Cassel’s words) to conclude the proceedings.
zh: 由于日本人手头没有可供各村升起以求保护的实际旗帜，便签发了写有村名与头人名的编号证书，作为日后领取旗帜的凭券分发（见
）。很难想象这类告示牌如何能保护平民免于交战中的误伤，或因身份被认错而受害。无论如何，日本官方史书在其占领记述中复制了这些证书的摹本，仿佛要证明军队的精确与辨别力——而这一切发生在一场粗暴蛮力的草率展示之中，其传递的信息与法国王室处决被控弑君的达米安（Damian）并无二致，后者经米歇尔·福柯（Michel Foucault）的著名重构而广为人知。
在这一迫近威胁的背景下，卡塞尔从伊萨那里争得一项协议，获准在琅峤再建一座堡垒，这次在东海岸。被充分震慑的伊萨接受了。这些简短的交涉来回传达之后，西乡的礼物被分发，同时一杯杯“中国烧酒”（samshu）被传递，使与会各方能“饮友谊之酒”（卡塞尔语）以结束议程。

en: The expedition’s only set-piece, scripted military operations—drawn up to punish the alleged killers of the Ryūkyūans—were raids on Mudan and Kuskus settlements from June 1 through June 3. These search-and-destroy missions were carried out by three detachments. They hacked through tough terrain and numerous improvised Paiwan defense works to cross the narrow peninsula. The sweltering heat, swollen rivers, Saigō’s nocturnal bivouac, and army food shortages became part of the mission’s lore. Although it was celebrated in press reportage and colorful wood-block prints as a glorious affair, the climax was less so: the burning of a few Paiwanese settlements in Mudan and neighboring Ernai. These villages were abandoned before the Japanese arrived, because they had been warned away by the skirmish at Stone Gate.
zh: 远征军唯一一场预先拟定方案的成套军事行动——旨在惩罚据称杀害琉球人的凶手——是 6 月 1 日至 3 日对牡丹社与高士佛聚落的袭击。这些搜索歼灭任务由三支分遣队执行。他们劈开艰难地形与众多排湾人临时构筑的防御工事，穿越狭窄的半岛。酷热、暴涨的河流、西乡的夜间露营、以及军队粮荒，都成为这次任务传说的一部分。尽管新闻报道与彩色木版画把它颂扬为一桩光荣事迹，高潮却没那么光彩：焚毁牡丹社及邻近尔乃（Ernai）的几个排湾聚落。这些村落在日军到来前已被放弃，因为石门的小规模战斗已警告他们离开。

en: To formalize the victory over Mudan, a triumphal procession was held at the Kameyama headquarters just south of Siaoliao on June 5. Three days later, delegates from numerous tribes came to meet Saigō. In American accounts, nine different certificates were redeemed for proper flags. In a Japanese account, based presumably on more detailed reports, sixteen flags were distributed that day.

At this meeting, the Japanese troops reinforced the lessons taught at Stone Gate and in the village-burning exercises of early June by displaying their Gatling guns and massed troops in formation. Resistance was futile. Again, gifts—though of a less generous nature—were distributed. Here, Isa consented to a Japanese fort at a specific location on the east coast, while refusing the offer of rent for the land.
zh: 为把对牡丹社的胜利正式化，6 月 5 日在射寮以南的龟山（Kameyama）司令部举行了一场凯旋游行。三天后，众多社的代表前来会见西乡。在美国记述中，九张不同的证书被兑换成正式旗帜。在一份大概基于更详细报告的日本记述中，那天分发了十六面旗帜。
在这次会上，日军通过展示加特林机枪与列队集结的部队，强化了石门及六月初焚烧村落的行动所给的教训。抵抗是徒劳的。礼物再次分发——尽管不那么丰厚。在这里，伊萨同意日本在东海岸一个特定地点建堡，却拒绝接受为土地付租的提议。

en: The June 8 meeting can be interpreted as the culmination of a series of meetings with lower-Hengchun headmen that commenced in 1867 with LeGendre’s first confab with Toketok. This sequence of complex encounters can be viewed as a progression of sorts. That is to say, over the course of seven years, wet diplomatic exchanges between Paiwan leaders and outsiders—effected by offers of gifts and pledges of mutual obligation—gave way to more scripted encounters wherein formalistic, rule-laden edicts were issued simultaneously with threats of violence. Initially, for LeGendre to meet Toketok on September 10, 1867, with a few interpreters, it required weeks of advance planning and mediation. Toketok made the U.S. consul wait and finally granted him a brief audience in his own compound. The first Japanese meeting with Isa, on May 16, 1874, was held on neutral ground, while the second one, on May 25, occurred in Miya’s courtyard within shouting distance of Camp Kameyama. For the June 8, 1874, meeting, Saigō and his men didn’t budge but instead waited for the Langqiao headmen to visit Saigō’s headquarters (see

). As Edward House reported, by then the Japanese had reckoned the total Paiwanese population of Langqiao at three thousand people—fewer than the number of Japanese forces brought to bear on the peninsula. The outcome of the military contest was longer in doubt by June 8. Therefore, the Paiwan emissaries were treated as supplicants.
zh: 6 月 8 日的会面，可被解读为与下恒春头人一系列会面的顶点——这一系列始于 1867 年李仙得与卓杞笃的首次洽谈。这一连串复杂接触可被视为某种递进。也就是说，七年间，排湾领袖与外人之间以赠礼和相互义务承诺促成的湿外交交换，让位于更按脚本编排的接触：在其中，按固定格式宣示的成文命令与暴力威胁同时发出。起初，李仙得要在 1867 年 9 月 10 日带几名通事去见卓杞笃，需要数周的事先筹划与居间协调。卓杞笃让这位美国领事等候，最终才在自己的院落里给他一次简短接见。日本人与伊萨的首次会面（1874 年 5 月 16 日）在中立地带举行，而第二次（5 月 25 日）发生在米亚的庭院，距龟山营仅咫尺之遥。至于 1874 年 6 月 8 日的会面，西乡及其部下留在营地等候，而是等琅峤头人来拜访西乡的司令部（见
）。正如爱德华·豪斯所报道，到那时日本人估算琅峤排湾人总人口为三千——少于被调来对付半岛的日军数目。到 6 月 8 日，军事较量的结果已不再悬而未决。因此，排湾使者被当作恳求者对待。
body.review: 原书此段作1867年9月10日，与本章前文所记10月10日不同。该段末句原文为 was longer in doubt，结合兵力对比及下句，疑脱 no，译为“已不再悬而未决”。

en: On July 1, a fourth meeting included the recently vanquished Mudan representatives. Sakuma Samata (who would become the fourth governor-general of Taiwan in 1906) acted as Saigō’s delegate at this session, which was held in Poliac, the Hakka settlement that functioned as the gateway to the interior. Much had happened since the June 8 conference at Camp Kameyama. On June 22, the Qing plenipotentiary Shen Baozhen visited Langqiao and demanded that Saigō cease operations. Saigō was not empowered to negotiate with Shen, but the writing was on the wall. Japanese troops would be leaving in the near future and would not colonize Taiwan. Nonetheless, Sakuma read a battery of prohibitions and warnings to the assembled headmen and issued flags. By November, at least fifty-three flags had been doled out to Paiwan emissaries (see
and 10).
zh: 7 月 1 日，第四次会面纳入了新近被征服的牡丹社代表。佐久间左马太（他将于 1906 年成为第四任台湾总督）在这次会议上充当西乡的代表；会议在保力举行——这个客家聚落是通往内陆的门户。自 6 月 8 日龟山营会议以来，发生了许多事。6 月 22 日，清朝全权大臣沈葆桢（Shen Baozhen）访问琅峤，要求西乡停止行动。西乡无权与沈谈判，但大势已去。日军将在不久的将来离开，不会殖民台湾。尽管如此，佐久间仍向聚集的头人宣读了一连串禁令与警告，并颁发旗帜。到 11 月，至少五十三面旗帜已分发给排湾使者（见
与
