en: But wet diplomacy was not yet dead in Hengchun, despite the complete reversal in power relations. In August, the Tuilasok headman invited Commander Saigō for a banquet with representatives from the interior of southern Taiwan. Saigō traveled by sedan chair across the peninsula. They stopped at Isa’s compound in Sabaree and then arrived for a large banquet in Tuilasok. His translator Mizuno Jun’s description documents indigenous-Japanese interpersonal relations at their dénouement. Mizuno recalled:
zh: 但尽管权力关系完全逆转，湿外交在恒春尚未消亡。8 月，猪朥束头人邀请西乡司令赴宴，与来自台湾南部内陆的代表同席。西乡乘轿穿越半岛。他们在射麻里伊萨的院落停留，然后抵达猪朥束参加一场大宴。其翻译水野遵（Mizuno Jun）的描述，记录了这段原住民与日本人往来的尾声。水野回忆：

en: A chief from a neighboring village with about ten men showed up, and a twilight feast ensued. A Chinese style wooden table was set up out of doors, and on top of it was pork gravy, deer, and pheasant with sweet potatoes, all cooked in a big pot and spread out on the table. The local sweet potato shōchū was ladled out of a big rice-cooking pot, and we were strongly urged to drink. While many of that day’s honored [Japanese] guests were renowned for their drinking abilities, they were no match for the amount of alcohol served at this banquet. This huge banquet appeared to consume a lifetime of wealth for the Indigenes to prepare, and this should have produced the best feelings of affection. However, the strong insistence that people continue to imbibe produced some uneasiness and perplexity...
zh: 邻村的一位酋长带着约十名男子出现，随即是一场黄昏宴。户外摆起一张中式木桌，桌上是猪肉羹、鹿肉、雉鸡配甘薯，全在大锅里煮好、摊摆桌上。当地的甘薯烧酎（shōchū）从一只大饭锅里舀出，我们被极力劝酒。尽管那天许多尊贵的[日本]客人以酒量闻名，却敌不过这场宴席上供应的酒量。这场大宴似乎耗尽了原住民一辈子的财富来备办，照理该使宾主情谊格外融洽。然而，极力坚持要人不断喝下去，却产生了一些不安与困惑……

en: Men then joined in a circle and began to dance and sing. Before leaving, Saigō attempted to do a little dancing himself, to the great delight of all present. The dancing was not unlike the obon dancing done in the Tokyo area. When the savages saw Saigō do their dance that evening, they were pleased beyond limit.
zh: 随后男子们围成一圈，开始歌舞。临别前，西乡自己也试着跳了一点舞，令在场所有人大为欢悦。这舞蹈与东京一带的盂兰盆舞（obon）不无相似。当番人那晚看到西乡跳他们的舞时，他们高兴得无以复加。

en: Unlike the exchanges of toasts, drinks, and presents at the May 16 feast attended by Isa in Wangsha, Saigō’s interactions with Tuilasok hosts in August were of no diplomatic import. By late July, all combatants had declared submission to Japan, and fighting had ceased. Monotony had set in among the soldiers.

Morale sank to new lows, and homesickness, boredom, and fatigue became widespread. Danny Orbach has unearthed a Japanese veteran’s memoir stating that young recruits, egged on by their officers, were shouting from the treetops to Saigō himself, “Let’s go home!,” when the commander made his rounds.
zh: 与伊萨在网纱出席的 5 月 16 日宴席上敬酒、饮酒与赠礼的交换不同，西乡 8 月与猪朥束主人的互动没有任何外交意涵。到 7 月底，所有交战方都已宣布归顺日本，战斗已停止。士兵中弥漫着单调乏味。
士气跌到新低，思乡、无聊与疲劳普遍蔓延。丹尼·奥巴赫（Danny Orbach）发掘出一份日本老兵回忆录，其中说：当司令巡视时，年轻新兵在军官怂恿下，从树梢上向西乡本人喊“我们回家吧！”。

en: In addition to flagging morale, malaria visited Japanese military camps. From late August through November, the outbreak—abetted by insufficient shelter, heavy rains, lack of medicine, food scarcity, and poor sanitation—took over 550 Japanese lives. Of the army’s 500-strong contingent of laborers, over 120 perished.

Reports in the Japanese press about illness at camps began to surface in late July; by October they had become routine. Journalistic reports were based on rumors and provided wildly fluctuating statistics. But all reports agreed that Taiwan’s climate was “miasmic” and unhealthy for Japanese people, an image of the island that persisted into the twentieth century. As Chen Xuan has pointed out, however, many Paiwan people also died from diseases spread by Japanese troops and workers, while Fujisaki Seinosuke, a colonial official, himself blamed lack of resources, planning, and medical knowledge for the high death toll. In other words, the ravages of illness, which were fiftyfold more lethal than combat in Langqiao, cannot be attributed to “tropical conditions” but rather to imperial overreach.
zh: 除了士气低落，疟疾也光顾了日军营地。从 8 月底到 11 月，这场疫情——因住所不足、暴雨、缺药、粮荒与卫生恶劣而助长——夺去 550 多名日本人的生命。在军队 500 人的劳工队中，120 多人丧生。

日本报章关于营地疾病的报道 7 月底开始出现；到 10 月已成常态。新闻报道基于传闻，提供剧烈波动的统计数字。但所有报道都一致认为台湾气候“瘴疠”、不利于日本人健康——这一岛屿形象一直延续到二十世纪。然而正如陈萱（Chen Xuan）所指出的，许多排湾人也死于日军与工人传播的疾病；而殖民官员藤崎清之助（Fujisaki Seinosuke）本人则把高死亡率归咎于资源、规划与医学知识的缺乏。换言之，疾病之肆虐——造成的死亡人数约是琅峤战斗阵亡人数的五十倍——不能归因于“热带条件”，而应归因于帝国的过度扩张。

en: Up until the time of the troops’ departure in December 1874, small groups of Japanese scouts made forays around the peninsula to learn about its social conditions and ethnic complexion. Numerous visits to headquarters near Siaoliao or the northern encampment in Fenggang for banquets or displays of military hardware were frequent. Importantly, no attempts were made to extract resources for commercial export from Langqiao or to police the day-to-day activities of the peninsula’s inhabitants. There were reports of insubordinate troops committing sexual harassment and petty crimes,
but Langqiao did not become the site of the ethnic cleansing threatened by Cassel aboard the Yūkōmaru on May 7, 1874.
zh: 直到 1874 年 12 月部队撤离，小股日本侦察兵在半岛各地四处活动，以了解其社会状况与族群面貌。为赴宴或观看军事装备展示而频繁造访射寮附近司令部或枫港北方营地的事屡见不鲜。重要的是，日方没有试图从琅峤攫取供商业出口的资源，也没有管制半岛居民的日常活动。有报道称违纪士兵犯下性骚扰与轻微罪行，
但琅峤并未成为卡塞尔 1874 年 5 月 7 日在有功丸上所威胁的种族清洗之地。

en: LANGQIAO AND THE SPECTER OF PUBLIC POWER
zh: 琅峤与公共权力的幽灵

en: After the December 1871 killing of the fifty-four Ryūkyūans, Qing district and provincial officials treated survivors with utmost care; at the next rung below, local literati and traders in southern Taiwan paid ransoms to save some lives and took it upon themselves to properly inter the remains of the dead. The slain Ryūkyūans were enshrined in mass graves that were subsequently feted at biannual rites to calm their spirits. In short, the murders of Ryūkyūans may have occurred beyond the formal limits of Qing jurisdiction, but they did not occur beyond the pale of civilization, as diplomats contended. Edwin Pak-wah Leung’s and Chou Wan-yao’s contentions that the dynastic system for handling shipwrecks worked without complaint are important, for they speak eloquently to the Qing court’s centripetal orientation, its narrow base of legitimacy, and its incompatibility with high-velocity capitalism.
zh: 1871 年 12 月五十四名琉球人被杀后，清朝府县与省级官员极其妥善地对待幸存者；再往下一层，台湾南部的地方士绅与商人支付赎金救下一些性命，并自行妥为安葬死者遗骸。被杀的琉球人被奉安于集体墓冢，随后每年两度祭祀以安其灵。简言之，琉球人之死或许发生在清朝正式管辖界限之外，却不像外交官所称的那样，发生在文明所及范围之外。梁伯华与周婉窈关于王朝处理沉船的制度运转无碍的论断很重要，因为它们有力地说明了清廷的向心取向、其狭窄的合法性基础、以及它与高速资本主义的不相容。

en: As Chou and Leung indicate, the complaint against the Qing for the deaths of the Miyakojimans was launched by Kagoshima activists, not the Ryūkyūan court. The activists who remonstrated for revenge, it should be noted, were not interested in extending the parameters of the treaty-port system. Their project was nonetheless intimately connected to the horizontal integration of the Meiji state. As power was centralized in Tokyo, and the “general good” redefined as the bottom line on a
instead of in terms of the exemplary moral conduct of officials,

the Satsuma activists—all samurai—advocated an attack on Taiwan to retain political relevance. While it is tempting to view them as members of an emergent national citizenry, aggrieved by the loss of newly imagined conationals from Miyakojima, the Satsuma men Kabayama, Saigō, and Ichiji were “domain nationalists,” in all likelihood.

Nonetheless, the fact that low-ranking men in a geographically remote prefecture were able to exert political pressure on the Tokyo government is significant. The post-Tokugawa state could not ignore bottom-up expansionist impulses, for it had to shore up its multiregional coalition via appeals to patriotism. If the Meiji oligarchs were to build a state strong enough to remain sovereign in an unforgiving social-Darwinist world order, they would require more than tacit acceptance of the central government’s primacy. Satsuma’s active commitment to the Meiji modernization project was crucial, so Ōkubo and the central leadership launched the expedition even against foreign objections and those of fiscal hawk and pragmatist Kido Takayoshi.
zh: 正如周婉窈与梁伯华所指出的，因宫古岛人死亡而向清廷提出的抗议，是由鹿儿岛活动人士发起的，而非琉球朝廷。应当注意，那些为复仇而抗议的活动人士，对扩展条约口岸体系的范围并无兴趣。然而他们的事业与明治国家的横向整合密切相关。随着权力集中于东京，“普遍善”被重新定义为国家财政账目上的收支结果，而非官员堪为表率的道德行为，
萨摩活动人士——全是武士——主张攻打台湾，以保住政治存在感。虽然人们容易把他们看作新兴国民公民的一员，为新近被视为日本同胞的宫古岛人遇害而悲愤，但桦山（Kabayama）、西乡与伊地知这些萨摩人，很可能都是“藩国民族主义者”。

尽管如此，一个地理偏远县份的低阶人士竟能对东京政府施加政治压力，这一事实意义重大。后德川国家无法忽视自下而上的扩张主义冲动，因为它必须借诉诸爱国主义来巩固其多地区联盟。倘若明治寡头要建设一个足够强大、能在无情的社会达尔文主义世界秩序中保持主权的国家，他们所需的就不止是对中央政府首要地位的默然接受。萨摩对明治现代化事业的积极投入至关重要，因此大久保与中央领导层即便面对外国反对、以及财政鹰派兼务实主义者木户孝允（Kido Takayoshi）的反对，仍发动了远征。

en: Qing support for limited forms of restorative justice and its tolerance of wrecking and unsanctioned violence on the periphery of its realm were relics of dynastic rule. The Qing did not rest its legitimacy on claims to embody, represent, nurture, and defend every one of its citizens, no matter where they were located. Its representatives even spoke of Paiwanese subjects as “beasts” and people of such low status that honorable governments would avoid any association with them. The Qing’s inward orientation, as so many have noted, was not conducive to building national strength, as was made painfully clear when Li Hongzhang was left to fight Japan’s imperial forces with his regional navy in 1894. Its anachronistic and low-velocity approach to diplomacy was best articulated in a formal response drafted by four members of the Zongli Yamen to pointed questions of Ōkubo Toshimichi at the September 14, 1874, negotiations for Japan’s withdrawal from Taiwan. The Qing ministers wrote:
zh: 清朝对有限形式的恢复性司法的支持，以及它对疆域边缘劫掠与未经批准暴力的容忍，都是王朝统治的遗存。清朝并不把合法性建立在声称体现、代表、培育并保护其每一个国民——无论他们身处何地——之上。其代表甚至把排湾人臣民说成“禽兽”、地位如此低下，以至体面的政府会避免与之有任何关联。正如许多人所指出的，清朝的内向取向不利于建设国家实力，这一点在 1894 年李鸿章被迫以其地方海军独自对抗日本帝国军队时痛苦地显现出来。它那种不合时宜、低速的外交方式，在 1874 年 9 月 14 日关于日本撤出台湾的谈判中，由总理衙门四位成员针对大久保利通尖锐问题起草的一份正式答复里，得到了最清楚的表述。清朝大臣写道：

en: In the aboriginal territory the Chinese Government let the indigenes keep their customs. Those who are able to pay tax pay it. Those who are talented enter nearby schools. We enforce generous and lenient policy to bring them up to a high level of edification. They are subject to the officials of the nearby districts. China stresses a gradual process of government, and has no intention to forcefully or too rapidly subjugate them. The natives of Hainan Island are treated the same. China has many regions of similar condition and every province has its own practices.
zh: 在原住民领土，中国政府任原住民保留其风俗。能纳税者纳税。有才者入附近学校。我们施行宽厚怀柔之政，以使其达到高度教化。他们归附近府县官员管辖。中国强调循序渐进的治理过程，无意以武力或过快地征服他们。海南岛土著亦受同样对待。中国有许多情况类似的地区，各省各有其做法。

en: In other words, the Qing realm included many areas deserving of special treatment, depending on local conditions and levels of economic development. In some areas, it was appropriate to govern very little, if at all. Consequently, at the margins of Qing rule in Langqiao, LeGendre and then Saigō were forced to rely upon a collection of headmen, brokers, and guides for hire to locate allies in their search for the remains of fellow countrymen or in pursuit of malefactors who had killed them.
zh: 换言之，清朝疆域包含许多值得特殊对待的地区，视地方条件与经济发展水平而定。在某些地区，极少治理乃至完全不治理才是恰当的。因此，在琅峤清朝统治的边缘，李仙得继而西乡，被迫依赖一批可雇用的头人、居间人与向导，以在寻找同胞遗骸或追索杀害他们的凶手时找到盟友。

en: Jürgen Osterhammel has argued that such “cross-border lobbies” of “pirates and partisans, semiprivate military operators and warlords” stitched the world of prenational empires together. It could not have been otherwise, given the limited state capacities of these far-flung multiethnic states, separated as they were by vast stretches of unadministered territory. As the international system consolidated itself around industrialized nation-states, however, these interstitial groups were displaced, ideally, with functionaries who answered to center-generated directives. Osterhammel terms this process “horizontal integration.”
zh: 于尔根·奥斯特哈默（Jürgen Osterhammel）曾论证，正是这类由“海盗与武装派别人员、半私营军事经营者与军阀”组成的“跨境游说集团”，把民族国家形成以前的帝国世界缝合在一起。鉴于这些幅员辽阔的多民族国家国家能力有限、彼此又被大片未治理领土隔开，情况不可能不是这样。然而，随着国际体系围绕工业化民族国家巩固自身，这些夹缝群体理想上被听命于中央指令的办事人员所取代。奥斯特哈默把这一过程称为“横向整合”。

en: Ōkubo rebutted the Zongli Yamen’s position paper, quoted above, with point-by-point objections that called for the horizontal integration of Langqiao with the Qing empire.Ōkubo asserted that “a nation is responsible for the control of crimes, and when crimes are not punished, then there is no law, therefore no national jurisdiction.” In addition, he stated that “tax is a contract agreed to between the ruler and the ruled, and must be applied uniformly upon every citizen and subject within the domain. Making any exception would reduce the payee into tributary status and as not owing allegiance to the ruler.” To his list of criteria for demonstrating sovereignty,Ōkubo added compulsory education. He charged that “the education of only a very small minority of a tribe could not be regarded as ‘civilizing’ the whole aboriginal population.”

Thus,Ōkubo advocated universal education for rural Taiwan at a time when the Japanese system itself only operated in fits and starts. Kido Takayoshi, Japan’s minister of education in 1874, argued against Ōkubo’s plan for outfitting an expedition to Taiwan for this very reason: Japan’s own public-school system was woefully underfunded, and the nation could not afford foreign adventures until it put its own house in order.
zh: 大久保逐条反驳上文所引总理衙门的立场文件，提出反对意见，要求把琅峤横向整合到清帝国的行政体系中。大久保断言“一国负责管控犯罪，若犯罪不受惩罚，便无法律，因而无国家管辖权”。此外，他声称“税收是统治者与被统治者之间议定的契约，必须统一施于领地内每一个公民与臣民。任何例外都会把纳税者降为朝贡地位、视为不效忠于统治者”。在他列举的展示主权的标准中，大久保又加上义务教育。他指责“一个社中仅极少数人受教育，不能视为‘教化’全体原住民人口”。
于是，大久保在日本自身制度尚且时断时续运作之时，却主张在台湾乡村普及教育。1874 年日本教育大臣木户孝允正是出于这个理由反对大久保为远征台湾筹措军费、装备部队的计划：日本自身的公立学校制度经费严重不足，国家在理顺自家事务之前无力承担海外冒险。

en: Ōkubo railed against Qing officials who “preside remotely and abandon the indigenes to their criminal undertakings.” Such leniency, he urged, was “tantamount to not having any jurisdiction.” Lastly,Ōkubo attacked Qing policies of attraction and voluntary submission, stating that “two hundred years of gradualism was a bit too slow.”

Some thirty years later, Japanese parliamentarian Takekoshi Yosaburō would make an identical argument to his own central government: TGG policies of voluntary submission through benevolence were too gradual, leaving the empire vulnerable at its extremities, he argued.
zh: 大久保痛斥那些“遥为主宰、却听任原住民从事犯罪勾当”的清朝官员。他力陈，这种宽纵“无异于没有任何管辖权”。最后，大久保抨击清朝的招抚与自愿归顺政策，声称“两百年的渐进主义有点太慢了”。
约三十年后，日本国会议员竹越与三郎将向本国中央政府提出一模一样的论点：他辩称，总督府以怀柔促自愿归顺的政策太过渐进，使帝国在边陲脆弱可欺。

en: The endless rounds of wet diplomacy that characterized political transactions in Langqiao before 1874 were symptomatic of “

children: the infra-power of acquired and tolerated illegalities

en: ” that provoked LeGendre and formed the basis of Ōkubo’s case against the Qing. At the same time, as Carol Gluck, Takashi Fujitani, Robert Eskildsen, Marlene Mayo, Danny Orbach, and Hyman Kublin have demonstrated amply, the Japan of 1874 had barely made a beginning on stamping out tolerated illegalities, regionalism, dynastic myopia, and threats to central authority within its own borders. It is thus unsurprising that many of Ōkubo’s charges against the Qing were based on international law as interpreted by Gustave Boissonade, who accompanied Ōkubo to Beijing on September 10, 1874, as his advisor.
zh: 1874 年之前琅峤政治交涉中一轮接一轮的湿外交，正是“既得且被容忍的非法性”之“底层权力”（infra-power）的症候——它激怒了李仙得，并构成大久保指控清朝的依据。与此同时，正如卡罗尔·格卢克（Carol Gluck）、藤谷隆、罗伯特·埃斯基尔森（Robert Eskildsen）、马琳·梅奥（Marlene Mayo）、丹尼·奥巴赫与海曼·库布林（Hyman Kublin）已充分证明的，1874 年的日本在铲除自身境内被容忍的非法性、地方主义、王朝短视与对中央权威的威胁方面，才刚刚起步。因此不足为奇的是，大久保对清朝的许多指控，依据的是古斯塔夫·布瓦索纳德（Gustave Boissonade）所阐释的国际法——后者于 1874 年 9 月 10 日作为顾问随大久保赴北京。

en: The French legal scholar also coached Itō Hirobumi and Inoue Kaoru on the fine points of international law as they extended the treaty-port system to Korea by military force and diplomatic cunning in the mid-1870s. Therefore, when Ōkubo alluded to constructions of sovereignty in Beijing that resembled the instantiation of public power, he referenced the abstract writings of jurists such as Emer de Vattel, Friedrich Martens, and Johann Kaspar Bluntschli, and not conditions in Japan.Ōkubo was not suggesting that the Qing behave more like the Meiji government, but he was rearticulating his own fledgling government’s centralizing aspirations in a different setting.
The Qing negotiators simply refused to play by these new rules (the Koreans would have less success rebuffing such arguments in 1876), and the Japanese ended up withdrawing from Taiwan that December.
zh: 这位法国法学家还在 1870 年代中期伊藤博文与井上馨（Inoue Kaoru）以武力与外交手腕把条约口岸体系扩展到朝鲜时，就国际法的细节指点过他们。因此，大久保在北京提出的主权构想，类似于建立福柯所谓公共权力的方案。阐述这些构想时，他参照的是瓦特尔（Emer de Vattel）、马滕斯（Friedrich Martens）与布伦奇利（Johann Kaspar Bluntschli）等法学家的抽象著作，而非日本的实况。大久保并非建议清朝行事更像明治政府，而是在另一种场景里重新表述他自己新生政府的中央集权抱负。
清朝谈判代表干脆拒绝按这些新规则行事（朝鲜人在 1876 年驳回此类论点时就没那么成功了），日本人最终在那年 12 月撤出台湾。

en: LeGendre himself did not envision the creation of a disciplinary society or the establishment of public power to end Langqiao’s threats to shipping. While LeGendre was still getting his feet wet in treaty-port diplomacy in the late 1860s, his vision for southern Taiwan was indigenous autonomy under Qing suzerainty. Like Native Americans or New Zealand’s Maori peoples, Taiwan’s Paiwans could be left to manage their own affairs but would be denied the ability to enter into agreements with foreign powers. The Qing would be responsible for “restraining them” and indemnifying injured foreigners. If the Qing could not accomplish these tasks, it would forfeit the territory.

A few years later, in mid-1874, after LeGendre had been removed from Taiwan for a couple of years, his view hardened. His new plan B for treaty-port era reterritorialization was extermination. If they could not be pacified, foot draggers who impeded access to sea-lanes were expendable. As an alternative to extermination, LeGendre proposed making Langqiao into a Japanese penal colony, developing it along Australian lines.

In all of these scenarios, there was no provision for dispersing power throughout a population to make it self-actuating, as was the goal of the Meiji oligarchs vis-à-vis Japan’s own citizens. At the same time, the Qing policy of gradualism, or letting border peoples maintain separate customs until they “came around,” was also ruled out.
zh: 李仙得本人并未设想创建一个规训社会、或确立公共权力以终结琅峤对航运的威胁。1860 年代末李仙得还在条约口岸外交中初试身手时，他对台湾南部的愿景是在清朝宗主权下的原住民自治。如同美洲原住民或新西兰的毛利人，台湾的排湾人可以获准管理自己的事务，但会被剥夺与外国列强缔约的能力。清朝将负责“约束他们”并赔偿受害外国人。倘若清朝无法完成这些任务，就会丧失该领土。
几年后，1874 年年中，在李仙得离开台湾约两年之后，他的观点强硬起来。他为条约口岸时代再领土化提出的新 B 计划是灭绝。倘若无法绥靖，那些迟迟不肯让步、妨碍商船使用航道的人是可以牺牲的。作为灭绝的替代，李仙得提议把琅峤变成日本的流放殖民地，沿澳大利亚的模式开发。
在所有这些设想中，都没有把权力分散到整个人口、使之自我驱动的安排——而那正是明治寡头针对日本本国公民的目标。与此同时，清朝的渐进主义政策，即让边境民族保留各自风俗直到他们“回心转意”，也被排除在外。

en: This newly emerging liminal space between the old Qing posture of letting distant tribes in Hainan or Langqiao maintain their own customs until they came into the fold of “civilization” and the concurrent Meiji policy of horizontal integration at all costs for Honshū, Kyūshū, and Shikoku created the ground for the transformation of southern Taiwan’s natives into indigenous peoples.
zh: 这个新出现的阈限空间——介于清朝让海南或琅峤偏远各社保留自身风俗、直到其纳入“文明”怀抱的旧姿态，与明治同时期对本州、九州、四国不惜一切代价推行横向整合的政策之间——为把台湾南部土著转变为原住民族创造了基础。

en: THE QING-JAPANESE INTERREGNUM AND UENO SEN’ICHI
zh: 清日过渡期与上野专一

en: In 1890, Foreign Minister Aoki Shūzō ordered Ueno Sen’ichi to Taiwan to investigate its commercial potential. In late December, Ueno set sail for Danshui (a port near Taipei).

In early 1891, Ueno departed Danshui “to meet a chief (doshū)” as part of his mission. Ueno described his destination as “the Tokoham region, which occupies a majority of the savage [territory] (seiban chū mottomo daibubun o shimuru Tokohamu chihō

Ueno used the term “Tokoham” (Dakekan) loosely; the route he described brought him not there but rather to Atayal peoples then known as the eight villages of Marai (near today’s Wulai). Ueno departed Taipei on a sedan chair, crossed a broad plain to Xindian, and from there traversed several creeks to the villages known as the Quchi tribes (Wulai, Raho, Raga, and Rimogan—see
zh: 1890 年，外务大臣青木周藏（Aoki Shūzō）命上野专一（Ueno Sen'ichi）赴台调查其商业潜力。12 月底，上野启航赴淡水（台北附近一港）。
1891 年初，上野离开淡水，“去会见一位酋长（doshū）”，作为其使命的一部分。上野把他的目的地描述为“大嵙崁地区，占据生番[领土]的绝大部分”（seiban chū mottomo daibubun o shimuru Tokohamu chihō ni shite）。
上野对“大嵙崁”（Tokoham，Dakekan）一词的使用很宽泛；他描述的路线并未把他带到那里，而是带到当时被称为马来（Marai）八社的泰雅人（近今乌来）。上野乘轿离开台北，穿过一片宽阔平原到新店，再从那里涉过几条溪流，到被称为屈尺群（乌来、拉号、拉卡、利莫干——见
）的村落。

en: MAP 6. Dakekan, Jiaobanshan, Quchi, Wulai, and Rimogan, ca. 1910. The lighter area of the map represents the Aborigine Territory.
zh: 地图 6. 大嵙崁、角板山、屈尺、乌来与利莫干，约 1910 年。地图较浅区域代表蕃地。
parallelFigureCaption: MAP 6. Dakekan, Jiaobanshan, Quchi, Wulai, and Rimogan, ca. 1910. The lighter area of the map represents the Aborigine Territory.
地图 6. 大嵙崁、角板山、屈尺、乌来与利莫干，约 1910 年。地图较浅区域代表蕃地。

en: By 1891 the Quchi area was a well-established trading junction for Atayal peoples to barter furs, bones, organs, and medicinal plants for cloth, iron, gunpowder, and ornaments with Chinese traders. It can be considered the functional equivalent of Poliac in Hengchun. Quchi analogously connected Xindian, and by extension Taipei/Danshui, to the mountain settlements and forests south along the Nanshi River (then known as the Xindian River). As early as 1871, European and American writers knew to travel there to pick up guides and information on their way to the interior. On the map Charles LeGendre published that year (which made its way into Japanese military archives along with Ueno’s handwritten report), the river junction abutting “Koo-cheu” (Quchi) is tagged “Chiankoey the name of all the places where exchanges between the Chinese & Aborigines take place.” According to Consul LeGendre, the Border Tower, just downriver, was a no-man’s-land between a southward-moving Han frontier and the indigenous villages tucked in the mountains.

As was the case when LeGendre advanced south past Fangliao in Langqiao, traders moving south past Quchi were dependent upon such intermediaries as they could find and went past the “savage border” at their own peril.
zh: 到 1891 年，屈尺地区已是泰雅人与华人商人以兽皮、骨、内脏与药用植物交换布匹、铁、火药与饰物的成熟贸易枢纽。它可被视为恒春保力的功能对等物。屈尺同样把新店、进而把台北/淡水，与沿南势溪（当时称新店溪）向南的山地聚落与森林连接起来。早在 1871 年，欧美作者就知道在前往内陆途中到那里雇向导、打听消息。在李仙得那年出版的地图上（该图与上野的手写报告一起流入日本军事档案），毗邻屈尺（Koo-cheu）的河流交汇处标着“Chiankoey，凡是华人与原住民交换货物的地方都称此名”。据李仙得领事说，下游不远处的界楼（Border Tower），是南移的汉人边疆与藏身山中的原住民村落之间的一片无人地带。
正如李仙得在琅峤向南越过枋寮时的情形，向南越过屈尺的商人，依赖他们能找到的这类居间人，越过“生番界”须自担风险。

en: In 1882 assistant Imperial Maritime Customs officer William Hancock also stopped in “Kochu” (Quchi) en route from Xindian. The year Hancock wrote, oolong tea exports from Taiwan were increasing annually, a trend that may have contributed to some of the frontier chaos and violence he witnessed. Hancock remarked on the presence of trading posts and Atayal-Chinese interpreters. According to Hancock, Chinese settlers in Quchi were still in danger of head-hunting raids, despite their inroads as settlers and tea cultivators. When he finally obtained passage to an Atayal village, he noted the presence of many severed Chinese heads. Since these borderland “illegalities,” to use Foucault’s terms, did not directly affect Westerners, Hancock did not remonstrate with the Qing to fix the problem, in contrast to the activist consul LeGendre just a decade earlier.
zh: 1882 年，海关助理关员威廉·汉考克（William Hancock）从新店出发途中，也在屈尺（Kochu）停留。汉考克写作那年，台湾乌龙茶出口逐年增长，这一趋势或许助长了他所目睹的某些边疆混乱与暴力。汉考克谈到贸易站与泰雅—华人通译的存在。据汉考克说，屈尺的华人定居者尽管作为定居者与茶农已有所推进，仍面临猎首袭击的危险。当他终于获准进入一个泰雅村落时，他注意到许多被割下的华人头颅。由于这些边疆“非法性”（用福柯的术语）并不直接影响西方人，汉考克没有像十年前那位积极干预的领事李仙得那样，向清朝抗议要求解决问题。

en: Hancock hired the services of a bicultural interpreter/tracker to continue inland. He stopped at a trading post to purchase samshu liquor for distribution. His guide, who quickly donned Atayal garb, weapons, and adornment before alighting, brought a small group from the interior, who were then duly plied with liquor. Convinced that Hancock was generous, they consented to a visit to an area that appears to have been close to Rimogan, upstream from Wulai. There, in a scene reminiscent of Saigō’s big August 1874 feast in Tuilasok, Hancock danced in a circle with Atayal women, ate roast pork, and poured down cups of alcohol with his hosts. He was led back to Quchi by a different path than the one by which he had arrived, and he noted in his consular report that the village was well hidden from outsiders.
zh: 汉考克雇了一名熟悉两种文化的通事兼向导，继续深入内陆。他在一个贸易站停下，购买烧酒（samshu）以备分发。他的向导在下轿前迅速换上泰雅式衣服和饰物，带上武器，带来一小群来自内陆的人，随即被殷勤劝酒。他们确信汉考克慷慨，便同意他造访一个似乎靠近利莫干、在乌来上游的地区。在那里，一幕令人想起西乡 1874 年 8 月在猪朥束的大宴：汉考克与泰雅妇女围圈起舞，吃烤猪肉，与主人一杯杯灌酒。他由一条不同于来时的路径被带回屈尺，并在领事报告中指出，该村对外人隐蔽得很好。

en: Following in Hancock’s tracks a decade later, Ueno finally found a guide “who could speak the Aborigine language a little.”

Ueno ordered him to arrange a parley with the paramount chief (shūchō no gotoki tōmoku). Taking his leave, Ueno’s interpreter removed his “Chinese-style” clothing, pinned up his queue, donned a tunic, waist dagger, and Atayal-style cap, and set off to find the paramount chief.

After a long wait, the interpreter returned with six Atayal people. The guests were a “paramount chief” named Watan Yū, his wife and daughter, and three retainers. After Ueno distributed the expected presents, Watan Yū produced sweet potatoes and a bundle of rice stalks from a “head carrying bag.” After this exchange of gifts, the chief, along with the other five, stood up at once and took turns striking Ueno in the chest with their right arms. Ueno asked the Chinese-language interpreter (tsūben) what this meant, and the interpreter replied that it was a sign of affection and happiness. It literally meant that the indigenes considered Ueno as kin, as a member of the “tribe/race” (dōjinshu). Ueno then reciprocated by striking Watan Yū’s chest with his right hand.
zh: 十年后沿着汉考克的足迹，上野终于找到一名“能讲一点原住民语言”的向导。
上野命他安排与最高酋长（shūchō no gotoki tōmoku）的会谈。上野的通译告辞后，脱下“中式”服装，挽起辫子，穿上短衣，佩上腰刀，戴上泰雅式帽子，出发去找最高酋长。

久等之后，通译带回六名泰雅人。客人是一位名叫瓦坦·尤（Watan Yū）的“最高酋长”、其妻与女，以及三名扈从。上野分发预期的礼物后，瓦坦·尤从一只“头顶搬运袋”里取出甘薯与一捆稻秆。这番赠礼交换之后，酋长与其他五人立刻站起，轮流用右臂击打上野的胸口。上野问汉语通辩（tsūben）这是什么意思，通译答道这是亲爱与喜悦的表示。其字面意思是原住民把上野视为亲人、视为“同人种”（dōjinshu）的一员。上野随即以右手击打瓦坦·尤的胸口作为回报。

en: As the festivities continued, Ueno showed Watan a bottle of sweet potato shōchū purchased at a trading post along the way. As Ueno was about to open it, Watan asked if he could take the bottle back to his own village for later consumption. Ueno convinced him that both sides should consume it together, on the spot, in the spirit of fraternity. Quite joyfully, according to Ueno, the imported liquor was consumed. Ueno’s attention to detail reveals his belief that every gesture and gift was freighted with meaning. Ueno noted that, as in a Japanese tea ceremony, after taking a drink, each person would wipe the rim of the bowl to show purity of intention before passing the bowl to the next person.
zh: 随着欢庆继续，上野给瓦坦看一瓶沿途在贸易站买的甘薯烧酎。上野正要开瓶，瓦坦问他能否把瓶子带回自己村子里日后再喝。上野说服他，本着兄弟情谊，双方应当场一起喝掉。据上野说，这瓶外来酒被相当欢快地喝光了。上野对细节的留意，透露出他相信每个姿态与礼物都满载意义。上野注意到，如同日本茶道，每人喝一口后，会擦拭碗沿以示心意纯净，再把碗传给下一人。

en: Upon his return to Tokyo, Ueno published a detailed record of his observations, along with information gathered from Western missionaries and Qing sources he was privy to as a Japanese consul. These appeared in the February 1892 issue of the
. Ueno also hit the lecture circuit to alert Japanese entrepreneurs about business opportunities in Taiwan and on the continent.

Ueno then addressed the Tokyo Geographical Society’s March 22, 1895, meeting. Brandishing the earrings and cape he had received from Watan Yū and his wife, Ueno reported that the unconquered “savages” regarded the Chinese as enemies. Like Hancock before him, he portrayed Atayal people as innocents, who stood little chance against their cunning civilized neighbors, the Chinese.
zh: 回到东京后，上野发表了一份详细的观察记录，附上他从西方传教士以及作为日本领事得以接触的清朝来源搜集的信息。这些刊于《东京地学协会杂志》1892 年 2 月号。上野还巡回演讲，向日本企业家提示台湾与大陆的商业机会。
上野随后在东京地学协会 1895 年 3 月 22 日的会上发言。他举起从瓦坦·尤及其妻那里收到的耳环和披肩，报告说未被征服的“番人”把华人视为敌人。与之前的汉考克一样，他把泰雅人描绘成天真无邪者，在其狡黠的文明邻居华人面前几乎没有胜算。
body.review: 原书正文作1895年3月22日，原注121所列《读卖新闻》的日期为1892年3月25日。正文和原注分别保留原载日期。

en: During his tenure as consul at Wonsan, Korea, Ueno recopied and edited his 1891 travel notes and submitted a handwritten draft to the Imperial Army’s General Staff, signing the updated report October 25, 1894.
Three months later, the General Staff published Ueno’s report under the title “A Gazetteer of Taiwan.”

All of these iterations institutionalized the notion that Taiwan’s population was divided between victimized indigenes and Han aggressors and that the former constituted a population of natural allies who could be won over with gifts of cloth, jars of liquor, and a willingness to participate in wet diplomatic transactions.
zh: 在担任朝鲜元山领事期间，上野重新誊抄并编辑了他 1891 年的旅行笔记，向陆军参谋本部提交一份手写稿，并于 1894 年 10 月 25 日在这份更新报告上署名。
三个月后，参谋本部以《台湾志》为题出版了上野的报告。
所有这些版本都把一种观念制度化：台湾人口分为受害的原住民与汉人侵略者，而前者构成一个天然盟友群体，可以用布匹、一坛坛酒、以及参与湿外交交易的意愿来争取。

en: Because Saigō and Ueno were short-timers, their interactions with indigenes were perforce of a different order than those of Qing officials or Han settlers. Thus their codified and serially reproduced assurances that relations of hostility or intimacy were attributable to the respective characters of Chinese, Taiwan Indigenous Peoples, and Japanese were based on false premises. These Japanese visitors, backed by the armed might of an occupational force or the implicit threat of Qing armies, were not charged with extracting raw materials from Taiwan’s interior, nor did they take responsibility for maintaining the peace between rival indigenous groups or between lowlanders and highlanders. Their faith in the efficacy of wet diplomacy would be severely tested when the Japanese government took over from the Qing and found itself torn between the notions of public power as expressed by Ōkubo Toshimichi in Beijing and the practical necessity of ruling within the constraints of finite resources. They would begin, as it turned out, by letting border peoples keep their own customs and by exercising leniency.
zh: 由于西乡与上野都是短期过客，他们与原住民的互动，必然与清朝官员或汉人定居者的互动属于不同性质。因此，他们反复写入公开记述、流传开来的说法——即敌对或亲密关系可归因于华人、台湾原住民与日本人各自的性格——建立在错误前提之上。这些日本访客，背后有占领军的武装力量或清军的隐含威胁撑腰，既不负责从台湾内陆攫取原料，也不负责维持敌对原住民群体之间、或低地人与高地人之间的和平。当日本政府从清朝手中接管、并发现自己在“大久保利通在北京所表述的公共权力观念”与“在有限资源约束下统治的实际必要”之间左右为难时，他们对湿外交效力的信念将受到严峻考验。结果，他们一开始竟会让边境民族保留自己的风俗、施行宽纵。

en: FEASTING, GIFTING, AND DRINKING: ATAYAL-JAPANESE DIPLOMACY IN THE COLONIAL ERA
zh: 宴饮、馈赠与共饮：殖民时代的泰雅—日本外交

en: On August 2, 1895, Admiral Kabayama Sukenori signed papers transferring the sovereignty of Taiwan to Japan aboard a ship in Jilong Harbor. Within a month, forty-six men under a garrison commander named Watanabe trekked southeast toward the mountains to initiate official relations with Atayal representatives. He chose the junction town of Dakekan, a gateway to the mountain trade. After marching for a couple of miles, Watanabe waited for a delegation of Atayals. Emissaries numbering seven, two of them women, showed up. The soldiers distributed gifts of liquor, tobacco, silver coins, and tinned mackerel to the seven red-caped representatives.
zh: 1895 年 8 月 2 日，桦山资纪（Kabayama Sukenori）海军大将在基隆港的一艘船上签署台湾主权移交日本的文件。不到一个月，一名叫渡边（Watanabe）的驻军指挥官率四十六人向东南跋涉入山，以开启与泰雅代表的官方关系。他选择了山地贸易的门户——大嵙崁这个枢纽镇。行军约两英里后，渡边等候一个泰雅代表团。七名使者出现，其中两名是妇女。士兵们向这七名披红披肩的代表分发酒、烟草、银币与罐装鲭鱼等礼物。
body.review: 原书此处作1895年8月2日。樺山资纪与李经方签署的《台湾受渡》公文实际署1895年6月2日，见日本亚洲历史资料中心所藏 B13090895300。原书日期照录。

en: The expected drinking soon ensued. As two o’clock rolled around, the chief reminded Watanabe that a five-mile journey back into the mountains awaited. He promised to meet the Japanese later at the same spot.

On September 4, a mission headed by section chief of industrial development (shokusan-buchō) Hashiguchi Bunzō (future Taipei governor) set out from Taipei to follow up. After negotiating the actual spot and timing over days of weather delays and messages shuttled through an interpreter, the summit commenced on September 8.
zh: 预期的饮酒随即开始。约两点钟时，酋长提醒渡边，回山还有五英里路程等着。他答应稍后在同一地点与日本人会面。
9 月 4 日，一个由殖产部长（shokusan-buchō）桥口文藏（Hashiguchi Bunzō，后来出任台北知事）率领的使团从台北出发跟进。在因天气延误数日、并通过一名通译来回传话商定了实际地点与时间后，峰会于 9 月 8 日开始。

en: The Japanese lined up the twenty-two Dakekan-area residents on a field. Then Taipei governor Tanaka Tsunatoku read a statement: “You have come from afar, down from the mountains, bringing even your women and children. We are overjoyed to meet with you here. We set out for Dakekan yesterday to meet with you because we wanted to establish good relations and to apprise you of matters of official import. To see you here in good health bearing a compliant (
) attitude makes all of us very happy.”
zh: 日本人把二十二名大嵙崁地区居民在一片场地上列队。随后台北知事田中纲常（Tanaka Tsunatoku）宣读一份声明：“你们远道而来，从山上下来，连妇女儿童都带来了。我们在此与你们会面，欣喜万分。我们昨天出发来大嵙崁与你们会面，是因为想建立良好关系，并把官方要事告知你们。看到你们在此健康安好、带着温顺（onjun）的态度，我们大家都非常高兴。”

en: These introductory remarks, made to “test the attitude of the indigenes,” were followed by a toast, and the liquor was produced. Like Watanabe and Ueno before them, Hashiguchi and Tanaka found themselves at close quarters with their Atayal counterparts. In Hashiguchi’s case, the intimacy produced mild discomfort tinged with amusement. Hashiguchi explained at a lecture before the Tokyo Geographical Society: “As everyone knows, when Germans make agreements, they face each other, put their hands like this, (Hashiguchi motions in imitation) and drink beer together. The indigenes are a little different. Touching their mouths together, they both drain the same cup. I don’t mean to boast, but when I said ‘how about some sake,’ immediately one came at me with his mouth and I joined him... If one cannot bear to do such things, one cannot associate or communicate with the indigenes at all.”
zh: 这些为“试探原住民态度”而作的开场白之后，是一次敬酒，酒被拿了出来。与之前的渡边和上野一样，桥口与田中发现自己与前来会谈的泰雅人近身相对。就桥口而言，这种亲密产生了略感不自在，又觉得有些好笑。桥口在东京地学协会的一次演讲中解释：“众所周知，德国人订约时，彼此面对面，把手这样放（桥口模仿示意），一起喝啤酒。原住民有点不同。他们嘴碰嘴，两人喝干同一杯。我不是自夸，但当我一说‘来点清酒如何’，立刻就有一个人把嘴凑向我，我便与他合口……倘若一个人受不了做这种事，就根本无法与原住民交往或沟通。”

en: This was not the first time a high-ranking Japanese official joined mouths with an Atayal man. In September 1873, Mizuno Jun—then a government language scholar and interpreter—accompanied future governor-general of Taiwan Kabayama Sukenori to Suao Bay (near Yilan) on reconnaissance. Upon meeting a delegation in the Nan’ao area, Kabayama’s group distributed spirits manufactured in Fujian in exchange for servings of the local alcoholic beverage, probably a fermented millet wine. Farther along, at a subsequent feast, shōchū was ladled out to the thirsty and tired Japanese travelers. The headman grabbed Kabayama’s colleague Naritomi Seifū by the shoulder and forced their mouths together so they could down the liquor out of the same cup.
zh: 这不是日本高官第一次与泰雅男子合口。1873 年 9 月，水野遵——当时任职于政府，研习语言并担任通事——随未来的台湾总督桦山资纪赴苏澳湾（近宜兰）侦察。在南澳地区遇到一个代表团时，桦山一行分发福建制造的烈酒，换取几杯当地的酒，大概是发酵的小米酒。再往前，在随后的一次宴席上，烧酎被舀给又渴又累的日本旅人。头人抓住桦山的同僚成富清风（Naritomi Seifū）的肩膀，强迫他们嘴对嘴，好让他们从同一杯里喝下酒。

en: Returning to the September 1895 mission: after the initial toasts, Tanaka announced to the gathered men and women that the relationship between Japan and the Dakekan peoples would conform to the principles of nondiscrimination:
zh: 回到 1895 年 9 月的使团：初次敬酒之后，田中向聚集的男女宣布，日本与大嵙崁各族的关系将遵循无差别原则：

en: Here we must communicate to you a matter of utmost importance. You should listen silently and with full attention. This island of Taiwan, the parts inhabited by you [Indigenes] and by the Chinese (

), has wholly become a possession of Great Japan, under the rule of our Great Emperor. Henceforth, the garrison troops and officials posted here will administer both Taipei and Dakekan, and govern everyone uniformly (

children: mina ichiritsu ni waga nihonkan kore o kanri suru

en: ). The previous Chinese administrators have fled and left, so from this day forward, you are all, just like us, the children of the Emperor, you are our brothers. Having listened well to our office’s order, you will exert yourself to be loyal subjects of the Emperor and the Great Empire of Japan.
zh: 在此我们必须告知你们一件至关重要之事。你们应静听、全神贯注。台湾这个岛，你们[原住民]与华人（shinajin，支那人）居住的部分，已完全成为大日本的领土，归我们大天皇统治。从此，派驻此地的驻军与官员将管理台北与大嵙崁两地，一律治理所有人（mina ichiritsu ni waga nihonkan kore o kanri suru）。先前的华人管理者已逃离，因此从今天起，你们全都和我们一样，是天皇的子民，是我们的兄弟。既已听清本官署的命令，你们就要努力做天皇与大日本帝国的忠良臣民。

en: Tanaka’s speech was communicated through Atayal interpreters and received in the context of joined-mouth drinking rituals and presentations of gifts. At the same time, it was filled with “dry” sobriquets written in lofty and abstract phrases that disavowed special treatment or a budding personal relationship. Japanese officials would propagate these mixed messages throughout the interior in subsequent “first-contact” events.
zh: 田中的讲话通过泰雅通译传达，是在合口饮酒仪式与赠礼的语境中被接受的。与此同时，它又充满用高调而抽象的语言表达的“干”（dry）式称谓，排除了特殊待遇或刚刚建立的私人情谊。日本官员将在随后的“初次接触”事件中，把这些混杂的信息传播到整个内陆。

en: Despite the layers of linguistic confusion, Hashiguchi’s and Tanaka’s adherence to Ueno’s notes on hospitality and their willingness to participate in wet diplomacy achieved their short-term goal. Twelve of the original twenty-two Atayal were persuaded to visit the Dakekan garrison. Seven of these, including the Jiaobanshan headman Watan Nui (who had dealt with Watanabe on August 29), returned to Jiaobanshan soon thereafter (see

). They were issued a beef cow and a written note signed by Hashiguchi and Tanaka as a receipt to commemorate Japan’s expression of sincerity and its announcement that Taiwan was now “imperial territory.” It is not clear from the documentation whether Watan Nui, like Toketok and his brother in 1867, requested this written record or if the Japanese team felt it served a purpose.
zh: 尽管有层层语言混乱，桥口与田中对上野待客笔记的遵循、以及他们参与湿外交的意愿，达成了短期目标。最初二十二名泰雅人中的十二名被说服造访大嵙崁驻军。其中七名——包括角板山头人瓦坦·努伊（Watan Nui，他曾于 8 月 29 日与渡边打交道）——不久后返回角板山（见
）。他们获发一头肉牛与一张由桥口和田中署名的字条作为凭据，记下日方表明诚意和宣布台湾已是“帝国领土”一事。从文档中不清楚，瓦坦·努伊是否像 1867 年的卓杞笃及其兄弟那样要求这份书面记录，还是日本团队觉得它有用。

en: FIGURE 11. Drawing of Watan Nawi’s wife, Lemoi Maton, present at the meeting during Watanabe’s expedition to Dakekan. In the head-hunting bag, note the alcohol bottle and can, which were gifts brought back from the meeting with representatives of the colonial government near or in Dakekan (Daxi).
11, no. 115 (1895): back cover.
zh: 图 11. 瓦坦·纳维（Watan Nawi）之妻莱莫伊·马顿（Lemoi Maton）的画像，她出席了渡边远征大嵙崁期间的会面。注意猎首袋中的酒瓶与罐子，那是从大嵙崁（大溪）附近或当地与殖民政府代表会面后带回的礼物。Tokyo jinruigakkai zasshi 11, no. 115 (1895): back cover.
parallelFigureCaption: FIGURE 11. Drawing of Watan Nawi’s wife, Lemoi Maton, present at the meeting during Watanabe’s expedition to Dakekan. In the head-hunting bag, note the alcohol bottle and can, which were gifts brought back from the meeting with representatives of the colonial government near or in Dakekan (Daxi).
11, no. 115 (1895): back cover.
图 11. 瓦坦·纳维（Watan Nawi）之妻莱莫伊·马顿（Lemoi Maton）的画像，她出席了渡边远征大嵙崁期间的会面。注意猎首袋中的酒瓶与罐子，那是从大嵙崁（大溪）附近或当地与殖民政府代表会面后带回的礼物。Tokyo jinruigakkai zasshi 11, no. 115 (1895): back cover.

en: The remaining five Atayal emissaries were lured to Taipei with the promise of additional wool blankets. Accompanied by their Atayal interpreter, Pu Chin, they went to the capital for meetings with Governor-General Kabayama, presentations of gifts, and photo sessions. The Dakekan contingent of six (including Pu Chin) was welcomed by a brass band and feted at an elaborate banquet with Kabayama himself. They also visited a military police station, where they taunted a Han Taiwanese prisoner with threats to cut off his head and bring it home as a souvenir. These events generated sufficient excitement to be chronicled in several magazines and newspapers.
The Shanghai illustrated
even published an engraving of the Japanese band serenading the tattooed Atayal men, women, and children as they dined in an ornate Chinese banquet hall.
zh: 剩下五名泰雅使者被以额外毛毯的许诺诱到台北。在他们的泰雅通译蒲靖（Pu Chin）陪同下，他们前往首府，与总督桦山会面、接受赠礼并拍照。大嵙崁一行六人（含蒲靖）受到铜管乐队欢迎，并与桦山本人一起出席精心安排的宴席。他们还参观了一个宪兵站，在那里威胁要砍下一名台湾汉族囚犯的头带回家当纪念品，以此嘲弄他。这些事件激起足够大的轰动，被数家杂志与报纸记载。
上海的《点石斋画报》甚至刊出一幅版画，描绘日本乐队为文身的泰雅男女儿童奏乐助兴，而他们正在一间华丽的中式宴会厅里用餐。

en: On September 12, the five emissaries were sent back to Dakekan on a boat, where they continued to drink, sing, and nap.

Thus the government-general established its initial method of rule in the uplands, whereby Japanese rural officials “governed” their indigenous subjects by personally distributing gifts to headmen and retainers at events that involved alcohol consumption and intimate physical contact, far removed from the habitations of the indigenes themselves.
zh: 9 月 12 日，五名使者乘船回大嵙崁，在船上仍旧饮酒、唱歌、打盹。
总督府由此确立了它在山地的最初统治方法：日本乡村官员通过在涉及饮酒与亲密身体接触、且远离原住民自身居所的场合，亲自向头人与扈从分发礼物，来“治理”其原住民臣民。

en: As did Ueno Sen’ichi in 1891, Hashiguchi returned to Tokyo and publicized his observations and opinions regarding Taiwan’s non-Han population. On October 13, 1895, he lectured at the Oriental Club (Tōhō Kyōkai). There, Hashiguchi reiterated Ueno’s assertion that indigenes and Han were mortal enemies, thanks to the Chinese practice of breaking their promises. Hashiguchi characterized the “brigands” (
) fighting the Japanese government as Hakka from Guangdong Province. The
(raw barbarians), by contrast, were well disposed to the Japanese.
Hashiguchi showed up at the Tokyo Geographical Society on October 22, 1895, to repeat his performance.

Colorful speeches like Hashiguchi’s, larded with asides, anecdotes, and speculation, remained popular in prewar Japan. At the same time, there was also an outpouring of attentive journalism and academic writing, including notes and observations about the indigenous alcoholic beverages mentioned in passing by LeGendre, Mizuno, Ueno, and Hashiguchi.
zh: 正如上野专一 1891 年所做的，桥口回到东京，宣传他对台湾非汉族人口的观察与意见。1895 年 10 月 13 日，他在东邦协会（Tōhō Kyōkai）演讲。在那里，桥口重申上野的断言：由于华人背弃承诺的做法，原住民与汉人是死敌。桥口把与日本政府作战的“土匪”（dohi）说成来自广东省的客家人。相比之下，生番（seiban，生蛮）对日本人怀有善意。
桥口于 1895 年 10 月 22 日现身东京地学协会，重复他的表演。
像桥口这样穿插题外话、轶事与揣测的生动演讲，在战前日本一直受欢迎。与此同时，也有大量细致的新闻与学术写作涌现，包括关于李仙得、水野、上野与桥口顺带提及的原住民酒饮的笔记与观察。

en: INDIGENOUS ALCOHOL PRODUCTION AND CONSUMPTION AS CULTURE
zh: 作为文化的原住民酒类生产与消费

en: As a low-ranking official in the Bureau of Education, ethnologist Inō Kanori conducted Japan’s first extensive ethnological survey of the island’s non-Han population. Inō’s influential descriptions confirm Hashiguchi Bunzō’s report on the etiquette observed in the north and indicate that there were several types of liquor found beyond the pale of the former Qing administration. Here is Inō’s description of Atayal spirit production:
zh: 作为教育局的一名低阶官员，民族学家伊能嘉矩开展了日本对该岛非汉族人口的首次大规模民族学调查。伊能那些有影响力的描述，印证了桥口文藏关于北部所见礼节的报告，并表明在原清朝直接管辖的范围之外，有几种不同的酒。以下是伊能对泰雅人酿酒法的描述：

en: To make liquor, millet or rice is steamed in a wooden basket steamer. It is mixed in a pot with water and yeast purchased from the Chinese. This is covered with leaves and brews for three or four days. Then the unfermented yeast is filtered out and the liquor is ready.
zh: 酿酒时，把小米或米放在木甑里蒸。在锅中与水和向华人买来的酒曲混合。盖上叶子，发酵三四天。然后滤去未发酵的酒曲，酒便成了。

en: We should say a word about the related matter of the actual drinking. There is the special custom of two people touching the sides of their mouths together and drinking out of the same vessel. This should be called a drinking ritual (
) which expresses good will or courtesy.
zh: 关于实际饮酒这一相关事项，我们应说几句。有一种特殊习俗：两人嘴侧相碰，从同一器皿饮酒。这应称为表达善意或礼节的饮酒仪式（inrei，饮礼）。

en: Based on more extensive fieldwork, fellow government ethnologist Mori Ushinosuke emphasized that Atayal people were not habitual drinkers; they manufactured and consumed spirits only on special occasions. Mori’s account echoes Inō’s but employs native terminology:
zh: 基于更广泛的田野工作，同为政府民族学家的森丑之助强调，泰雅人并非习惯性饮酒者；他们只在特殊场合酿造与饮用烈酒。森的记述与伊能相呼应，但采用本地术语：

en: Rice or millet is placed in a steamer basket (called a

) and then put on top of a kettle and steamed. It is transferred to a winnowing basket and cooled, and then the appropriate amount of powdered yeast is added and mixed in. It is put in a pot and a little water is mixed in, and the whole thing is covered with leaves. Then heat is applied to certain areas of the pot and it brews for three or four days. Now more water is added and the liquor is filtered in a device made from wisteria, and it is ready to drink.
zh: 把米或小米放进蒸篮（称为 koro），再置于锅上蒸。转移到簸箕里放凉，然后加入适量粉末状酒曲拌匀。放入锅中，拌入少许水，整个盖上叶子。然后在锅的某些部位加热，发酵三四天。这时再加水，用紫藤制的器具滤酒，便可饮用。

en: In some villages, after brewing, the refined portion of the liquor is consumed first and then the rest is expressed. To distribute the liquid portion, a bamboo cup called a zō is dipped into the middle of the kettle.
zh: 在某些村落，酿好后先喝掉酒的精纯部分，再把其余的榨出。为分发液体部分，把一种称为 zō 的竹杯浸入锅中央。

en: Inō’s earlier account also provided recipes and commentary on manufacturing processes and consumption practices among Bunun, Tsou, and Paiwan peoples. Inō noted that Atayal and Bunun both engaged in joined-mouth drinking, while southern groups used double-chambered drinking vessels for the same purpose.
zh: 伊能较早的记述还还记录了布农、邹与排湾各族的酿酒配方，并评述了他们的酿造和饮用方式。伊能指出，泰雅与布农都进行合口饮酒，而南部族群则用双腔饮酒器达到同样目的。

en: Inō Kanori’s diary documents his own direct participation, revealing that even anthropologists were expected to get wet if they would ply their trade in northern Taiwan. On May 26, 1897, in Wulai (just south of Taipei), Inō was welcomed by a young

(brave) named Watosinai, whom Inō had previously met. Upon seeing his acquaintance, Watosinai struck Inō in the chest and then opened up some liquor. Subsequently, Inō and his men joined in a banquet with the village headman, Wataniurrak (Watan Yūra), and Watosinai, during which the younger man broke out into exuberant singing before the group turned in for the evening.
It is probable that this was the same Watan Yū who drank with Ueno in 1891.
zh: 伊能嘉矩的日记记录了他自己的直接参与，揭示出即使是人类学家，要在台湾北部做调查，别人也期待他入席共饮。1897 年 5 月 26 日，在乌来（台北以南），伊能受到一位名叫瓦托西奈（Watosinai）的年轻蕃丁（bantei，勇士）欢迎，伊能此前见过他。一见到熟人，瓦托西奈就击打伊能的胸口，然后打开一些酒。随后，伊能及其随从与村头人瓦丹有洛（Wataniurrak，即 Watan Yūra）及瓦托西奈一起赴宴，期间那年轻人纵情高歌，之后众人才就寝。
这很可能就是 1891 年与上野共饮的那位瓦坦·尤。

en: Through firsthand observation and his study of Qing records, Inō also learned that in addition to welcoming strangers, indigenous Taiwanese engaged in communal drinking at fixed times on the ritual-agricultural calendar. On September 2, 1897, in Tōsha (near Sun Moon Lake), Inō’s party was feasted on native liquor as part of a thirty-day harvest celebration. Inō and his party drank the festival liquor with young and old, finally joining in a ring, dancing and singing as participants in a scene reminiscent of Saigō Tsugumichi’s 1874 adventure. Similar festivities were held when Inō’s party arrived in Beinan on November 9, 1897.
zh: 通过亲身观察与对清朝记录的研究，伊能还了解到，除了欢迎陌生人，台湾原住民还在仪式—农事历法的固定时间进行集体饮酒。1897 年 9 月 2 日，在头社（近日月潭），伊能一行在为期三十天的丰收庆典上受到当地酒款待。伊能及其随从与老少一起喝节庆酒，最后围成一圈歌舞，共同参与了这场让人想起西乡从道1874年经历的庆典。1897 年 11 月 9 日伊能一行抵达卑南时，也举行了类似的欢庆。

en: Okada Shinkō, prefect of Jiayi in 1905, recorded investigations of Tsou customs near Alishan. Okada emphasized that, though liquor was the staple beverage (excepting water) among the Tsou, it was not produced regularly and stored for everyday use but was only for special occasions.

This observation would be repeated in many later reports on various groups of indigenes in Taiwan. In sum, it is evident from contemporary firsthand observations that alcohol consumption, before 1905, was variable and often restricted to particular seasons, occasions, or festivals. For Japanese administrators in the early years, social drinking was an effective method of bringing indigenes down from the hills to government stations and trading posts in order to gather information.
zh: 1905 年嘉义厅长冈田信兴（Okada Shinkō）记录了对阿里山附近邹人习俗的调查。冈田强调，虽然酒是邹人（除水外）的主饮，却并非定期酿造、储存以供日常之用，而只用于特殊场合。
这一观察后来在许多关于台湾各族原住民的报告中被重复。总之，从当时亲身观察可以明显看出，1905 年之前，饮酒是多变的，往往限于特定季节、场合或节日。对早年的日本行政官员而言，社交性饮酒是把原住民从山上引到政府站点与贸易站以搜集信息的有效方法。

en: ESTABLISHING CONNECTIONS THROUGH WET DIPLOMACY
zh: 通过湿外交建立联系

en: Just as the five emissaries from Jiaobanshan were leaving Taipei in September 1895, Hashiguchi Bunzō ordered Captain Kawano Shuichirō to lead Japan’s first official embassy to the Yilan Plain on September 14, 1895. Kawano reported that under the Qing, the border trade with the Nan’ao and Xitou Atayal was conducted privately by interpreters. In 1889, however, after a military campaign to establish a Qing presence in upland Yilan (at a cost of a thousand Chinese lives), a Pacification Office (
) was built at the mountain pass Dingpobuwu to supervise trade with the Xitou tribes. Another

outpost was built at Alishi to manage trade with the Nan’ao tribes. Thus, like Watanabe and Hashiguchi before him, Kawano headed for a well-established junction settlement to initiate diplomacy with Atayal peoples.
zh: 就在角板山五名使者 1895 年 9 月离开台北之际，桥口文藏命河野主一郎（Kawano Shuichirō）大尉于 1895 年 9 月 14 日率日本首个官方使团赴宜兰平原。河野报告说，在清朝治下，与南澳、溪头泰雅人的边境贸易由通译私下进行。然而 1889 年，在一场以一千名华人生命为代价、确立清朝在宜兰山地存在的军事行动之后，清廷在山隘顶破布乌（Dingpobuwu）建了一座抚垦局（fukenju），以监督与溪头各社的贸易。另一座抚垦局哨所建在阿里史（Alishi），以管理与南澳各社的贸易。因此，与之前的渡边和桥口一样，河野前往一个成熟的枢纽聚落，以开启与泰雅各族的外交。

en: Kawano’s expedition left Yilan on November 16, 1895, for Dingpobuwu and wound through narrow passes beset by bamboo thickets. The troop’s ears were assaulted by howling dogs and shrieking waterfowl. The Japanese ferried across a large ravine and forded the same stream over twenty times. To avoid scaring the Atayal away, “fourteen or fifteen” men were ordered to take a rest under cover of a thicket. The government translator and two others were sent ahead. Kawano’s men hiked along a valley from which they saw smoke rising from the many active camphor stoves. At a clearing, the Japanese presented themselves to ten emissaries from two Xitou villages, Xiyanlaowa and Mosu. Among them were eight men, including the Xiyanlaowa headman Yawa Ui, and two women—Kawano recorded all of their names and ages. Kawano’s speech made no mention of nondiscrimination but emphasized Japan’s military superiority, while it demanded compliance. Here is the text Kawano entered in his report:
zh: 河野的远征队 1895 年 11 月 16 日离开宜兰前往顶破布乌，蜿蜒穿过长满密竹的狭窄山口。队伍耳边充斥着嚎叫的狗与尖叫的水禽。日本人渡过一条大沟壑，并二十多次涉过同一溪流。为避免吓跑泰雅人，“十四五名”男子被命令在灌木丛掩护下休息。官派通事与另外两人被派往前方。河野的人沿一条山谷徒步，从那里看到许多正在运作的樟脑灶升起烟。在一处空地，日本人向来自溪头两个村——四烟老瓦（Xiyanlaowa）与墨宿（Mosu）——的十名使者现身。其中有八名男子，包括四烟老瓦头人雅瓦·乌伊（Yawa Ui），以及两名妇女——河野记下他们所有人的姓名与年龄。河野的讲话只字未提无差别，却强调日本的军事优势，同时要求服从。以下是河野写入报告的文本：

en: The Great Empire of Japan has recently defeated the Qing in battle. Now Taiwan and the Pescadores islands belong to us. Henceforth, you shall follow the directives issued by the Great Japanese Empire. Since the local villagers (

) shall henceforth absolutely cease their violent acts, you shall in turn cease committing violent acts against the residents of this district. Because they were enemies of Japan, we killed ten thousand Qing subjects in this region; we sent the other ten thousand back to China. You should not disobey the commands of the Japanese empire and bring disaster upon yourselves. [We shall pacify your hearts, everywhere cultivating virtue and encouraging industry. Eventually, we shall open a path of intercourse between yourselves and Japan.]
zh: 大日本帝国新近在战斗中击败清朝。如今台湾与澎湖群岛归我们所有。从此，你们应遵循大日本帝国发布的指令。既然当地村民（jinmin，人民）从此绝对停止其暴力行为，你们也应停止对本区居民施暴。因为他们是日本的敌人，我们在此地区杀了一万名清朝臣民；把另外一万名送回中国。你们不应违抗日本帝国的命令而自招灾祸。[我们将安抚你们的心，处处修德劝业。最终，我们将在你们与日本之间开辟一条交往之路。]

en: Echoing the June 8, 1874, meeting between Paiwan emissaries and Commander Saigō in Hengchun, Kawano and his men distributed a Japanese flag, gifts, drink, and food to the assembled Xitou men and women. The meeting featured trappings of a negotiation, with its attendant toasting, gifting, and oathing, but the visitors were backed with overwhelming military force just beyond the scene of the meeting. In this regard, parleys on Taiwan’s “savage border” in the opening decade of Japanese colonial rule were not so different from treaty-port negotiations between Qing, Tokugawa, and Joseon officials and gunboat diplomatists.
zh: 呼应 1874 年 6 月 8 日排湾使者与西乡司令在恒春的会面，河野及其部下向聚集的溪头男女分发一面日本国旗、礼物、酒与食物。这次会面带有谈判的排场，伴随敬酒、馈赠与宣誓，但访客背后有压倒性军力就在会面场景之外撑腰。在这方面，日本殖民统治头十年台湾“生番界”上的会谈，与清朝、德川、朝鲜官员同炮舰外交官之间的条约口岸谈判，并无太大不同。

en: In some cases, as with LeGendre’s early meetings with Toketok or Akamatsu’s first meeting with Isa, the threat was imperfectly understood or ignored. Such was the case with Kawano’s mission. Despite the bluster, the Xitou men firmly refused Kawano’s entreaties to visit the walled city of Yilan for further parleys, just as Watan Nui of Jiaobanshan refused a similar request from Hashiguchi to visit Taipei. They also rebuffed Japanese requests to travel farther inland. The Xitou emissaries did offer to distribute the remaining gifts to other tribes and act as intermediaries between the Japanese and the inland villages.
The mission succeeded in establishing rudimentary communication, but the new subjects of empire successfully parried Japanese attempts to visit their habitations.
zh: 在某些情况下，如李仙得早期与卓杞笃的会面、或赤松与伊萨的首次会面，威胁被不完全理解或被忽视。河野使团正是如此。尽管虚张声势，溪头男子坚决拒绝河野请他们到宜兰城内继续会谈的邀请，正如角板山的瓦坦·努伊拒绝桥口类似的赴台北请求。他们也驳回日本人更深入内陆的要求。溪头使者确实提议把剩余礼物分发给其他社，并充当日本人与内陆村落之间的居间人。
使团成功建立了初步沟通，但帝国的新臣民成功挡开了日本人探访其居所的企图。

en: The Watanabe, Hashiguchi, and Kawano missions all took place near the Taipei Basin or Yilan Plain, at active nodes of indigenous-Chinese-Qing communication, trade, and warfare. The junction city of Puli, farther south, shared these attributes but was farther inland and more remote from the coastal ports and cities. While the highest mountains in the Langqiao visited by Saigō in 1874 were about 200 meters above sea level, the Puli basin sat at about 500 meters, and Japan’s first Sediq contact settlement of Paalan was at an altitude of about 1200 meters. At these higher altitudes, the Hiyama mission broke new ground among villages not found on treaty-port maps of Taiwan.
zh: 渡边、桥口与河野使团都发生在台北盆地或宜兰平原附近，处于原住民—华人—清朝沟通、贸易与战争的活跃节点。更南边的枢纽城市埔里具备这些特征，但更深入内陆、更远离沿海港口与城市。西乡 1874 年所访琅峤的最高山约海拔 200 米，而埔里盆地约海拔 500 米，日本首个赛德克接触聚落芭兰（Paalan）则约海拔 1200 米。在这些更高海拔处，桧山使团在条约口岸台湾地图上找不到的村落间开辟了新天地。

en: Puli prefect Hiyama Tetsusaburō made his first overtures to the Tgdaya (Sediq) tribes of Paalan in December 1895. Following precedent, Hiyama dispatched a “northern tribe” wife of a
(cooked barbarian) to carry gifts and a message to the most powerful Tgdaya chief, the headman of Paalan.

After her second trip and much delay, four Sediq scouts came to test the waters in Puli. They were promptly treated to drinking, dancing, and photographs with a Captain Ishihara of the Puli garrison. On December 31, the Paalan headman brought five “subordinate” village headmen and a contingent of three hundred retainers, plus women and children, down to Puli. The Japanese put them up on the grounds of the old Qing Pacification Office post, sending them provisions of sake, rice, and salt. The next day Hiyama Tetsusaburō, a government interpreter (tsūyakukan), and “two or three low-ranking officials” delivered an inaugural Japanese speech:
zh: 埔里厅长桧山铁三郎（Hiyama Tetsusaburō）于 1895 年 12 月首次向芭兰的德固达雅（Tgdaya，赛德克）各社示好。遵循先例，桧山派一名熟蕃（jukuban）的“北番”妻子携带礼物与口信给最强大的德固达雅酋长——芭兰头人。
在她第二次出行并久拖之后，四名赛德克人先到埔里探察情形。他们随即被款待饮酒、跳舞，并与埔里驻军的石原（Ishihara）大尉合影。12 月 31 日，芭兰头人带五名“下属”村头人与三百名扈从，外加妇女儿童，下到埔里。日本人把他们安置在旧清朝抚垦局哨所的场地上，送给他们清酒、米与盐。次日，桧山铁三郎、一名政府通译官（tsūyakukan）与“两三名低阶官员”发表了一篇日本开场讲话：

en: We are overjoyed that you have come here from afar. From the beginning, we Japanese, as your brothers, have desired to meet and parley with you. Fortunately, the whole of the island has been restored as the emperor’s territory. Now we have come to establish our administration on this part of the island. We are genuinely pleased to have this opportunity to meet with you.
zh: 你们远道而来，我们欣喜万分。从一开始，我们日本人作为你们的兄弟，就希望与你们会面洽谈。幸而全岛已恢复为天皇的领土。如今我们来岛上这一部分建立我们的行政。我们由衷高兴有此机会与你们会面。

en: We have heard that you have always killed and injured Chinese people. This is a very evil practice. If you are really our brothers, as we have already mentioned, you absolutely must stop murdering. You may come visit our offices at any time. We, in turn, would like to go to your abodes. Today, since you have visited our offices, we have prepared a meager offering of drinks and side dishes. So let us drink with gladness to your arrival!
zh: 我们听说你们一向杀伤华人。这是非常恶劣的做法。倘若你们真如我们已提到的那样是我们的兄弟，就绝对必须停止杀人。你们可随时来拜访我们的官署。我们相应也想去你们的住处。今天，既然你们拜访了我们的官署，我们备下薄酒小菜。那么就为你们的到来欣然共饮吧！

en: After hearing this initial Japanese declaration, the Tgdaya contingent replied with a counterspeech: “Murder and carnage do not come naturally to us. In the past, the Chinese have gathered strength in numbers and committed murder when catching one or two of us alone. Therefore, when we find a small group of Chinese, we murder them. But now that the Japanese are our brothers, we will certainly not act this way anymore.”
zh: 听完这篇日本开场声明，德固达雅一行以一篇答辞回应：“杀人与屠戮并非我们的天性。过去，华人聚众恃强，在抓到我们一两人落单时便下杀手。因此，当我们发现一小群华人时，就杀他们。但既然如今日本人是我们的兄弟，我们绝不会再这样做了。”

en: With this exchange of solemn promises and admonishments, a stone-burying ceremony ensued. The anonymous correspondent who chronicled this exchange explained, “even should this stone and things thus buried disintegrate, our promises to each other shall not be altered.”
zh: 随着这番郑重承诺与告诫的交换，一场埋石仪式随之举行。记载这次交流的匿名通讯员解释：“即便这块石头与如此埋下之物朽坏，我们彼此的承诺也不会改变。”

en: INSTITUTIONALIZING WET DIPLOMACY
zh: 湿外交的制度化

en: In January 1896, district officials and Taipei authorities issued decrees and created organs of government for the purpose of routinizing and regulating contacts with indigenes. As a former Qing center of administration and hub of the border trade, Dakekan was the logical starting point. The old walled city of Dakekan housed the government-general’s first dispatch station (shutchōjo), the forerunner of the Pacification Offices.

Its chief, Miyanohara Tōhachi, applied to the government general for a modest 143 yen to fund “Barbarian Feasts” (seiban kyōhi) as a first step to addressing the area’s endemic violence. Miyanohara acknowledged that a recent rash of murders and beheadings by Atayal people could be attributed to Japanese disarmament policies that left Chinese dwelling near the “savage border” defenseless. Nonetheless, Miyanohara trotted out a list of good reasons for Atayal to murder Han sight unseen: Qing policy was one-sided and relied exclusively on force; Han merchants cheated indigenes in trading; Han cultivators encroached on Atayal lands; and finally, Han were just as guilty of murdering uplanders as the mountaineers were of raiding the townspeople.
zh: 1896 年 1 月，府县官员与台北当局发布法令、设立政府机构，以使与原住民的接触常规化、规范化。作为前清朝行政中心与边境贸易枢纽，大嵙崁是合乎逻辑的起点。大嵙崁旧城墙内城市设有总督府首个出张所（shutchōjo），即抚垦署的前身。

其长官宫之原藤八（Miyanohara Tōhachi）向总督府申请区区 143 日元，以资助“生番宴飨费”（seiban kyōhi），作为处理该地区痼疾性暴力的第一步。宫之原承认，泰雅人近来一连串的杀人与斩首，可归因于日本的缴械政策——它使住在“生番界”附近的华人毫无防卫。尽管如此，宫之原仍列举了泰雅人即使面对素不相识的汉人也杀害对方的诸般理由：清朝政策片面、专恃武力；汉商在贸易中欺骗原住民；汉人垦民侵占泰雅土地；最后，汉人杀害山地人之罪，正如山地人袭击镇民一样深重。

en: Miyanohara insisted that the Atayal were stubborn, obstinate, and unreasonable. However, they were very well disposed toward the Japanese and could be counted on to keep an agreement. Thus, to prevent further violence, Miyanohara invited over ten village headmen and admonished them to stop killing Han. To govern through suasion, Miyanohara argued, regular feasts for village leaders were the ticket.

The government organ that would forever be associated with feasting and drinking, the Pacification Office, was chartered to begin work on April 1, 1896, soon after Miyanohara made his recommendations.
zh: 宫之原坚称泰雅人顽固、执拗、不讲理。然而他们对日本人怀有善意，可以指望他们守约。因此，为防止进一步暴力，宫之原邀请十多名村头人，告诫他们停止杀汉人。宫之原辩称，要通过劝服来治理，定期为村领袖设宴是不二法门。
那个将永远与宴饮联系在一起的政府机构——抚垦署——获准于 1896 年 4 月 1 日开始运作，就在宫之原提出建议后不久。

en: The early years of Japanese “Aborigine administration” (

) —the “Pacification Office period”—were later criticized for their leniency, along the same lines for which Ōkubo criticized lax Qing rule in Langqiao in 1874. As a policy that left border areas opaque and hindered Taiwan’s economic integration, the gift policy became a lightning rod for invective. These criticisms perhaps overstated the government-general’s largesse, however. The initial proposed budget of ¥1,293 for gifts, or about ¥215 per prefecture, was less than half the monthly cost of subsidizing a local Chinese militia to stand guard against the very same Atayal men and women targeted to receive these gifts. In short, the feasts and gift distributions held at the dispatch stations wrapped the savage-border militia’s iron fist in a velvet glove. Just as LeGendre and Saigō professed the warm relations between non-Chinese foreigners and indigenes as a product of each side’s sincerity, the actual meetings were held with overwhelming firepower in reserve on the side of the visitors.
zh: 日本“理蕃”（riban）的早年——即“抚垦署时期”——后来因其宽纵而受批评，理由与 1874 年大久保批评清朝在琅峤松弛统治的理由相同。作为一项使边境地区不透明、阻碍台湾经济整合的政策，礼物政策成了众矢之的。然而这些批评或许夸大了总督府的慷慨。最初拟议的礼物预算 1293 日元、即每厅约 215 日元，还不到资助一支地方华人团练每月开销的一半——而那支团练正是用来防备那些将被馈赠礼物的泰雅男女。简言之，在出张所举行的宴饮与礼物分发，给生番界团练的铁拳套上了天鹅绒手套。正如李仙得与西乡宣称非华人外国人与原住民之间的温情是双方诚意的产物，实际会面举行时，访客一侧却有压倒性火力作为后备。

en: As a veteran of the 1874 expedition, Satsuma man Kabayama Sukenori took a special interest in indigenous affairs. Yet his programs had to meet strict budget constraints, due to the cost of the war against Han insurgents and the fact that Taiwan was a drain on Tokyo’s finances. Therefore, the twenty policemen originally requested by the governor-general for each of eleven proposed Pacification Offices, at a total cost of ¥111,181, were cut out of the budget. Instead, each station received one interpreter (tsūyaku of
rank), two assistants to the chief (
of
rank), and two “operatives” (
of
rank); only eight out of the eleven stations would have a chief (
of sōnin rank), for a total of sixty-three officials, including chiefs.
In May 1896, Bureau of Industrial Development Chief Oshikawa Noriyoshi, under whose purview the Pacification Office fell, requested forty-two additional “staffers and special commissioners (
and
)” for the rural outposts.
zh: 作为 1874 年远征的老兵，萨摩人桦山资纪对原住民事务有特别兴趣。然而由于对汉人抗日军作战的开销、以及台湾是东京财政的负担这一事实，他的计划必须满足严格的预算约束。因此，总督最初为十一座拟议抚垦署各请求的二十名警察、总计 111181 日元，被从预算中砍掉。取而代之，每站获配一名通译（判任级，tsūyaku）、两名长官助理（判任级书记补，shujiho）、两名“技手”（判任级，gishu）；十一站中只有八站设长官（奏任级书记，shuji），含长官共六十三名官员。
1896 年 5 月，抚垦署所属的殖产局长押川则义（Oshikawa Noriyoshi）为乡村前哨请求增派四十二名“雇员与事务嘱托”（koin and jimu shokutaku）。

en: In our first concrete example of how Japan governed the indigenes “on the cheap,” these 105 pacification officers were charged with intelligence gathering, diplomatic relations, commerce, and public works among a population commonly believed to cover 60 percent of Taiwan’s territory and comprising at least eight major language groups (and many dialects). Although the indigenous population was estimated at around only 100,000 souls, they inhabited forbidding terrain and guarded their autonomy with widely available firearms.
zh: 这是我们关于日本如何“廉价”治理原住民的第一个具体例子：这 105 名抚垦官员负责对至少分属八个主要语言群（另有许多方言）的居民开展工作，包括收集情报、外交交涉、商业和公共工程；这些居民的居住范围通常被认为占台湾面积的60%。尽管原住民人口估计仅约十万，他们却居住于险恶地形，并以广泛可得的火器捍卫其自治。

en: Dispatch station chief Miyanohara Tōhachi was appointed first Dakekan Pacification Office head on May 25, 1896. The station itself commenced activities on June 30.

Within the month, local headmen accepted Miyanohara’s invitations to Dakekan city for parleys. He was not sure exactly where these villages were located, however. Things got off to a rocky start when his Han tsūji (interpreter) refused to go inland for fear of a bandit leader known as Jian Ai. This so-called bandit was ensconced in the mountains beyond Dakekan in Shinajii, with his Atayal wife and a number of followers. Shinajii was home to many of the emissaries who had met with Hashiguchi the previous September.
Miyanohara heard that Jian Ai was turning the Atayal against the Japanese, so he wanted to apprehend him.
zh: 出张所长官宫之原藤八于 1896 年 5 月 25 日被任命为首任大嵙崁抚垦署长。该站本身于 6 月 30 日开始活动。
当月之内，地方头人接受宫之原邀请到大嵙崁城会谈。然而他并不确切知道这些村落位于何处。事情开局不利：他的汉族通事（tsūji）因害怕一名叫简阿（Jian Ai）的土匪首领而拒绝进入内陆。这个所谓的土匪带着他的泰雅妻子与若干追随者，盘踞在大嵙崁以外山中的希纳吉（Shinajii）。希纳吉是许多去年 9 月会见过桥口的使者的家乡。
宫之原听说简阿正在煽动泰雅人反对日本人，因此想逮捕他。

en: Miyanohara hired two local interpreters in Dakekan as well as two

(female Atayal) to accompany them to the interior. Their immediate target was the paramount headman Daima Weixian of Yiheng. The four interpreters reached him, and then Daima sent six scouts to Dakekan. They were duly feasted, toasted, and lodged on the evening of July 21, 1896. The Japanese sent them back to Yiheng with fancy cigars to entice Daima to broker a parley.
zh: 宫之原在大嵙崁雇了两名地方通译，以及两名蕃婦（banpu，泰雅妇女）陪同他们进入内陆。他们的直接目标是义兴（Yiheng）的最高头人大马·威贤（Daima Weixian）。四名通译找到他，随后大马派六名侦察兵到大嵙崁。1896 年 7 月 21 日晚，他们被殷勤设宴、敬酒、安置住宿。日本人送他们回义兴，带上精美雪茄，以诱使大马居间安排一次会谈。

en: On July 28, a contingent of chiefs, men, women, and children representing six villages arrived at Dakekan. Miyanohara recorded, “When the indigenes arrived, the two

explained to us what sort of feast to prepare. They like nothing more than pork, salted fish, and native liquor.” As it turned out, Jian Ai answered the call, while Daima did not. Miyanohara offered Jian Ai amnesty for his past crimes against Japan in return for a pledge to become an interpreter and informant on conditions near Shinajii, conditions to which Jian Ai apparently assented. Chief Daima’s emissaries attributed his absence to an injured leg.
zh: 7 月 28 日，代表六个村的一行酋长、男子、妇女与儿童抵达大嵙崁。宫之原记录：“原住民到来时，两名蕃婦向我们解释该备什么样的宴席。他们最爱的莫过于猪肉、咸鱼与本地酒。”结果，简阿应召而来，大马却没有。宫之原向简阿提出赦免他过去对日本的罪行，以换取他承诺充当通译与线人、报告希纳吉附近的情况——简阿显然同意了这些条件。大马酋长的使者把他的缺席归因于腿伤。

en: Saitō Otosaku, the chief of the Linyipu Pacification Office (see
), counted fifty-two villages under his charge. He reported that in August 1897, twenty of his twenty-seven men were in sick bay.

The turnover rate was high. In its second year, the total number of salaried officials in the Pacification Office increased to sixty-five (from fifty-seven the year before), but forty-one of these officials were new. In some posts, like Puli, the turnover rate was 100 percent for titled officials.

And here was a potentially fatal flaw: from the indigenous side, particularistic bonds were being forged via wet-diplomatic protocols, while from the Japanese side, duty on the savage border was a sort of exile to be endured and then left behind as quickly as possible.
zh: 林圮埔抚垦署长齐藤音作（Saitō Otosaku，见
）辖下计有五十二个村。他报告说，1897 年 8 月，他二十七名部下中有二十名在病号房。
人员流动率很高。第二年，抚垦署领薪官员总数增至六十五名（前一年为五十七名），但其中四十一名是新人。在某些职位，如埔里，有官衔官员的流动率达 100%。
这里有一个潜在致命缺陷：从原住民一侧，依托特定个人的关系正通过湿外交礼仪被锻造；而从日本一侧，在生番界任职是一种流放，须忍受而后尽快撇下离开。

en: FIGURE 12. The Linyipu District Administrative Office, successor to the Pacification Office, on eve of expedition to the mountain tribes, December 15, 1898. Twenty indigenous porters are loaded down with gifts to bring to the interior. Karl Theodor Stöpel,

children: Eine Reise in das Innere der Insel Formosa und die erste Besteigung des Niitakayama (Mount Morrison

zh: 图 12. 林圮埔区行政署（抚垦署的继任机构），1898 年 12 月 15 日远征山地各社前夕。二十名原住民脚夫满载要带入内陆的礼物。Karl Theodor Stöpel, Eine Reise in das Innere der Insel Formosa und die erste Besteigung des Niitakayama (Mount Morrison) (Buenos Aires: Companñía sud-americana de billetes de banco, 1905), 42.
