图 12. 林圮埔区行政署（抚垦署的继任机构），1898 年 12 月 15 日远征山地各社前夕。二十名原住民脚夫满载要带入内陆的礼物。Karl Theodor Stöpel, Eine Reise in das Innere der Insel Formosa und die erste Besteigung des Niitakayama (Mount Morrison) (Buenos Aires: Companñía sud-americana de billetes de banco, 1905), 42.

en: The Pacification Office installations themselves were built over a period of two months, from June 2 to August 3, 1896. Oshikawa Noriyoshi, Hashiguchi Bunzō’s successor in the Industrial Promotion Section, issued a thirteen-point circular defining the Pacification Office’s mission. Oshikawa underscored the importance of explaining to chiefs and men of influence that the Japanese were impartial rulers. He wrote that the simple, savage indigenes could quickly be won over by gift giving, and he instructed officers to meet with headmen on appointed days, distribute presents, and explain Japan’s imperial mission. Loyal villages would be rewarded with further gifts, while disobedient ones would be punished by withholding presents.

This last caveat presupposed that indigenous hunger for imported goods was strong enough to leverage cooperation in such operations as mapping, labor dragoons, and even turning over local peoples to Japanese police officers. For many areas of Taiwan, however, such conditions would not obtain until the 1920s or even later.
zh: 抚垦署设施本身在 1896 年 6 月 2 日至 8 月 3 日两个月间建成。押川则义——桥口文藏在殖产课的继任者——发布一份列有十三条内容的通函，界定抚垦署的使命。押川强调向酋长与有影响力者说明日本人是公正统治者的重要性。他写道，单纯、野蛮的原住民可以通过赠礼迅速争取过来，并指示官员在指定日子与头人会面、分发礼物、解释日本的帝国使命。忠诚的村落将获得更多礼物作为奖赏，不顺从的则被扣留礼物作为惩罚。
这最后一条但书预设：原住民对进口货的渴望足够强烈，足以撬动他们在测绘、强征劳役、甚至把当地人交给日本警官等行动中的合作。然而对台湾许多地区而言，这样的条件直到 1920 年代甚至更晚才会具备。

en: THE ORIGINS OF SPECIAL ADMINISTRATION
zh: 特别行政的起源

en: During the early years of Japanese rule, members of parliament and other public intellectuals advocated for the extension of the Japanese constitution to Taiwan. The debate was similar to ones raging in the United States about the Philippine Islands. At issue was the capacity of colonized populations to “play by the rules,” or bear the rights and responsibilities of citizens. While the “extend the constitution” faction lost the early rounds of the debate, over the course of Japanese colonial rule in Taiwan, a great deal of legal integration between the mother country and the colony actually occurred. However, the geographic reach of this integration stopped at the areas beyond the old Qing savage border, in the areas placed under “special administration.”
zh: 日本统治初年，国会议员与其他公共知识分子主张把日本宪法延伸适用于台湾。这场辩论与美国围绕菲律宾群岛激烈展开的辩论相似。争议的焦点是被殖民人口是否有能力“按规则行事”，即享有公民权利并履行公民责任。尽管“延伸宪法”派在辩论的前几个回合落败，但在日本殖民统治台湾的过程中，母国与殖民地之间实际上发生了大量法律整合。然而，这种整合的地理范围止于旧清朝的生番界，生番界外的地区划入“特别行政”。

en: Early debates about the legal bifurcation of Taiwan, into normally and specially administered zones, occurred in the spring of 1897. Then, the Pacification Office heads met under the aegis of Oshikawa to chart a course for the future based on their first eight or nine months of field experience. One of the burning issues regarded punishments for head taking, robbery, and other violent crimes—the myriad “illegalities” that fester in ungoverned areas beyond the reach of “public power,” to use Foucault’s phraseology. Hiyama Tetsusaburō, the first Japanese prefect posted to Puli, argued that Japanese law could not be applied to the Sediq peoples under his charge. Echoing the Zongli Yamen members who contested Ōkubo two decades prior, Hiyama argued that, if penalized severely for murder, as called for in Japanese law, Sediq people would rebel en masse. Besides, Hiyama added, if Japan enacted a strict, consistent law code for the Sediq and Atayal peoples, it could only be applied to those who had shown themselves at the Pacification Offices. In the end, he recommended an ad hoc form of punishment, appropriate to the means at the disposal of the overstretched colonial state: “for those who take heads, cut off their gifts completely, stop distributing liquor, and stop giving them their needed salt.”
zh: 关于把台湾在法律上二分为普通行政区与特别行政区的早期辩论，发生在 1897 年春。当时，各抚垦署长在押川则义的主持下开会，依据他们最初八九个月的实地经验为未来规划路线。其中一个紧迫议题涉及对猎首、抢劫及其他暴力犯罪的惩罚——借用福柯的措辞，即在“公共权力”鞭长莫及的无治理地区滋生的种种“非法行为”。首位派驻埔里的日本厅长桧山铁三郎主张，日本法律不能适用于他管辖下的赛德克人。呼应二十年前与大久保争辩的总理衙门大臣，桧山辩称，若按日本法律的要求对杀人严惩，赛德克人会群起反抗。此外，桧山补充说，即便日本为赛德克与泰雅人制定一套严格、一致的法典，它也只能适用于那些曾到抚垦署露过面的人。最终，他建议一种权宜的惩罚形式，以与这个捉襟见肘的殖民国家所能支配的手段相称：“对猎首者，完全断绝其礼物，停止分发酒，并停止给予他们所需的盐。”

en: On the last day of the aforementioned conference, the Civil Affairs Bureau of the Taiwan Government General issued regulations to the prefects, subprefects, and gendarmes (

) in regions with significant non-Han populations. The regulations are prefaced by a recognition that hunting was crucial to indigenous livelihoods, explaining that a complete ban on guns was inadvisable. Nonetheless, the following restrictions were put into effect to check what was perceived as rampant disorder:
zh: 在上述会议的最后一天，台湾总督府民政局向非汉人口较多地区的各厅长、支厅长与宪兵（kenpeitai）发布了规章。规章开头承认狩猎对原住民生计至关重要，并说明全面禁枪并不可取。尽管如此，为遏制被视为猖獗的混乱，仍实施了以下限制：

children: 1. Merchants must have a certificate/warrant (shōmei) from the Pacification Office head to supply indigenes with gunpowder —no exceptions (kyokashō) or special permits (tokkyo shō) are allowed.
1. 商人向原住民供应火药，必须持有抚垦署长出具的证明/凭照（shōmei）——不允许任何特许状（kyokashō）或特许证（tokkyo shō）。
2. Those who are not merchants must have a permit/permission (
) from the Pacification Office to supply indigenes with gunpowder; for hunting rifles, the police and gendarmes may supply up to 3
(about 375 grams) of gunpowder or 500 percussion caps/fuses; to supply over this limit requires permission of the prefect.
2. 非商人向原住民供应火药，必须获得抚垦署的许可（kyoka）；就猎枪而言，警察与宪兵至多可供应 3 百目（约 375 克）火药或 500 枚火帽/导火索；超过此限额的供应须经厅长许可。

body.review: 原书第93页纸面作 3 hyakume (about 375 grams)。按匁为3.75克，三百目应为1,125克。正文照录原书两种数值。

children: 3. The distribution of gunpowder to indigenes falls within the purview of the Pacification Office and therefore should be witnessed by officials.
3. 向原住民分发火药属抚垦署职权范围，因此应由官员在场见证。
4. The Pacification Office must issue a monthly report to the police and gendarmes stating the amount and kinds of gunpowder distributed to indigenes.
4. 抚垦署必须每月向警察与宪兵提交报告，说明分发给原住民的火药数量与种类。

en: Some Pacification Office heads judged the 1897 regulations on trade as too lenient. In the fall of 1897, Nagano Yoshitora, who replaced Hiyama Tetsusaburō as Puli Pacification Office chief in July, argued that Atayal tribes were more bloodthirsty than the Bunun tribes who resided south of Puli. Nagano agreed that the new regulations on gunpowder and shot should be observed in the south, but that a complete ban should be put into effect for Atayal. In keeping with the early Japanese view that the indigenes were, at heart, good subjects, Nagano suggested that the northern “savages” be reformed by taking them on sightseeing tours of Taipei.
After sufficient transformation, the trade in gunpowder and shot, so vital to peoples who relied on hunting for protein, could be resumed.

In fact, Nagano’s recommendation was taken to heart, and a delegation of indigenous representatives toured Japan that year; they were received by throngs of curious onlookers. In the short term, the tours did not have the intended effect of reducing violence related to camphor forests, however.
zh: 一些抚垦署长认为 1897 年的贸易规章过于宽松。1897 年秋，于 7 月接替桧山铁三郎出任埔里抚垦署长的长野义虎（Nagano Yoshitora）主张，泰雅各社比居住在埔里以南的布农各社更好杀。长野同意南部应遵守关于火药与弹丸的新规章，但对泰雅人应实施全面禁令。与早期日本人认为原住民骨子里是良善臣民的看法一致，长野建议通过带北方“生番”到台北观光游览来教化他们。
待充分转变之后，对依赖狩猎获取蛋白质的族群至关重要的火药与弹丸贸易便可恢复。
事实上，长野的建议被采纳，当年一个原住民代表使团游览了日本；他们受到成群好奇围观者的接待。然而短期内，这些游览并未起到减少樟脑森林相关暴力的预期效果。

en: In response to a report that the Wuzhishan Pacification Office had punished a camphor worker’s murder by levying a “traditional fine” of shell-money currency, Division of Interior head Sugimura Shun took exception. “Traditional” punishments, even if supplemented by embargoes of trade or the cessation of gifts, he argued, would embolden indigenes and cause them to despise the weak government. Outraged, Sugimura suggested that Pacification Office chiefs use gifts as weapons, and that trade embargoes, as means of collective punishment, could force the hands of indigenous leaders. Before resuming trade, the Pacification Office should
zh: 针对一份报告称五指山（Wuzhishan）抚垦署在一名樟脑工人被杀后，循“传统罚金”的方式向肇事一方征收贝币，内务部长杉村浚（Sugimura Shun）提出异议。他辩称，“传统”惩罚即便辅以贸易禁运或停止赠礼，也会助长原住民的气焰，使他们藐视软弱的政府。杉村愤而建议，抚垦署长应把礼物当作武器使用，而贸易禁运作为集体惩罚的手段，可以迫使原住民头人就范。在恢复贸易之前，抚垦署应：

children: 1. Order that the indigenous perpetrator be delivered.
1. 命令交出原住民肇事者。
2. After receiving the delivered perpetrator, deal with them by applying the law.
2. 收到被交出的肇事者后，依法处置。

3. During the time that the perpetrator has not been delivered, the whole village should be held responsible: the distribution of gifts will be suspended; it goes without saying that the sale of arms and ammunition will be strictly banned.
3. 在肇事者尚未被交出期间，全村应被追究责任：暂停分发礼物；武器弹药的售卖更将严格禁止，自不待言。
4. During the period referred to in item 3, other villages will be ordered to cut off commerce/communication with the [offending] village.
4. 在第 3 条所述期间，将命令其他村落断绝与〔肇事〕村落的商业/往来。

en: In July 1897, Kawakami Chikakata, Pacification Office head in southern Taiwan’s Fanshuliao Prefecture, also railed against the patchy sovereignty that characterized Japan’s government along the savage border. Kawakami noted that many camphor harvesters were forced to present gifts to indigenous headmen for access to the forests; some demanded rattan, others tea leaves. These audacious headmen even collected tribute outside the so-called Aborigine Territory. The indigenes were acting under the mistaken impression that they “owned the land” and could force outsiders to pay tribute, which in turn required the services of the hated “go-betweens,” who were completely untrustworthy, according to Kawakami. In the end, commerce and “Aborigine education” were impeded because of blurred distinctions between public and private. Kawakami suggested that all lands abutting the Aborigine Territory be put under the jurisdiction of the Pacification Office.
zh: 1897 年 7 月，台湾南部番薯寮（Fanshuliao）厅抚垦署长川上亲方（Kawakami Chikakata）也抨击了日本沿生番界治理所呈现的那种斑驳残缺的主权。川上指出，许多采制樟脑的人被迫向原住民头人送礼以换取进入森林的权利；有的索要藤条，有的索要茶叶。这些大胆的头人甚至在所谓的蕃地之外征收贡赋。原住民是在一种错误印象下行事，以为自己“拥有土地”、可以强迫外人纳贡，而这又需要为人所恨的“居间人”效劳——按川上的说法，这些人完全不可信任。最终，由于公私界限模糊，商业与“蕃人教育”都受到阻碍。川上建议把所有毗邻蕃地的土地置于抚垦署管辖之下。

en: THE FUKAHORI MISSION AND THE END OF WET DIPLOMACY
zh: 深堀使团与湿外交的终结

en: While the Pacification Office was still operative, in February 1897, an expedition led by one Captain Fukahori Yasuichirō disappeared in the Neng’gao mountain peaks just northeast of Puli while searching for a potential railway route to Hualian Harbor. Captain Fukahori left Puli in late January 1897, and by March, all fourteen of his men were given up for dead. In April the local garrison chief initiated a prolonged, frustrating series of negotiations with area headmen to find the remains and the Fukahori expedition’s murderers. Reminiscent of LeGendre’s search for the remains of shipwreck victims in 1860s Langqiao, the usual methods of gift presentations backed by threats were used, but the area headmen stonewalled the investigation.

To pour salt in the wounds, a camphor worker was slain by Tgdaya locals at the same time. In retaliation for Fukahori’s disappearance, the stymied investigation, and the fresh killing, the government imposed an embargo on salt, ammunition, and guns for eight whole years.
zh: 抚垦署尚在运作之时，1897 年 2 月，一支由深堀安一郎（Fukahori Yasuichirō）大尉率领的探险队在埔里东北方的能高（Neng'gao）山峰失踪，当时他们正在探寻一条通往花莲港的潜在铁路路线。深堀大尉于 1897 年 1 月下旬离开埔里，到 3 月，他手下的十四人均被认为已经遇难。4 月，当地驻军长官发起了一场旷日持久、令人沮丧的与地区头人的谈判，以寻找遗骸与深堀探险队的凶手。令人想起李仙得 1860 年代在琅峤搜寻沉船受害者遗骸的情形，日本人使用了以威胁为后盾的惯常赠礼手段，但地区头人对调查百般阻挠。
更雪上加霜的是，与此同时一名樟脑工人被德固达雅当地人杀害。为报复深堀的失踪、受阻的调查与这桩新的杀戮，政府对盐、弹药与枪支实施了整整八年的禁运。

en: As we have seen, the Pacification Office officials operated through concentric rings of intermediaries at this time. The whole structure was bound together by the distribution of material goods and the forging of personal bonds through drinking rituals. The first intermediaries were the “Aborigine interpreters,” male and female, who were sent to mountain redoubts to bring headmen to the Pacification Office stations with promises of gifts, food, and drink. The next ring of intermediaries were the “conciliated/submitted” indigenes who carried invitations to other villages, bringing more headmen, interpreters, warriors, and children to the Pacification Office’s banquets, gift distributions, and trading fairs. Although this system performed well enough for an understaffed, poorly informed, outnumbered set of rural outposts, it could not protect camphor harvesters from indigenes who felt cheated of customary tolls or were defending what they considered ancestral territory. Moreover, indigenes desperate for salt, guns, ammunition, or machine-made cloth traded through other indigenous groups to subvert the embargo.

Rightly sensing that the understaffed, lightly armed, and linguistically disadvantaged Pacification Office could not extend sovereignty by wet diplomacy alone, the government-general decided to abolish it altogether and place indigenous affairs within the purview of the Third Section of the lowest rung of the territorial administrative hierarchy, the District Administrative Office (
, hereafter DAO).
zh: 如我们所见，此时抚垦署官员通过一圈圈同心圆式的居间人来运作。整个结构靠物品的分发以及通过饮酒仪式建立的个人情谊维系在一起。第一层居间人是“蕃人通事”，有男有女，他们被派往山地据点，以礼物、食物与酒水的许诺把头人带到抚垦署站点。下一层居间人是“已归顺/已臣服”的原住民，他们把邀请带到其他村落，带来更多头人、通事、战士与儿童，参加抚垦署的宴饮、礼物分发与贸易集市。尽管对于一组人手不足、信息匮乏、寡不敌众的乡村前哨而言，这套系统运作得还算不错，但它无法保护樟脑采伐者免受原住民的伤害——这些原住民或觉得自己被剥夺了惯常的通行税，或在保卫其视为祖先领土的土地。此外，亟需盐、枪支、弹药或机织布的原住民通过其他原住民群体进行贸易，以规避禁运。
总督府正确地意识到，人手不足、武装薄弱、语言上处于劣势的抚垦署无法单靠湿外交扩展主权，于是决定将其彻底撤销，把原住民事务置于地方行政层级最底层的辨务署（Benmusho，下称 DAO）第三课的职权范围之内。

en: After the DAO replaced the Pacification Office in the summer of 1898, Japanese rural administrators repeatedly called for tougher measures against the indigenes who fought back against aggressive timber harvesting. Time and again, administrators called for trade blockades to be used as incentives for good behavior. In other words, now that the Japanese, like the Qing before them, were taking sides in an economic war for rights to harvest timber along the savage border, mentions of Japan’s “special relationship” to indigenes disappeared.
zh: 1898 年夏辨务署取代抚垦署之后，日本乡村行政官员一再呼吁对反抗激进木材采伐的原住民采取更强硬的措施。官员们一次次要求把贸易封锁用作激励良好行为的手段。换言之，既然日本人像此前的清朝一样，在沿生番界争夺木材采伐权的经济战争中选边站队，关于日本与原住民“特殊关系”的提法便消失了。

en: In February 1900, Governor-General Kodama Gentarō lambasted the policies of his predecessors Kabayama, Mizuno, and Hashiguchi. With insurrection ebbing in the plains areas, Kodama declared, “we must shift our military forces to the savage territory. Those who live there are stubborn, and live like wild beasts; if we continue to feast them with liquor and food, staying with a policy of attraction, it will take many months and years for them to reach even a limited degree of evolutionary development.”

And here was the crux of the matter: wet diplomacy would not make indigenes into loyal, governable, imperial subjects in a timely manner. For Kodama, the clock was indeed ticking, as Japan was a relatively poor country playing in the high-stakes international game of competitive colonialism. In late 1900, Japan was undergoing a massive armament expansion to prepare for war against Russia and could not afford to manage a colony in the red.
zh: 1900 年 2 月，总督儿玉源太郎（Kodama Gentarō）痛斥其前任桦山、水野与桥口的政策。随着平原地区的叛乱逐渐平息，儿玉宣称：“我们必须把军事力量转移到蕃地。住在那里的人顽固不化，活得像野兽；如果我们继续以酒食款待他们，固守怀柔政策，那么即便要让他们达到有限程度的进化发展，也要花上许多年月。”
而问题的症结正在于此：湿外交无法及时把原住民变成忠诚、可治理的帝国臣民。对儿玉而言，可用的时间越来越少，因为日本是一个相对贫穷的国家，却在参与竞争性殖民主义这场高风险的国际博弈。1900 年末，日本正在进行大规模军备扩张以备对俄战争，无力承受一个赤字经营的殖民地。

en: The years 1896 through 1900 paved the way for the aggressive measures that followed. During this interval, gift distribution centers became trading posts, with fixed exchange rates. Having established the posts as primary nodes of exchange, the government-general then began to impose selective embargoes against mischief-makers.

By this method, devised from expedience but also based on field reports about wet diplomacy from the 1870s and 1880s, Japanese officials in northern Taiwan’s mountain districts had cultivated an effective network of collaborators, trading partners, informants, and mercenaries to go along with a rudimentary knowledge of local political conditions.
zh: 1896 至 1900 这几年为随后的激进措施铺平了道路。在此期间，礼物分发中心变成了有固定交换比率的贸易站。在把这些站点确立为交换的主要节点之后，总督府继而开始对滋事者实施选择性禁运。
通过这种出于权宜、但也基于 1870 与 1880 年代湿外交实地报告而设计的方法，台湾北部山地的日本官员培育了一张由合作者、贸易伙伴、线人与雇佣兵组成的有效网络，并随之获得了对地方政治状况的初步了解。

en: The effectiveness of wet diplomacy as a stepping-stone to the eradication of indigenous sovereignty is best illustrated by a notorious 1903 incident on the Sediq/Bunun border just south of Wushe. The grislier details and some of the specifics come down to us through memoirs many decades after the events, so there are factual discrepancies in these accounts. The cataclysm had its origins in the salt embargo placed on the Tgdaya tribes after the disappearance of the Fukahori mission in early 1898. On December 16, 1902, the Puli subprefect dispatched a “savage woman [

] named Iwan” to sound out Tgdaya tribes about an upcoming Japanese punitive expedition to the north. Iwan learned that they sought a truce with Japan in order to resume trade in salt. Besides, they were engaged in a cycle of revenge feuding with neighboring Toda and needed arms and ammunition.

Iwan was a common name in the Tgdaya region, so it is hard to say if Iwan Robao (see chapter 2) is the person mentioned in the above report. Nonetheless, Deng Xiangyang, Aui Heppa, and Pixo Walis have all attributed the planning of the “Bukai incident” that followed Iwan’s reconnaissance to Kondō Katsusaburō and his Paalan wife, Iwan Robao.
This interpretation is consistent with other documented facts, but I have yet to find direct documentary evidence of Kondō’s involvement.
zh: 1903年，雾社以南赛德克与布农的交界处发生了一桩臭名昭著的事件，最能说明湿外交如何为铲除原住民主权铺路。更血腥的细节与部分具体情形，是通过事件发生数十年后的回忆录流传给我们的，因此这些记述存在事实出入。这场剧变的根源，在于 1898 年初深堀使团失踪后对德固达雅各社实施的盐禁运。1902 年 12 月 16 日，埔里支厅长派遣一名叫伊万（Iwan）的“蕃婦”（banpu）去试探德固达雅各社对日本即将向北讨伐一事的态度。伊万得知，他们寻求与日本休战，以恢复盐的贸易。此外，他们正与邻近的都达（Toda）人陷入一轮复仇仇杀，需要武器弹药。
伊万在德固达雅地区是个常见名字，因此很难说伊娃莉·罗拔俄（Iwan Robao，见第 2 章）是否就是上述报告中提到的人。尽管如此，邓相扬、阿乌伊·赫帕（Aui Heppa）与比荷·瓦利斯（Pixo Walis）都把伊万侦察之后发生的“布凯（Bukai）事件”的策划，归于近藤胜三郎（Kondō Katsusaburō）及来自芭兰的妻子伊娃莉·罗拔俄。
这一解释与其他有文献记载的事实相符，但我尚未找到近藤参与的直接文献证据。
body.review: 原书此处称深堀使团于1898年初失踪，本章前文则明确记为1897年2月。两处日期均依原书保留。

en: On October 5, 1903, the continued economic blockade drove Tgdaya men into a bloody trap. Short of salt and firearms, men from Paalan consented to a meeting with Gantaban men of the Bunun group south of Puli, at Shimaigahara (Bukai). The meeting’s pretext was Gantaban’s promise to funnel embargoed goods to Paalan behind the government’s back. On the appointed day, the Gantaban trading delegation served the Paalan men large quantities of alcohol to initiate talks. Thereafter, concealed men rushed in, killing 95 of the 100 Paalan men and taking their heads.

The Japanese press reported 104 dead along with a yield of 57 rifles, 130 spears, and 127 daggers. The Bunun warriors brought 27 of the heads to the Puli subprefect, who appears to have expected this outcome (see
The TGG file gives similar casualty figures while noting that Wushe’s once reluctant posture toward the Japanese was much improved.
zh: 1903 年 10 月 5 日，持续的经济封锁把德固达雅男子驱入了一场血腥陷阱。缺盐少枪的芭兰人同意在姊妹原（Shimaigahara，布凯）与埔里以南布农族的干卓万（Gantaban）人会面。会面的借口是干卓万人承诺背着政府把禁运物资输送给芭兰。到了约定的日子，干卓万贸易代表团向芭兰人奉上大量酒以开启谈判。随后，埋伏的人冲了出来，杀死一百名芭兰人中的九十五人并割下他们的首级。
日本报纸报道有一百零四人死亡，伏击者还缴获五十七支步枪、一百三十支长矛与一百二十七把匕首。布农战士把其中二十七颗首级带到埔里支厅长那里，后者似乎早已预料到这一结果（见
总督府的档案给出类似的伤亡数字，并指出雾社一度对日本不情愿的姿态已大为改善。

en: THE CAMPHOR INDUSTRY AND THE GUARDLINE
zh: 樟脑产业与隘勇线

en: The causes of armed conflict along the indigenous-Han border were multiple. Japanese officials reported a surge in revenge killings and ritually sanctioned head taking in the wake of Japanese arms confiscation sweeps that were part of the antibandit campaigns of 1896 through 1902. But most of the killings represented efforts by indigenes to defend hunting grounds, fallow fields, or forests previously subject to fees levied by headmen on camphor harvesters. These camphor-related killings dated from the treaty-port period (1860–1895), reached a fever pitch by 1900, and climaxed in a major battle between the Japanese state and Ri Aguai in late 1902.
zh: 原住民—汉人边界沿线武装冲突的起因是多重的。日本官员报告说，在 1896 至 1902 年剿匪行动中日方收缴武器的扫荡之后，复仇杀人与仪式认可的猎首激增。但大多数杀戮体现了原住民保卫猎场、休耕地或森林的努力——过去靠这些森林生产樟脑的人，要向头人缴费。这些与樟脑相关的杀戮可追溯到条约口岸时期（1860–1895），到 1900 年达到白热化，并在 1902 年末日本国家与日阿拐（Ri Aguai）之间的一场大战中达到顶点。

en: The camphor tree (
, or
, or

in Japanese) “is a rather small-leafed evergreen, attaining... [a] height of from sixty to one hundred feet, with wide-spreading branches and a trunk two to four feet in diameter.” By century’s turn, the western plains had been denuded. Camphor was still abundant, however, in the “debatable land between the Savage territory” and the foothills.

The aggressive collection of the product in the latter half of the nineteenth century incited warfare between highlander and lowlander, creating a frontier that resembled a permeable membrane; commerce flowed through, but armies and lowlanders were kept at bay. During the last decade of Qing rule, government losses from these battles were horrendous, totaling hundreds of casualties per encounter.
zh: 樟树（Cinnamonium camphora，或 Camphora officinarum，日语称 kusunoki）“是一种叶子相当小的常绿树，可长到……六十至一百英尺高，枝条广展，树干直径二至四英尺”。到世纪之交，西部平原已被砍伐殆尽。然而，在蕃地与山麓丘陵之间的“争议地带”，樟树仍然丰富。
十九世纪下半叶对这一产品的激进采集激起了山地人与平地人之间的战争，造就了一条类似可渗透膜的边界：商业流通其间，军队与平地人却被挡在外面。清朝统治的最后十年，政府在这些战斗中的损失惨重，每次遭遇战伤亡总计达数百人。

en: Camphor, traditionally used as an insect repellent and medicine, had been harvested in Taiwan since the seventeenth century, but developments in technology and politics increased the product’s value sharply in the late nineteenth century. In 1858, Englishman Alexander Parkes invented a way to use camphor in the manufacture of celluloid, which meant that “combs, tobacco pouches... and indeed everything which had before been made of ivory, coral or tortoise-shell now came to be made of celluloid.”
Camphor also became a crucial ingredient in the production of smokeless gunpowder during the latter half of the century.

In the same year that Parkes put camphor on the industrial map, the Treaty of Tianjin forced Taiwan’s two major ports to open to international trade as part of the settlement of the so-called Arrow War. With demand for camphor up, increased numbers of foreign traders called on Taiwan’s ports, and an influential comprador class emerged. By 1878, the export economy of camphor, tea, and sugar “absorbed about twenty percent of [Taiwan’s] population.”
The Lin family of Wufeng, who later supplied the Japanese colonial government with its first hired troops to guard the camphor districts, were part of this class.
zh: 樟脑传统上用作驱虫剂与药物，自十七世纪以来就在台湾被采集，但技术与政治的发展在十九世纪末急剧提升了这一产品的价值。1858 年，英国人亚历山大·帕克斯（Alexander Parkes）发明了一种在赛璐珞制造中使用樟脑的方法，这意味着“梳子、烟草袋……乃至此前用象牙、珊瑚或玳瑁制作的一切东西，如今都用赛璐珞来制作了”。
樟脑也在该世纪下半叶成为生产无烟火药的关键原料。
就在帕克斯使樟脑登上工业舞台的同一年，《天津条约》作为所谓亚罗战争解决方案的一部分，迫使台湾的两个主要港口对国际贸易开放。随着樟脑需求上升，越来越多的外国商人光顾台湾港口，一个有影响力的买办阶级随之兴起。到 1878 年，樟脑、茶与糖的出口经济“吸纳了〔台湾〕约百分之二十的人口”。
雾峰林家后来为日本殖民政府提供了第一批守卫樟脑产区的雇佣兵，正是这个阶级的一部分。

en: The old Lin guardline stretched from Taizhong city to Puli.
Iriye Takeshi, an infantryman who surveyed the area in 1896 for the army and wrote extensively for the trade press about Taiwan’s indigenes, reported that these private guards (
) could be bought off and had conspired to allow the murder of Japanese telegraph-wire stringers in February 1896.

By 1898 camphor manufacturers were hiring their own guards in addition to the ones employed by the Lins and subsidized by the Japanese government. One company paid out ¥1,200 per month for its own security.

That same year, the Taiwan Government-General began recruiting guards for its rural installations in the foothills. With the emergence of camphor as a pillar of state revenue collection, the government-general abdicated its role as referee between indigene and Han and jumped onto the playing field as a partisan of the lumber business. The total number of government and privately employed camphor guards totaled over 1,100 in 1898.
zh: 旧林家隘勇线从台中市一直延伸到埔里。
入江武（Iriye Takeshi）是一名步兵，1896 年曾为军方勘察该地区，并为行业报刊大量撰写关于台湾原住民的文章；他报告说，这些私人隘勇（aiyong）可以被收买，并曾串通放任 1896 年 2 月日本电报线架设工被杀。
到 1898 年，樟脑制造商除了雇用林家手下、由日本政府补贴的隘勇外，还开始自雇守卫。一家公司每月为自身安保支出 1200 日元。
同年，台湾总督府开始为其山麓丘陵的乡村设施招募守卫。随着樟脑成为政府收入的支柱，总督府放弃了它在原住民与汉人之间充当裁判的角色，转而直接站到木材经营者一边。1898 年，政府与私人雇用的樟脑守卫总数超过 1100 人。

en: The majority were Taiwanese resident in the border areas, working under Japanese police officers. With these forces, sporadic Japanese-led military offensives were launched against villages accused of attacking government installations, experimental camphor plots, or Taiwanese plainsmen. These episodic “punitive expeditions” (tōbatsu) had mixed results—at times whole villages were burned, at other times companies of Japanese officers with their squads were routed and killed. Many battles were inconclusive.
zh: 其中多数是居住在边界地区的台湾人，在日本警官手下做事。凭借这些力量，日方零星发动由日本人率领的军事进攻，打击被控袭击政府设施、试验樟脑园或台湾平地人的村落。这些间歇性的“讨伐”（tōbatsu）结果不一——有时整个村落被烧毁，有时日本军官连同其小队被击溃、杀死。许多战斗不分胜负。

en: Recorded instances of armed conflict totaled 79 in 1897; they more than trebled to 271 in 1898. In each of the years between 1898 and 1901 (inclusive), over 500 deaths and 100 injuries were dealt out to government forces by indigenes near the guardlines. The great majority of the casualties were Han and

en: A look at the financial stakes for the central government in Japan explains why the Taiwan Government-General was willing to absorb so many losses. In 1896, expenses related to war and civil government in Taiwan cost the Japanese Treasury 11 percent of its annual budget. From 1895 to 1902, subsidies to Taiwan were about 7 percent of the Japanese national budget. By 1898 there were calls in Japan for the sale of the new colony back to China or to a European power.
In this atmosphere of crisis, Governor-General Kodama Gentarō and his civil minister Gotō Shinpei took charge of the colony in February 1898.

Gotō’s short-term solution to the colony’s financial problems was a government monopoly on opium, camphor, and salt. By instituting a government monopoly on camphor in June 1899, the government-general not only received the profits from a lucrative export product but also forced up the world price, since the only major competitor was Japanese camphor. As

illustrates, with the exception of 1903, which showed uncharacteristically low yields for the monopoly, camphor consistently supplied 13 to 30 percent of the Taiwan-generated revenue for the colonial state during the critical 1900 through 1907 period of Japan’s rule.
zh: 审视日本中央政府的财政利害，就能解释台湾总督府为何愿意承受如此多的损失。1896 年，台湾的战争与民政开支耗去日本国库年度预算的百分之十一。1895 至 1902 年，对台湾的补贴约占日本国家预算的百分之七。到 1898 年，日本国内出现呼声，要求把这块新殖民地卖回中国或卖给某个欧洲列强。
在这种危机气氛中，总督儿玉源太郎与其民政长官后藤新平于 1898 年 2 月接掌殖民地。
后藤对殖民地财政问题的短期解决方案，是政府对鸦片、樟脑与盐的专卖。通过在 1899 年 6 月实行樟脑政府专卖，总督府不仅获得了一项利润丰厚的出口产品的收益，还抬高了世界价格，因为唯一的主要竞争者就是日本樟脑。如
所示，除 1903 年专卖收益异常偏低外，在日本统治关键的 1900 至 1907 年期间，樟脑持续提供殖民政府在台湾本地取得的收入的百分之十三至三十。

en: To finance projects in governmentality that would ultimately make the Han-dominated lowlands into a disciplinary society (see introduction), Gotō secured a Japanese government bond issue of ¥35 million in 1898. The proceeds were earmarked for railroads, land surveys, harbors, and other improvements. Between 1899 and 1905, the Taiwan Government-General received ¥31.2 million in installments from this bond issue, which gradually overtook and then replaced Tokyo’s annual subsidies. (For this period, Taiwan’s annual revenues, subsidies included, were a little over ¥10 million.) The home government released this money expecting the government-general to repay it out of the colonial budget.
zh: 为资助那些最终将使汉人主导的低地变成规训社会的治理术工程（见导论），后藤于 1898 年争取到一笔 3500 万日元的日本政府公债发行。所得款项指定用于铁路、土地调查、港口及其他改良。1899 至 1905 年间，台湾总督府从这笔公债中分期获得 3120 万日元，逐步超过并继而取代了东京的年度补贴。（这一时期，台湾的年度收入含补贴在内略超 1000 万日元。）本国政府拨出这笔钱，指望总督府从殖民预算中偿还。

en: To increase the output of camphor and reduce injuries to the labor force, all privately employed guards were brought under the command and employ of the Japanese government in 1902. Then, on January 27, 1903, all affairs pertaining to the indigenous territories were moved from various provincial and subprovincial offices to the jurisdiction of the central police headquarters in Taipei. In March 1903, Kodama and Gotō convened a conference of all high-ranking officials on the island to discuss a plan for ending “the Aborigine Problem.” The committee was chaired by Mochiji Rokusaburō, a councillor in the Ministry of Civil Affairs.
zh: 为增加樟脑产量并减少劳动力的伤亡，1902 年所有私人雇用的守卫都被纳入日本政府的指挥与雇用之下。随后，1903 年 1 月 27 日，所有涉及原住民领土的事务从各地方官署及其下级机关移交给台北中央警察本部的管辖。1903 年 3 月，儿玉与后藤召集全岛所有高级官员开会，讨论一项终结“蕃人问题”的计划。委员会由民政部参事官持地六三郎主持。

en: During his ten years in Taiwan, Mochiji worked in provincial administration, engineering, communications, and education.

In December 1902, he was sent on an inspection tour of the aborigine border. The resulting “Mochiji line” was approved and codified as a working document at the “Provisional Section for the Investigation of Affairs in the Aborigine Territory,” convened in March 1903.
zh: 持地在台湾的十年间，历任地方行政、工程、通信与教育职务。
1902 年 12 月，他被派去巡视蕃人边界。由此形成的“持地线”在 1903 年 3 月召开的“蕃地事务调查临时课”上获批并被编纂为一份工作文件。

en: As a proponent of the governmental modality discussed in the introduction, Mochiji urged calculated restraint after an initial “big bang” of brutal landscaping to create the playing field for modern economic growth. Instead of eradicating the indigenes, which would have been an expensive, drawn out, and ultimately pointless enterprise (from the standpoint of efficiency), Mochiji argued that Japanese offensives be limited to areas that would bring in enough revenue to justify the expenditures of life and treasure.

With these priorities in mind, Mochiji proposed a three-pronged approach to savage border policy: (1) to unify command under one head; (2) to divide the indigenous territory into the north and south—treating the northerners (Atayal, Saisiyat, Truku, and Sediq) as hostiles and the southerners (Bunun and presumably Paiwan) as allies; and (3) to revive the Chinese guardline system to surround the hostiles in the northern district.
Mochiji’s academic credentials made him a true exemplar of “Meiji youth,” a generation for whom social Darwinism formed the backbone of a modern, scientific worldview.
zh: 作为导论所讨论的那种治理术的倡导者，持地主张在最初一番残酷改造景观的“大爆炸”之后实行精打细算的克制，以为现代经济增长创造条件。与其灭绝原住民——那将是一项昂贵、旷日持久且最终毫无意义的事业（从效率的角度看）——持地主张日本的进攻应限于那些能带来足够收入、足以抵偿人员伤亡及财政开支的地区。
带着这些优先考量，持地为生番界政策提出一个三管齐下的方案：（1）把指挥权统一于一人之手；（2）把原住民领土分为南北——视北方人（泰雅、赛夏、德路固与赛德克）为敌对者，视南方人（布农，推测还有排湾）为盟友；（3）恢复华人隘勇线制度，以圈围北区的敌对者。
持地的学历使他成为“明治青年”的真正典范——对这一代人而言，社会达尔文主义构成了现代科学世界观的支柱。

en: According to Mochiji, in cases where inferior races came into contact with superior ones, “history” taught that the inferior race was either eradicated in the struggle for survival or assimilated to the superior race.

His analysis suggested that indigenous defense of local forests was an affront to imperial prestige: “Until we solve this problem with the indigenes, we will not have sufficient cause to boast to the outside world of our nation’s will and ability to expand and be enterprising. The Aborigine territory occupies 56% of the island’s surface, and is a storehouse of mineral, forest, and agricultural wealth. Unfortunately, the savage and cruel indigenes have thrown up a barrier to this storehouse of natural resources.”
zh: 按持地的说法，在劣等种族与优等种族接触的情形中，“历史”教导说，劣等种族要么在生存竞争中被灭绝，要么被优等种族同化。
他的分析暗示，原住民保卫地方森林是对帝国威望的冒犯：“在我们解决与原住民的这个问题之前，我们没有足够的理由向外部世界夸耀我国扩张与进取的意志和能力。蕃地占全岛面积的百分之五十六，是矿产、森林与农业财富的宝库。不幸的是，野蛮而残忍的原住民为这座自然资源宝库竖起了一道屏障。”

en: Echoes of treaty-port rhetoric are audible in Mochiji’s position paper. In the 1860s and 1870s, it was Paiwan treachery that endangered free trade and use of the sea-lanes, thus thwarting “progress.” Now it was the “aborigine problem” on Taiwan’s forested inland sea that frustrated imperial Japan’s drive to become a first-rank nation-state.
zh: 持地的意见书中可听到条约口岸修辞的回响。在 1860 与 1870 年代，扩张派宣称排湾人背信，危及自由贸易及航道通行，从而阻碍“进步”。如今，则是台湾这片森林覆盖的内陆海上的“蕃人问题”，挫败了帝制日本跻身一流民族国家的努力。

en: From 1903 until 1909, the Taiwan Government-General extended guardlines around the perimeter of northern indigenous territories. The extension process involved building trails, stringing wire, and erecting guardhouses in cooperation with hired, allied, or coerced Taiwanese. The case study of the Quchi alliance in chapter 4 indicates that the networks, knowledge base, and control over trade established during the Pacification Office and DAO periods made it possible to close this perimeter before marching it inward. Large-scale coordinated military offensives were the exception during the 1903–09 extension period; more common were skirmishes that came from attacks on advance posts, camphor workers, and police installations. To build the first strongholds, Japanese forces put mortars and other forms of mountain artillery at commanding heights to provide cover for timbering, wire-hanging, and construction crews. All of these men were exposed to sniper fire, boulder cascades, and sabotage from above. The Bureau of Aboriginal Affairs recorded a total of 1,154 such confrontations for the 1903–09 period, for a total of 1,693 killed and 902 wounded on the government side. The great majority of the casualties were Taiwanese (see
). One estimate of the number of indigenous casualties put the figure at 30 percent of the number of Japanese casualties.
zh: 从 1903 到 1909 年，台湾总督府沿北部原住民领土的周边延伸隘勇线。延伸过程包括修筑小径、架设铁丝、搭建哨所，与受雇、结盟或被胁迫的台湾人合作。第 4 章对屈尺联盟的个案研究表明，抚垦署与辨务署时期建立的网络、知识基础与对贸易的控制，使得先合拢沿外缘构筑的防线、再向内推进成为可能。1903–09 年延伸期间，大规模协同军事进攻是例外；更常见的是因袭击前哨、樟脑工人与警察设施而起的小冲突。为建造最初的据点，日军把迫击炮与其他形式的山地火炮布置在制高点，为伐木、架线与施工队提供掩护。所有这些人都暴露于狙击火力、滚石与来自上方的破坏之下。蕃务本署记录了 1903–09 年间共 1154 起此类对抗，政府方面共 1693 人死亡、902 人受伤。伤亡者绝大多数是台湾人（见
）。一项对原住民伤亡人数的估计认为，该数字为日方伤亡人数的百分之三十。

en: The next phase brought overwhelming force to bear on mobile, motivated, and fugitive populations in the deeper mountain recesses of central northern Taiwan. The price tag for this endeavor and its timing support this book’s contention that the attempted integration of former Qing peripheries into the Japanese polity was a continuation of the treaty-port project to accommodate higher volumes and velocities of global commerce by expanding the radius of public power. While Governor-General Sakuma lobbied to fund a military “surge” in Taiwan’s northern and central mountain forests, the government-general also battled to secure funds to expand and deepen Jilong Harbor.
zh: 下一阶段把压倒性武力施加于台湾中北部更深山坳中那些不断转移、决意抵抗、躲避追捕的人群。这项事业的代价及其时机支持本书的论点：把前清边缘地带纳入日本政体的尝试，是条约口岸工程的延续——后者通过扩大公共权力的半径来容纳全球商业更高的流量与流速。当佐久间总督游说为台湾北部与中部山林的军事“增兵”提供资金时，总督府也在力争获取资金以扩建并加深基隆港。

en: In sync with guardline construction to pipe flows of camphor from interior to port, Jilong Harbor had been subject to dredging and incremental improvements since 1898 to push bulk commodities, including camphor, onto the world market. Initially, the government in Tokyo dribbled out only small fractions of TGG funding requests, often reducing or suspending allocations. In 1906, the twenty-second Diet finally released a large sum—over ¥6 million—for a seven-year harbor improvement plan. But increased demand for Taiwanese rice and camphor exceeded the harbor’s capacity to service sufficiently large cargo ships to clear the docks. Therefore, the Diet earmarked another ¥5 million in 1912, to be disbursed over a fourteen-year period.
zh: 与把樟脑从内陆接连运往港口的隘勇线建设同步，基隆港自 1898 年起就不断疏浚与逐步改良，以把包括樟脑在内的大宗商品推向世界市场。起初，东京政府只零星拨给总督府资金请求的一小部分，常常削减或暂停拨款。1906 年，第二十二届国会终于释放了一笔巨款——超过 600 万日元——用于一项七年港口改良计划。但台湾稻米与樟脑需求的增长，超出了该港接纳能及时把码头积货运走的大型货船的能力。因此，国会在 1912 年又指定拨款 500 万日元，分十四年拨付。

en: By 1917, a total of ¥11,720,000 had been allocated, out of ¥15,700,000 million requested over an eighteen-year period, to build Jilong Harbor.

For the duration of colonial rule, Jilong dominated Taiwan’s foreign trade in ship traffic and tonnage. Unlike the budget for Sakuma’s punitive expeditions, however, the Jilong Harbor budgets were paid completely out of the Tokyo treasury.
Nonetheless, their roughly equal cost suggests the urgency and magnitude of the “Aborigine problem” for advocates of an aggressive policy circa 1909.
zh: 到 1917 年，为建造基隆港已共拨款 1172 万日元，而十八年间请求的总额为 1570 万日元。
在整个殖民统治期间，基隆在船舶往来与吨位上主导台湾的对外贸易。然而，与佐久间讨伐的预算不同，基隆港预算完全由东京国库支付。
尽管如此，两者大致相当的成本表明，对 1909 年前后激进政策的倡导者而言，“蕃人问题”何等紧迫、何等重大。
body.review: 原书第103页作 ¥15,700,000 million，million 疑为衍文。结合本段总额及其与佐久间预算的比较，译为1,570万日元。

en: Sakuma’s famous five-year plan (1910–14) was actually his second five-year plan. The first five-year offensive was launched in 1907. Sakuma sought mass surrenders and, apparently, glorious victories crowned with parades and triumphal arches. These failing, Sakuma’s staff submitted a budget to the twenty-fifth Diet with ¥15,399,000 slotted for the construction, staffing, and movement of the guardlines, to be disbursed and spent over a five-year period.
This enormous sum was the lion’s share of the estimated ¥18 million that Japan poured into the camphor wars from 1904 through 1916.
Even the abandoned first five-year plan was ambitious, financially. In 1907 and 1908, a total of ¥3.58 million was allocated for the extension and movement of the guardlines.
zh: 佐久间著名的五年计划（1910–14）其实是他的第二个五年计划。第一个五年攻势于 1907 年发动。佐久间追求大规模投降，显然还追求以游行与凯旋门装点的辉煌胜利。这些落空后，佐久间的幕僚向第二十五届国会提交了一份预算，其中 1539.9 万日元被指定用于隘勇线的建造、配员与推进，分五年拨付与花费。
这笔巨款占了日本 1904 至 1916 年投入樟脑战争的估计 1800 万日元中的大头。
即便被放弃的第一个五年计划，在财务上也雄心勃勃。1907 与 1908 年，共拨款 358 万日元用于隘勇线的延伸与推进。

en: The expense of this seemingly inconclusive war had its critics. At the February 1909 session of the twenty-fifth Diet, the firebrand representative Sasaki Yasugorō grilled Prime Minister Katsura, Communications Minister Gotō Shinpei, and Home Minister Harada Tōsuke for requesting large outlays of blood and treasure to subdue a “dying race.” Sasaki was known as the “King of Mongolia” and as a “continental adventurer” (tairiku rōnin) for his exploits in Central Asia during the Russo-Japanese War.

While Mochiji invoked world history to espouse social Darwinism, Sasaki held up Zheng Chenggong and other imperial powers as models of competence in aborigine administration, compared to the Taiwan Government-General, which Sasaki considered inept.
zh: 这场看似不分胜负的战争的开销有其批评者。在 1909 年 2 月第二十五届国会的会议上，火爆的众议员佐佐木安五郎（Sasaki Yasugorō）质询首相桂太郎、递信大臣后藤新平与内务大臣原田冬介，指责他们为征服一个“垂死的种族”而不惜让国家承受大量人员伤亡和财政开支。佐佐木因日俄战争期间在中亚的所作所为而被称为“蒙古王”与“大陆浪人”（tairiku rōnin）。
持地援引世界历史来拥护社会达尔文主义，佐佐木则举出郑成功与其他帝国列强作为蕃人行政能干高效的典范，以对比他认为无能的台湾总督府。

en: Sasaki accused the cabinet members of refusing to answer questions, criticized them for their inattentiveness to the science of colonial statecraft, and even charged that measures to annihilate the indigenes were unconstitutional. At the heart of Sasaki’s long harangue, which was interrupted by applause, was the charge that the cost of indigenous suppression had no end in sight and would increase ad infinitum until it broke the national budget. He doubted that suppression of the indigenes was an urgent national matter.
zh: 佐佐木指责内阁成员拒绝回答问题，批评他们对殖民治国这门科学漫不经心，甚至指控灭绝原住民的措施违宪。佐佐木那篇被掌声打断的长篇抨击，核心是指控镇压原住民的成本看不到尽头，将无限增加，直到压垮国家预算。他怀疑镇压原住民是否是一件紧迫的国家大事。

en: Despite Sasaki’s sharp questioning and the thirty signatures his inquiry garnered, the budget passed. Fujii Shizue attributes the approval to Sakuma’s connections with Yamagata Aritomo. A hero of the Meiji Restoration, Yamagata was also the father of Japan’s modern army, a prime minister, and a mentor to sitting prime minister Katsura Tarō. In addition, Fujii argues, the Meiji Emperor himself took a personal interest in the undertaking and lent his prestige to Sakuma’s proposal.
zh: 尽管佐佐木尖锐质询，其质询也征集到三十个签名，预算还是通过了。藤井静枝（Fujii Shizue）把这一批准归于佐久间与山县有朋的关系。作为明治维新的英雄，山县还是日本现代陆军之父、一位首相，以及现任首相桂太郎的导师。此外，藤井认为，明治天皇本人对这项事业有个人兴趣，并以自己的威望为佐久间的提案背书。

en: Out of an estimated 1909 aborigine population of 122,000, there were 28,242 Atayals, the principal targets of the guardline movements. These guardlines were manned and advanced by forces that varied between 6,000 and 7,000 inspectors, engineers, laborers, guards, and police officers (mostly Taiwanese guards).
A description of the guardline’s physical aspect explains how these thousands were deployed:
zh: 在估计 1909 年 12.2 万的原住民人口中，有 28242 名泰雅人，他们是隘勇线推进的主要目标。这些隘勇线由 6000 至 7000 名不等的警部、工程师、劳工、隘勇与巡查（多为台湾人隘勇）驻守与推进。
一段对隘勇线物理形态的描述说明了这数千人如何部署：

en: The guard-line has two components. The first is a road opened up in the mountain areas.... The other is the guard station. This is a kind of a dugout, a sentry box with gun holes which is protected from bullets and shells by impenetrable sandbags, earth, stone, etc. Where necessary, electric wire fences have been hung and land mines have been buried. An electric current was passed through the wires, and many uplanders and their domesticated animals have died from electric shock. At this time, field and mountain artillery, as well as mortars were set up... As for the land mines, they were installed by the police inspectors and their assistants; the construction was left to police officers, who were all Japanese, and the assistant patrolmen, who were of Chinese descent, were not allowed to install them for the maintenance of secrecy. It appears that the electric wire fences began to be hung beginning in 1905. The electric switch was controlled by a Guardline Headquarters police inspector; since there were only one of these stations per guardline, even the guards were electrocuted from time to time.
zh: 隘勇线有两个组成部分。其一是在山地开辟的道路……其二是哨所。这是一种掩体，一种带枪眼的岗亭，由防弹的沙袋、泥土、石块等保护，不受枪弹与炮弹侵袭。在必要处架设了通电铁丝网并埋设了地雷。电流通过铁丝，许多山地人及其驯养的动物触电而死。此时，野战炮与山地炮以及迫击炮也布置起来……至于地雷，由警部及其助手安装；施工交给巡查——他们全是日本人——而华裔的巡查补则为保密起见不被允许安装。通电铁丝网似乎从 1905 年开始架设。电开关由隘勇线本部的一名警部控制；由于每条隘勇线只有一个这样的站点，连隘勇也不时触电身亡。

en: By 1912 the lines contained 756 guard stations, 427 branch stations, and 196 superintendent stations, extending to a total length of 226 miles.
The organization of these facilities was quite methodical, at least in its schematic form:
zh: 到 1912 年，隘勇线共有 756 座哨所、427 座分遣所与 196 座监督所，总长达 226 英里。
这些设施的组织相当有条不紊，至少在其示意图形式上如此：

en: The width of the guardline’s path was 1.8 meters, and the foliage for 100 meters on either side of the path was cut down so for the sake of visibility. The Chinese guards protected the guard stations, and were equipped with rifles, which allowed them to be mobile. Two to four guards manned each guard post. A branch superintendent station was placed every four to five guard stations; officers and assistant policemen, as well as guards were stationed here. For every four to five branch stations a superintendent station built; besides the police and guards, inspectors and assistant inspectors were stationed here, as well as the intermittent medical personnel or reserve unit... amazingly, one of these posts was erected every 220 meters, which testifies to the strength of the resistance to Japanese rule.
zh: 隘勇线小径宽 1.8 米，小径两侧各 100 米内的植被被砍光，以便瞭望。华人隘勇守卫哨所，配备步枪，使他们得以机动。每座哨所由二至四名隘勇驻守。每四至五座哨所设一座分遣所；警官、巡查补以及隘勇驻守于此。每四至五座分遣所建一座监督所；除巡查与隘勇外，警部与警部补也驻守于此，还有间歇配置的医务人员或预备队……令人惊讶的是，每 220 米就设立一座这样的哨所，这证明了对日本统治抵抗之强烈。

en: The guardline’s organizational chart mirrored an ideal of centralized administration: priorities were set, and knowledge was concentrated, at the bureaucratic apex, while sacrifice was demanded from those at the bottom. At the pinnacle stood the police headquarters in Taipei, executing policy that was drafted with an eye to the “greater good” of imperial Japan, as defined by the imperatives to balance annual colonial budgets. At the nerve center of the guardline itself were the control stations. Here, Japanese inspectors were attended by physicians and heavily guarded. The inspectors were entrusted with the electrical switches, as well. Below them were Japanese nationals at branch stations and substations who were apprised of mine placement, and then at the bottom rung were the exposed Chinese and

units. They absorbed the preponderance of casualties and, for fear of security breaches, were kept in the dark about operational secrets (the placement of mines or the ignition of the electrical fences), to their own physical peril.
zh: 隘勇线的组织结构图映照出一种中央集权行政的理想：优先事项在官僚顶层设定，知识在顶层集中，而牺牲则被要求于底层。顶端是台北的警察本部，执行政策时着眼于日本帝国所宣称的“整体利益”，其定义来自平衡年度殖民预算的迫切需要。隘勇线本身的中枢是监督所。在这里，日本警部有医生随侍，并受到重重守卫。电开关也托付给警部。在他们之下，是分遣所与支所的日本国人，他们知悉地雷的布置；再往下，最底层是暴露的华人与熟蕃单位。他们承受了大部分伤亡，而且出于对泄密的恐惧，被蒙在鼓里，不知行动机密（地雷的布置或通电铁丝网的启动），使他们自己也随时可能受伤或丧命。

en: Schematic maps from the extension and movement phases of these pacification campaigns represent the scorched-earth installations as circles and triangles arrayed on a “line.” However, written accounts described a “hundred-meter-wide clear-cut” path, while photographs attest to three-dimensional, undulating ecological boot-prints. In a word, the term “guardline” (aiyūsen) soft-pedaled the physical magnitude of the scorched-earth installations. The photographs below document Japanese, Taiwanese, and indigenous guards, tree fellers, and porters who walked this tightrope during the period 1903–15 (see
zh: 这些绥靖战役延伸与推进阶段的示意图，把焦土设施表现为排列在一条“线”上的圆圈与三角。然而，文字记述描述的是一条“百米宽的皆伐”小径，照片则见证了沿起伏山势留下的大面积生态创痕。一言以蔽之，“隘勇线”（aiyūsen）这个词淡化了焦土设施的物理规模。下面的照片记录了 1903–15 年间在这条危险防线上作业的日本、台湾与原住民隘勇、伐木工与挑夫（见

en: As guards, porters, and soldiers, Taiwanese recruits were exposed to enemy fire. In 1911, for example, 151 Taiwanese, compared to only 4 Japanese, were killed advancing the guardline.
Overall, over 2,000 government forces perished (including Japanese), with another 2,200 wounded, in the camphor wars of 1904 to 1915.

Taking a longer view, the death toll attributed to the war against indigenous people—including the spike in resistance from 1897 to 1901 and the dead from the Wushe uprising—amounted to 7,080 Taiwanese and Japanese, with another 4,116 wounded (1895–1935).
Caroline Hui-yu Ts’ai reports that some “55,600 [Taiwanese] men” were commandeered to serve in the subjugation campaigns as corvée labor.
At its peak, expeditionary forces proper numbered 12,000 men (including regular army and navy units).
zh: 作为隘勇、挑夫与士兵，受征募的台湾人暴露于敌方火力之下。例如 1911 年，推进隘勇线时有 151 名台湾人被杀，而日本人仅 4 人。
总体而言，1904 至 1915 年的樟脑战争中，超过 2000 名政府军丧生（含日本人），另有 2200 人受伤。
拉长时段看，归因于对原住民战争的死亡人数——包括 1897 至 1901 年抵抗的激增与雾社起义的死者——达 7080 名台湾人与日本人，另有 4116 人受伤（1895–1935）。
蔡慧玉（Caroline Hui-yu Ts'ai）报告说，约“55600 名〔台湾〕男子”被强征到征服战役中服劳役。
峰值时，远征军本身达 12000 人（含正规陆军与海军单位）。

en: Acknowledging the danger these exposed patrolmen, sentries, porters, and infantrymen faced, day and night, the Taiwan Government-General promulgated criteria to award special cash bonuses for meritorious service on the guardline in July 1905. The rationale stated that this type of duty was no different from fighting a war.

In April 1907, another TGG internal order announced that medals would be awarded to the bravest scouts and soldiers on the guardline; the governor-general himself would bestow top honors; battalion leaders would dole out lesser awards. The medals and prizes gave these punitive expeditions and related activities the trappings of a glorious undertaking.
zh: 承认这些暴露的巡查、哨兵、挑夫与步兵日夜面临的危险，台湾总督府于 1905 年 7 月颁布标准，对隘勇线上的有功服务颁发特别现金奖金。其理据声明，这类勤务与打仗无异。
1907 年 4 月，总督府另一道内部命令宣布，将向隘勇线上最勇敢的侦察兵与士兵颁发奖章；总督本人亲自授予最高荣誉；营级长官分发较低奖项。奖章与奖品给这些讨伐及相关活动披上了光荣事业的外衣。

en: There were three tiers within which the pay levels for the one-time bonuses were set. Awards for inspectors and assistant inspectors ranged from the most meritorious award of ¥60 (grade A), down to the grade D award of ¥30. Policemen started at ¥35 and could earn as little as ¥12. Lastly, assistant policemen earned from ¥20 to ¥8 (descending from A- to D-class awards). In other words, the most meritorious assistant policemen would earn ¥10 less than the least meritorious inspector and ¥15 less than the most meritorious policeman.
zh: 一次性奖金的薪酬水平分三个等级设定。警部与警部补的奖金从最优等的 60 日元（甲等）到丁等的 30 日元。巡查从 35 日元起，最低可至 12 日元。最后，巡查补从 20 日元到 8 日元（从甲等到丁等递减）。换言之，最优等的巡查补比最末等的警部少赚 10 日元，比最优等的巡查少赚 15 日元。

en: A list of sixty-four awards submitted to Governor-General Sakuma by Nantou Prefect Koyanagi Shigemichi in May 1906 included commendations for twenty-eight assistant patrolmen, all with Taiwanese names. The remaining inspectors and policemen had Japanese names, meaning that Japanese guardline combatants outearned their Chinese compatriots handily, while casualties and the risk of death were much higher for Taiwanese participants.
zh: 1906 年 5 月，南投厅长小柳重道（Koyanagi Shigemichi）向佐久间总督提交的一份六十四人获奖名单中，包括对二十八名巡查补的表彰，全是台湾人名字。其余的警部与巡查都是日本名字，这意味着日本隘勇线战斗员的拿到的奖金远高于与他们并肩作战的华人，而台湾人参与者的伤亡与死亡风险却高得多。

en: At the height of the five-year campaign,Ōtsu Rinpei, who directed operations as Sakuma’s police chief, wrote the preface for a collection of

(glorious tales) about the brave men of the guardline. Some of the men lionized in this volume were killed in action; others were severely wounded.Ōtsu introduced these fifty-four sketches by magnifying the importance of the war. He wrote that Taiwan presented three challenges to Japan: bandits, pestilence, and savages. The former two were eradicated with policing and medicine in the early years of Japanese rule, while the last obstacle was still being overcome. These tales describe the actions of men running into nests of headhunters to secure strongholds, fighting gamely against ambushes, or collecting intelligence in the face of grave danger. In total, the collection lauds the actions of twenty-six Taiwanese guards and twenty-eight Japanese policemen. In contrast to the cash bonus system’s racially determined hierarchy of danger and compensation, the glorious tales were presented in chronological order with no preference for rank, age, or nationality.

The roughly equal representation and equalitarian format of Ōtsu’s pamphlet stood in stark contrast to the patently discriminatory nature of day-to-day operations, be it measured in terms of risk or reward.
zh: 在五年战役的高峰期，作为佐久间警察部长指挥行动的大津麟平（Ōtsu Rinpei），为一部关于隘勇线勇士的美谈（bidan，光荣故事）集撰写了序言。这部集子中被颂扬的一些人阵亡了；另一些则身受重伤。大津通过夸大这场战争的重要性来引出这五十四篇速写。他写道，台湾给日本带来三大挑战：匪徒、瘟疫与生番。前两者在日本统治初年以警务与医药铲除，而最后一道障碍仍在克服之中。这些故事描述了人们冲入猎首者巢穴以夺取据点、勇敢抗击伏击、或面对重大危险搜集情报的行动。集子总共颂扬了二十六名台湾人隘勇与二十八名日本巡查的行动。与现金奖金制度按种族决定的危险与补偿等级相反，这些光荣故事按时间顺序呈现，不分等级、年龄或国籍。
大津这本小册子两类人员大致相当的入选人数和不分身份的编排方式，与日常运作公然歧视的性质形成鲜明对比，无论以风险还是报酬衡量。

en: There were four major offensives in Sakuma’s campaign, beginning with the attack on the Gaogan Atayal near Jiaobanshan in 1910. The picture that emerges is not so much that of a master plan coming to fruition as that of a centralized state with vastly superior technology and resources exhausting itself in a border region whose political economies, topographies, and traditions of armed resistance confirmed the wisdom of Mochiji’s formula—some areas of Taiwan would not be worth the investment of blood and treasure to administer. In fact, the original ¥15.4 million budgeted for the campaign was insufficient. Supplementary requests drove the costs up to ¥16.24 million. Although official summary reports buried this figure, a contemporary economic analysis of the government-general’s developmental policies discovered that over half of this burden—about ¥8.3 million—was paid out of the national treasury in Tokyo as supplemental funding.
zh: 佐久间的战役有四次主要进攻，始于 1910 年对角板山附近高干（Gaogan）泰雅人的攻击。浮现的图景与其说是一个总体规划开花结果，不如说是一个拥有压倒性技术与资源的中央集权国家，在一个边境地区耗尽力气——该地区的政治经济、地形与武装抵抗传统印证了持地公式的智慧：台湾有些地区不值得投入血与财富去治理。事实上，为战役最初编列的 1540 万日元预算不够用。追加请求把成本推高到 1624 万日元。尽管官方总结报告掩埋了这个数字，但当时一份对总督府开发政策的经济分析发现，这一负担的一半以上——约 830 万日元——由东京国库作为补充资金支付。

en: Although the five-year budget was drawn up with great precision, planners could not predict the course of the war. Early movements were repulsed, soldiers ran away, and the plan fell behind schedule. The 1914
, which assiduously updated annual entries regarding the war’s progress, reported ominously: “The [first] three campaigns cost about [¥9 million], but only about

children: one-tenth of the program was effected

en: .” In other words, well over half the budget had been spent, and four of the five budget years had passed, but only 10 percent of the plan had been completed.
Time and money ran out that summer. The vaunted plan abruptly ended with Sakuma’s declaration of victory over the Truku peoples in August 1914.

Although southern and eastern Taiwan remained untouched, and the proposed network of roads and fences to secure the perimeter of the indigenous territory remained a dream, Sakuma and his officers erected triumphal arches in various parts of Taiwan and paraded to celebrate.
The Emperor Taishō granted Sakuma an audience on September 19, 1914. The seventy-one-year-old general reported to the throne, “the indigenous suppression undertaking has been concluded.”
zh: 尽管五年预算编列得极为精确，规划者却无法预测战争进程。最初几次推进受阻，部队被击退，士兵逃跑，计划落后于进度。逐年勤勉更新战争进展条目的 1914 年《日本年鉴》刊出的数字已显出不妙：“〔头〕三次战役花费约〔900 万日元〕，但计划只实现了约十分之一。”换言之，预算已花去远超一半，五个预算年度已过去四个，但计划只完成了百分之十。
那年夏天，时间与金钱都耗尽了。这项被吹嘘的计划，随着佐久间 1914 年 8 月宣布战胜德路固人而戛然而止。
尽管台湾南部与东部仍未触动，拟议中用以巩固原住民领土周边的道路与铁丝网网络仍是个梦想，佐久间及其军官却在台湾各地搭建凯旋门、游行庆祝。
大正天皇于 1914 年 9 月 19 日接见佐久间。这位七十一岁的将军向天皇上奏：“原住民镇压事业已告完成。”

en: Japan declared war on Germany on August 23, 1914, a week before the Truku campaign ended. The six-week siege of the German port at Qingdao cost 1,400 Japanese casualties (400 deaths), while the Japanese Navy steamed southward to occupy German holdings in the South Pacific.

The opening of the so-called Great War marked the end of imperial Japan’s attempts to incorporate indigenous Taiwan into the empire. Sakuma’s successor, Governor-General Andō Sadami, closed down organs and installations associated with the five-year plan between July and September 1915.
In 1917, the guard posts themselves were dismantled. Their personnel rotated into police administration as mobile units in more scattered but densely staffed police boxes.
zh: 日本于 1914 年 8 月 23 日对德国宣战，比德路固战役结束早一周。对青岛德国港口的六周围攻使日本付出 1400 人伤亡（400 人死亡）的代价，而日本海军则向南航行，占领德国在南太平洋的属地。
所谓大战的开启，标志着帝制日本把原住民台湾纳入帝国之尝试的终结。佐久间的继任者、总督安东贞美（Andō Sadami）于 1915 年 7 至 9 月间关闭了与五年计划相关的机关与设施。
1917 年，哨所本身也被拆除。其人员转入警察行政，编入地点分散、各自配有较多人手的警察驻在所，担任机动队员。

en: Tōgō Minoru and Satō Shirō, who finished their tome on Taiwanese colonial development in February 1916, wrote hopefully that the resources expended during the five-year campaign would be recovered as more indigenous territory in Taiwan was added to the tax base through incorporation into “normal administration.”

The official digest of Taiwan’s administration for 1915, however, was less optimistic. It issued a skeptical and prophetic warning: “The work of subjugation has thus been completed..., but this may not mean that the savages have been reduced to submission. Some of them

children: may still remain incorrigible at heart

zh: 东乡实（Tōgō Minoru）与佐藤四郎（Satō Shirō）于 1916 年 2 月完成他们关于台湾殖民开发的大部头著作，满怀希望地写道，随着更多台湾原住民领土通过纳入“普通行政”而被加入税基，五年战役中耗费的资源将得到回收。
然而，1915 年台湾行政的官方摘要却不那么乐观。它发出一个怀疑而预言性的警告：“征服工作至此已完成……但这未必意味着生番已被压服。他们中有些人在心里可能仍桀骜不驯。”

en: The subsequent 1916 edition was more pointed. The “work of subjugation,” it reported, “has thus been completed over all the aborigines’ region,
. Strictly speaking, out of the total tribes of 672 with 129,715 inhabitants, 551 tribes representing 116,744 have vowed allegiance and the balance of the 121 tribes with 13,000 are
As testament to the TGG’s lack of appetite for resuming Sakuma’s aggressive policies after World War I, subsequent
repeated the 1916 summary verbatim, as boilerplate, for ten years running through 1927.
zh: 随后的 1916 年版更为直白。它报道，“征服工作”“至此已在全蕃人区域完成，至少目前如此。严格说来，在总计 672 社、129715 名居民中，共有116,744人的551社已宣誓效忠，其余 121 社、13000 人仍有待处置。”
作为总督府在一战后无意重启佐久间激进政策的明证，随后的《日本年鉴》把1916年的这段摘要当作固定文字，逐年照录，直到1927年，接连十年如此。

en: FROM MIDDLE GROUND TO NATIVE AUTHORITY
zh: 从中间地带到土著权威

en: The historical contours of wet diplomacy in Taiwan’s uplands recall the fate of North America’s “middle ground.” Historian Richard White’s study of eighteenth-century frontier diplomacy argues that as long as Algonquians and Ojibwas had the leverage to force British and French agents onto the “middle ground” between state and nonstate spaces, gifts, feasts, and oaths were required to secure indigenes’ provisional allegiance. By the early 1800s, writes White, the United States had neutralized the French and British threats to its sovereignty. Without rival powers to divide its energies, Washington trained its guns on Indians and enforced directives in Algonquian and Ojibwa territory with ultimatums and firearms instead of with banquets and gifts.
zh: 台湾高地湿外交的历史轮廓令人想起北美“中间地带”的命运。历史学家理查德·怀特（Richard White）对十八世纪边疆外交的研究主张，只要阿尔冈昆人（Algonquians）与奥吉布瓦人（Ojibwas）还有筹码迫使英法代理人进入国家与非国家空间之间的“中间地带”，就需要礼物、宴饮与誓言来确保原住民暂时的效忠。怀特写道，到 1800 年代初，美国已消解了法英对其主权的威胁。没有了分散其精力的敌对列强，华盛顿把枪口对准印第安人，以最后通牒与火器而非宴饮与礼物，在阿尔冈昆与奥吉布瓦领土上强制执行指令。

en: Echoing this pattern, wet diplomacy in Taiwan prospered when indigenes occupied the middle position between contending powers: the Japanese state and Han guerilla fighters. The government-general’s fear of a two-front war recommended a policy of negotiation, feasting, and gifting. Fiscal and political pressure to produce income from the camphor monopoly made wet diplomacy less tenable, however. After Gotō Shinpei’s mass annihilation of Han rebels in 1902, Taiwan’s middle ground became harder to maintain. Even so, while the Taiwan Government-General from 1903 onward trained its forces on indigenous peoples, tōmoku and
(headmen and men of influence) remained important intermediaries, resembling the functional group “native authority” as described by Mahmood Mamdani.
zh: 呼应这一模式，台湾的湿外交在原住民占据两个敌对力量之间的位置，这两股力量分别是日本国家和汉人游击队时兴盛。总督府对两线作战的恐惧使谈判、宴饮与赠礼政策成为可取。然而，从樟脑专卖产生收入的财政与政治压力使湿外交不那么站得住脚。1902 年后藤新平大规模歼灭汉人叛乱者之后，台湾的中间地带变得更难维持。即便如此，当台湾总督府从 1903 年起把武力对准原住民时，头目（tōmoku）与地方有影响力者（seiryokusha）仍是重要的居间人，类似于马哈茂德·马姆达尼（Mahmood Mamdani）所描述的功能群体“土著权威”。

en: The members of the native authority, who were recruited and coerced by the Taiwan Government-General in the 1910s and 1920s during the peak of the guardline movements, had achieved local leadership status through prowess in mediation or battle, as leaders of ritual groups, or as members of chiefly lineages. The government-general supported the authority of these men with field trips to Tokyo and Taipei, stipends, badges, medals, and cash awards for meritorious service. This generation of mediators, despite these emoluments, were not utterly dependent upon the state for authority nor were they disciplined imperial subjects. Some remained
zh: 土著权威的成员在 1910 与 1920 年代隘勇线推进的高峰期被台湾总督府招募与胁迫，他们通过调解或战斗的本领、作为仪式群体的领袖、或作为酋长世系的成员，取得了地方领导地位。总督府以到东京与台北的实地考察、津贴、徽章、奖章与有功者的现金奖励来巩固这些人的权威。这一代调解者尽管有这些薪酬，却并非完全依赖国家获得权威，也不是受规训的帝国臣民。有些人在心里仍桀骜不驯。

en: By 1933, there were 186 Atayal, 92 Bunun, and 128 Paiwan officially recognized tōmoku. Of 431 headmen for all of Taiwan, only 22 could understand Japanese; a mere 20 had attended a Japanese educational facility (see chapter 2). Therefore, while members of the native authority might have been amenable to bribes, threats, or expedient alliances, they could not be counted on to prosecute Japan’s interests for love of country, the emperor, or a belief that the new order would bring progress—the hallmarks of discipline (or interiority).

In short, Japan’s version of native authority in Taiwan was a poor instrument for establishing public power in the interior, and it can be viewed as a stopgap measure for a government that could no longer expand its territory through the use of massed force.
zh: 到 1933 年，有 186 名泰雅、92 名布农与 128 名排湾官方认可的头目。在全台湾 431 名头人中，只有 22 人懂日语；仅 20 人曾在日本设立的教育机构就读（见第 2 章）。因此，尽管土著权威的成员可能易于接受贿赂、威胁或权宜联盟，却不能指望他们出于爱国、爱天皇、或相信新秩序会带来进步——这些规训（或内在性）的标志——而去推进日本的利益。
简言之，日本在台湾的土著权威版本是在内陆确立公共权力的拙劣工具，它可以被视为一个再也无法通过集结武力扩张领土的政府的权宜之计。

en: Mona Ludao, who would lead the Wushe Rebellion in 1930, himself played the role of tōmoku. He traveled to Nantou City and Japan as a government-sponsored “tourist” in 1911, along with dozens of other tōmoku and

. At the height of the guardline movements, four troops of headmen were brought to Japan to overawe them with views of Japan’s economic, demographic, and military power. According to TGG police records, Mona himself was a revered warrior and a physically imposing man, recognized by other Tgdaya as a worthy successor to his father, Ludao Bai, a local chief (
zh: 将于 1930 年领导雾社起义的莫那·鲁道本人就扮演头目的角色。1911 年，他作为政府资助的“观光客”，与其他数十名头目与势力者一起前往南投市与日本。在隘勇线推进的高峰期，四批头人被带到日本，以日本经济、人口与军事力量的景象震慑他们。据总督府警察记录，莫那本人是一位受人尊崇的战士、体格魁梧之人，被其他德固达雅人认可为其父鲁道·拜（Ludao Bai）——一位土目（domoku，地方酋长）——的合格继承者。

en: Ludao Bai’s adoption of Japanese son-in-law Kondō Gisaburō, in fact, had one foot in the world of wet diplomacy and another in the scorched-earth policy. To consecrate the marriage of Kondō and Ludao Bai’s daughter Chiwas and activate the new Japan-Tgdaya alliance, the Taiwan Government-General contributed six oxen for slaughter and twenty oil cans of sake, most of it distributed at a wedding feast at Kasumigaseki (near Wushe) in 1909. Ludao Bai’s son Mona Ludao mediated between Sediq men and their new Japanese in-laws during the drunken and tense proceedings. The debauch carried on for about a week. Afterward, about 650 of Ludao Bai’s followers, thanks to this wedding feast and promises (unfulfilled) of enemy heads, supported guardline extensions at the expense of Truku and Toda settlements just north of Wushe (see chapter 2).
zh: 事实上，鲁道·拜招赘日本女婿近藤仪三郎（Kondō Gisaburō），既延续了湿外交，也被用来推行焦土政策。为庆贺近藤与鲁道·拜女儿奇瓦斯（Chiwas）的婚姻、激活新的日本—德固达雅联盟，台湾总督府提供了六头供屠宰的牛与二十油罐清酒，大部分在 1909 年霞关（Kasumigaseki，雾社附近）的一场婚宴上分发。鲁道·拜之子莫那·鲁道在酒醉而紧张的仪式中，在赛德克男子与他们的新日本姻亲之间调解。这场狂饮持续了约一周。之后，鲁道·拜约 650 名追随者，得益于这场婚宴与（未兑现的）敌人首级许诺，支持以雾社正北的德路固与都达聚落为代价的隘勇线延伸（见第 2 章）。

en: A decade later, the government-general called upon Mona Ludao. Much has been written about the Salamao incident of 1920. Official sources consider Mona a conspirator against Japan during this affair, whose bad aims were thwarted by leaks. Oral histories and documentary evidence, on the other hand, suggest that Mona helped lead, or at least mobilize, about 560 Tgdaya troops to punish Salamao rebels. The incident began with an influenza epidemic attributed to the presence of outsiders. The most infamous in a series of Salamao raids and ambushes was an attack on a police station that took nineteen Japanese lives. As a condition of their earlier surrenders, and to avoid suspicion of conspiracy, warriors from Malepa, Xalut, and several Tgdaya villages signed on to fight with Japan. Fujisaki Seinosuke judged Japan’s crushing victory a turning point, noting that the wrath of imperial forces frightened indigenes throughout northern Taiwan into submission.
zh: 十年后，总督府召唤莫那·鲁道。关于 1920 年的萨拉茅（Salamao）事件，已有大量著述。官方史料认为莫那在此事中是反日的阴谋者，其不良企图因泄密而被挫败。另一方面，口述历史与文献证据则暗示，莫那帮助率领、或至少动员了约 560 名德固达雅战士去惩罚萨拉茅叛乱者。事件始于一场被归因于外人到来的流感疫情。萨拉茅一系列袭击与伏击中最臭名昭著的，是一次夺去十九条日本人生命的警察驻在所袭击。作为他们早先投降的条件，并为避免阴谋嫌疑，来自马赫坡（Malepa）、白狗（Xalut）与几个德固达雅村落的战士同意与日军一道作战。藤崎清之助（Fujisaki Seinosuke）判定日本的压倒性胜利是一个转折点，指出帝国军队的怒火吓得台湾北部各地原住民归顺。

en: Reminiscent of the Stone Gate Battle of 1874 and the Gantaban slaughter of 1903 (see

), Salamao heads were displayed publicly to heighten the demonstration effect. Twenty-seven heads were photographed in front of the Wushe police station as trophies of the punitive expedition. Five heads were brought back to Malepa, where they were feted at a large head-taking festival—a long-banned practice that the police allowed on this one occasion, since the killings were government sanctioned.
zh: 令人想起 1874 年的石门战役与 1903 年的干卓万屠杀（见
），萨拉茅人的首级被公开展示以强化示范效应。二十七颗首级在雾社警察驻在所前被拍照，作为讨伐的战利品。五颗首级被带回马赫坡，在那里在一场大型猎首祭中受到祭祀——这是一项长期被禁的习俗，警察在这一次破例允许，因为杀戮是政府批准的。

en: Mona Ludao’s involvement in the 1920 maneuvers is sporadically documented; the contested nature of the records reflects his structural position as a member of native authority, which inclined him toward double-dealing. His clan expected material benefits for his family and followers by taking Japanese in-laws such as Gisaburō or contributing fighting men and laborers to Japanese expeditions. At the same time, chiefly cooperation was forced, on pain of the resumption of bombardment from mountain guns or of trade embargoes, leaving men like Mona with little choice. On the other hand, alliances with Japan, as the above campaigns showed, provided young Atayal, Sediq, Bunun, and Truku men opportunities to take heads and exhibit bravery in battle—rare occasions, since head taking had technically been outlawed.
zh: 莫那·鲁道对 1920 年行动的参与只有零星记载；记载彼此冲突，反映了他身为土著权威体系一员所处的位置，这使他倾向于两面行事。他的氏族期望通过接纳像仪三郎这样的日本姻亲、或为日本远征贡献战士与劳工，为他的家族与追随者带来物质利益。同时，酋长的合作是被迫的，否则将面临山炮轰炸重启或贸易禁运的痛苦，使莫那这样的人几乎没有选择。另一方面，正如上述战役所示，与日本结盟给年轻的泰雅、赛德克、布农与德路固男子提供了猎首与在战斗中表现勇敢的机会——这是难得的场合，因为猎首在名义上已被禁止。

en: But to favor Mona’s men, thereby propping up his stature as a tōmoku, the Taiwan Government-General perforce eroded the prestige of Mona’s Truku and Toda counterparts or the Salamao chiefs, just as the government-general had taken sides against Paalan (Tgdaya) in 1903, when they sanctioned the Gantaban head-taking binge. In other words, the favoritism entailed by wet diplomacy was anathema to the rationalization of state machinery, while it was the very antithesis of isshi dōjin (impartiality).
zh: 但为了偏袒莫那的人、从而支撑他作为头目的地位，台湾总督府不得不侵蚀莫那的德路固与都达同侪或萨拉茅酋长的威望，正如总督府 1903 年批准干卓万猎首狂潮时选边反对芭兰（德固达雅）一样。换言之，湿外交离不开对特定对象的偏袒，这与国家机器的理性化格格不入，也正是“一视同仁”（isshi dōjin，公正）的对立面。

en: Mona himself, according to one memoir, was known to burst into anger at the mention of his role in Salamao. Official records describe him as a reluctant imperial soldier—the government-general marked him as a malcontent. Kondō himself complained that his Wushe in-laws had donated twenty thousand man-hours of labor to building the guardline in early 1909, while their fields lay unattended.

Kondō argued that long-term resentment at the government’s ingratitude, which could have been allayed with a few kegs of sake and an official thank-you or a few more guns and bullets for Mona and his allies, ultimately led many locals to sympathize with and participate in the Wushe Rebellion of 1930.
zh: 据一部回忆录，莫那本人一提他在萨拉茅的角色就会勃然大怒。官方记录把他描述为一个不情愿的帝国士兵——总督府把他标记为不满分子。近藤本人抱怨说，他的雾社姻亲在 1909 年初为建造隘勇线贡献了两万工时的劳动，而他们的田地却无人照料。
近藤认为，对政府忘恩负义的长期怨恨——本可用几桶清酒与一声官方感谢、或给莫那及其盟友更多枪支弹药来平息——最终使许多当地人同情并参与 1930 年的雾社起义。

en: Therefore, Sugiura’s rebuff of Mona’s offer of mediation after the Yoshimura beating incident on October 8, 1930, should be seen as the last straw, one that added humiliation to long-standing torment. Of course, the relationship was also unsatisfactory from the TGG side. Accordingly, Japanese officials took steps to break their reliance on Mona’s generation of headmen in the 1930s and to replace them with more dependent and reliable intermediaries, whose loyalty would not be purchased with canisters of alcohol, head-hunting licenses, or the promise of preferential treatment at government gun depots.
zh: 因此，1930年10月8日，杉浦在吉村殴打事件后拒绝莫那提出的调解，应被视为压垮骆驼的最后一根稻草，它在长期折磨之上又添了羞辱。当然，从总督府一侧看，这段关系同样令人不满。因此，日本官员在 1930 年代采取措施，打破对莫那那一代头人的依赖，代之以更依附、更可靠的居间人，其忠诚不再用罐装酒、猎首许可证、或政府枪械库优先待遇的许诺来购买。
body.review: 原书在“吉村殴打事件”之后写1930年10月8日。本章首段记斗殴发生于10月7日，杉浦拒绝调解在次日，译文按该事件顺序表述。

en: Kodama and Gotō are the “heroes” of Japanese colonization of Taiwan; they are usually given credit for ending rebellion, making the colony profitable, and reducing the military’s role on the island. Comparisons to Paul Doumer’s regime in French Indochina come to mind when reading of their efficiency and ruthlessness; see Edward I. Chen, “Goto Shimpei, Japan’s Colonial Administrator in Taiwan: A Critical Reexamination,”
zh: 儿玉（Kodama）与后藤（Gotō）是日本殖民台湾的“英雄”；人们通常把结束叛乱、使殖民地有利可图、以及削减军方在岛上角色的功劳归于他们。读到他们的效率与冷酷时，令人联想到保罗·杜梅（Paul Doumer）在法属印度支那的政权；见 [Edward I. Chen, “Goto Shimpei, Japan's Colonial Administrator in Taiwan: A Critical Reexamination,” American Asian Review 13, no. 1 (1995): 29–59]。
